                                           EXPLANATORY NOTE


     The proposed General Appropriations Bill (GAB) for Fiscal Year (FY) 2027 translates the National Expenditure
Program (NEP) into the annual spending authority of the National Government. It is anchored on the theme:

                             "People-Centered Growth for an Inclusive and Resilient Future"

     Consistent with this theme, the proposed appropriations direct public resources toward expanding access to quality
education and healthcare, strengthening social protection, creating quality employment and sustainable livelihoods,
improving food and energy security, accelerating development of strategic and climate-resilient infrastructure, and
reinforcing responsive, transparent and accountable public institutions.

     The measure carries forward the Philippine Development Plan 2023-2028 and Ambisyon Natin 2040 through
investments in human capital, social protection, food and energy security, strategic infrastructure, digital transformation,
climate resilience, peace and security, and capable institutions.

     The FY 2027 proposal was prepared amid slower economic growth, inflationary pressure, geopolitical conflict,
volatile fuel prices, climate-related risks, and constrained fiscal space. These conditions require a budget that protects
essential government services, sustains productive investment, responds to immediate vulnerabilities, and preserves the
country's capacity to finance development over the medium term.


                            Constitutional Mandate and the Power of the Purse

     The 1987 Constitution vests in Congress the power of the purse. Through appropriations legislation, Congress
determines the purposes for which public funds may be spent, the amounts that may be made available, and the conditions
governing their use. This authority is inseparable from legislative oversight and ensures that public money is applied
only to lawful, necessary, efficient, and accountable ends.


                                                              i
     Article VI, Section 24 provides: "All appropriation, revenue or tariff bills, bills authorizing increase of the public
debt, bills of local application, and private bills, shall originate exclusively in the House of Representatives, but the
Senate may propose or concur with amendments."

    Article VI, Section 29(1) further declares: "No money shall be paid out of the Treasury except in pursuance of an
appropriation made by law."

     Article VII, Section 22 states: "The President shall submit to the Congress within thirty days from the opening of
every regular session, as the basis of the general appropriations bill, a budget of expenditures and sources of financing,
including receipts from existing and proposed revenue measures."


                              Constitutional Timeline for the FY 2027 Budget

     On July 27, 2026, President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. delivered his fifth State of the Nation Address, formally
opening the Second Regular Session of the Twentieth Congress and setting the Administration's policy direction for FY
2027. On August 11, 2026, the President submitted the proposed FY 2027 National Budget to Congress, together with
the President's Budget Message, the National Expenditure Program, and the Budget of Expenditures and Sources of
Financing, in compliance with Article VII, Section 22 of the Constitution. The submission commenced the House review
through the Committee on Appropriations, which examines agency requirements, performance, implementation
capacity, policy coherence, and changes from the FY 2026 General Appropriations Act, and recommends the allocations
and safeguards needed to address national and local priorities.


                                    Fiscal Context, Strategy, and Directions

      The FY 2027 budget seeks to support economic recovery and transformation while advancing fiscal consolidation.
Under the macroeconomic assumptions adopted for the budget, real gross domestic product is projected to grow by 5.0
to 6.0 percent in 2027, following an adjusted growth outlook of 3.5 to 4.5 percent for 2026.

      The macroeconomic assumptions for FY 2027 include an inflation forecast of 4.0 to 5.0 percent, a foreign exchange
rate of ₱60.00 to ₱62.00 per US dollar, and a Dubai crude oil price of US$70.00 to US$90.00 per barrel. Goods exports
are projected to grow by 4.0 percent, while goods imports are projected to increase by 5.0 percent. Financing-related
assumptions place the 364-day Treasury Bill Rate at 5.0 to 6.0 percent, and the six-month Secured Overnight Financing
Rate at 3.0 to 4.0 percent. Collectively, these parameters provide general planning references for estimating revenues,
financing requirements, operating costs, procurement requirements, and the resource needs of government programs and
projects.

      Within this fiscal and economic context, the budget strategy calls for disciplined prioritization: protecting high
impact and constitutionally mandated services; prioritizing strategic and implementation-ready infrastructure;
strengthening food, energy, climate, and disaster resilience; modernizing government systems; and subjecting lower-
priority, duplicative, poorly targeted, or weakly performing expenditures to closer review, redesign, or appropriate
conditions.




                                                            ii
     National Government revenues are projected at ₱5.21 trillion in 2027, equivalent to 15.7 percent of GDP. Tax
revenues of ₱4.85 trillion will supply the bulk of collections, including ₱3.74 trillion from the Bureau of Internal Revenue
and ₱1.07 trillion from the Bureau of Customs. Non-tax revenues are projected at ₱252.90 billion, while privatization
proceeds are estimated at ₱101.50 billion.

     Disbursements are programmed at ₱6.90 trillion, equivalent to 20.8 percent of GDP. This results to a projected
deficit of ₱1.69 trillion (or 5.1 percent of GDP), compared to ₱1.66 trillion (or 5.4 percent of GDP) in FY 2026.

        To finance the deficit and to refinance maturing obligations, the National Government projects gross borrowings
of ₱3.30 trillion in FY 2027. Of this amount, ₱2.39 trillion is expected to be raised from domestic sources and ₱914.98
billion from external sources. This composition is broadly consistent with the 72.0 percent domestic and 28.0 percent
external financing mix presented in the fiscal program. The predominantly domestic financing mix moderates direct
foreign exchange exposure, while external programing and project loans maintain access to development financing.


       The projected deficit is equivalent to 5.1 percent of GDP in FY 2027, compared to 5.4 percent of GDP in FY
2026. Together with projected interest payments and other mandatory expenditures, these fiscal parameters provide
context for the allocation of resources under the proposed budget.


                                         The Proposed Expenditure Program

     The FY 2027 Total Expenditure Program (TEP) amounts to ₱7.20 trillion, equivalent to 21.7 percent of GDP and
higher by ₱407.02 billion (or 5.99 percent) than the FY 2026 program of ₱6.79 trillion. It consists of ₱4.49 trillion in
programmed new general appropriations and ₱2.71 trillion in automatic appropriations.

       New general appropriations requiring annual legislative authorization total ₱4.61 trillion. Of this amount, ₱4.49
trillion is programmed and ₱111.98 billion is unprogrammed. The programmed amount provides ₱3.86 trillion for
departments and agencies and provides ₱635.90 billion for Special Purpose Funds (SPFs).

      Automatic appropriations rise by 13.21 percent to ₱2.71 trillion and constitute 37.58 percent of the TEP. Major
items include the ₱1.32 trillion National Tax Allotment, ₱1.11 trillion in debt-service interest payments, ₱104.19 billion
for the BARMM Annual Block Grant, and ₱89.03 billion for Retirement and Life Insurance Premiums.

                                        Dimensions of the Proposed Budget
                                                     Budget by Sector

     Social Services accounts for the largest share at 34.11 percent of the FY 2027 Total Expenditure Program (TEP)
and 7.39 percent of GDP, corresponding to an allocation of ₱2.46 trillion. Economic Services represents 25.45 percent
of the TEP and 5.51 percent of GDP, with an allocation of ₱1.83 trillion. Together, Social Services and Economic
Services comprise 59.56 percent of the TEP and 12.90 percent of GDP.

     The remaining balance of the TEP is distributed among General Public Services, Defense, and Debt Burden.
General Public Services accounts for 18.28 percent of the TEP and 3.96 percent of GDP, corresponding to ₱1.32 trillion.
Defense represents 6.28 percent of the TEP and 1.36 percent of GDP, with an allocation of ₱452.38 billion. Debt Burden
accounts for 15.87 percent of the TEP and 3.44 percent of GDP, amounting to ₱1.14 trillion.

     Within the Economic Services allocation, infrastructure priorities include projects considered in terms of
implementation readiness, geographic responsiveness, climate resilience, and linkages with education, health, food
security, local service delivery, and poverty reduction.

                                                Budget by Expense Class

     Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses (MOOE) remains the largest expense class at ₱2.94 trillion, equivalent
to 40.89 percent of the TEP. The amount is 1.22 percent lower than the FY 2026 level. MOOE covers agency operations,
supplies, utilities, transfers, subsidies, and other service-delivery requirements, including major transfers to local
government units.

      Compared to FY 2026, Personnel Services increase by 7.50 percent to ₱1.98 trillion and covers salaries, benefits,
newly created or filled positions, and other personnel requirements in education, health, public safety, defense, and the
rest of the National Government. Financial Expenses amounts to ₱1.11 trillion and consists principally of interest
payments. Capital Outlays and Net Lending total ₱1.16 trillion, representing an increase of 13.81 percent and include
expenditures for transport, roads, flood management, schools, hospitals, irrigation, equipment, and other public assets.




                                                                 iv
                                            Budget by Recipient Entity

      The recipient classification presents the institutional distribution of the FY 2027 Total Expenditure Program (TEP).
National Government Agencies receive ₱4.33 trillion, or 60.17 percent of the TEP. Local Government Units receive
₱1.53 trillion, or 21.29 percent of the TEP. Government-owned and -controlled corporations (GOCCs) and Net Lending
account for ₱220.50 billion, or 3.06 percent of the TEP. Creditors receive ₱1.11 trillion, or 15.48 percent of the TEP, for
interest payments.

      Compared to the FY 2026 program, allocations to National Government Agencies increase by 4.47 percent, while
transfers to local government units increase by 10.07 percent. GOCCs and Net Lending decline by 27.33 percent, while
interest payments increase by 17.29 percent.


                                     Key Budget Priorities and Directions

      The President’s Budget Message organizes the expenditure program around investments in people, productive
capacity, resilience, and governance. It places the government-wide FY 2027 education budget at ₱1.326 trillion,
equivalent to 3.99% of GDP. Within this broader aggregate, the recipient-level comparison identifies ₱975.96 billion for
the Department of Education and ₱176.50 billion for Higher Education, comprised of State Universities and Colleges
and the Commission on Higher Education. These aforementioned allocations total ₱1,152.46 billion, while the remaining
₱161.54 billion reflects appropriations for the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority and other
education-related institutions, programs and expenditures across the National Government. Major interventions include
basic education facilities, school feeding, learning recovery, textbooks and instructional materials, teacher support,
digital equipment, tertiary education assistance, and technical-vocational education and training.

     Health and social protection continue to address household vulnerability. The combined Health allocation is at
₱353.76 billion, which includes allocations for the Department of Health, the Philippine Health Insurance Corporation,
and specialty hospitals. The Department of Social Welfare and Development receives ₱241.56 billion for programs such
as the Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program, assistance to individuals and families in difficult circumstances, social
pension, nutrition, livelihood, and the new Panahon ng Pagkilos community-resilience initiative.

     Under the sectoral classification, the Agriculture and Agrarian Reform subsector is allocated ₱276.57 billion for
FY 2027. The allocation covers programs and interventions relating to crop, livestock and fisheries production, irrigation,
farm-to-market connectivity, buffer stocking, crop insurance, agrarian reform, and other food-security requirements.
Included under the Department of Agriculture is the ₱20.00 billion for the Animal Competitiveness Enhancement Fund
for animal health, production, and value-chain development.

     Infrastructure remains a principal growth driver. DPWH receives ₱643.95 billion. The grouped Transportation
allocation totals ₱302.19 billion, consisting of the Department of Transportation, the Light Rail Transit Authority, and
the Philippine National Railways. These allocations support road preservation and development, bridges, flood
management, rail, maritime, aviation, and land transport systems. The National Disaster Risk Reduction and
Management Fund is allocated ₱45.70 billion, while ₱53.10 billion is provided for government digitalization and related
systems.

                                                          Conclusion

        The General Appropriations Bill (GAB), upon enactment as the General Appropriations Act (GAA), embodies
the constitutional principle that no public money shall be disbursed without congressional authorization, ensuring that
every peso in the FY 2027 budget serves the Filipino people. It fulfills Congress’ mandate to exercise fiscal oversight
with prudence, authorize expenditures consistent with national priorities, and uphold transparency, accountability and
equity in resource allocation.

        This General Appropriations Bill for FY 2027 seeks to authorize the expenditure of approximately ₱4.606 trillion
in total new general appropriations to fund government operations. Of this amount, ₱4,494.09 billion constitutes
programmed new general appropriations included in the Total Expenditure Program (TEP), comprised of ₱3,858.19
billion for departments and agencies and ₱635.90 billion for Special Purpose Funds. The remaining ₱111.98 billion
consists of unprogrammed appropriations outside the programmed expenditure component and may be released only
upon the availability of specified funding sources and upon compliance with the statutory conditions in the General
Appropriations Act. These aforementioned appropriations will provide the annual authority needed to sustain
government operations and implement programs, activities, and projects approved by Congress.

       Automatic appropriations totaling ₱2.706.10 billion are authorized under standing laws and, together with the
₱4,494.09 billion in programmed new general appropriations, comprise the ₱7,200.19 billion Total Expenditure Program
(TEP).

        The timely enactment of the General Appropriations Bill is particularly important amid global geopolitical
tensions, volatility in fuel prices and supply chains, persistent inflationary pressures, and broader economic uncertainty
affecting production costs, household purchasing power, investor confidence and investment decisions. While the budget
cannot eliminate these external risks, dependable spending authority will enable the Government to sustain essential
services, protect vulnerable households and productive sectors, support public and private investment, and reinforce
confidence in its capacity to respond. These conditions give added importance to unified and timely congressional action.




                                                                 vi
       In view of the foregoing fiscal context, constitutional mandates and national imperatives, I earnestly appeal to
every distinguished Member of this august body to join the Committee on Appropriations in fulfilling our collective
responsibility to shape a budget that reflects our nation’s priorities and sustains our people’s aspirations. Here, we echo
the President’s Budget Message: “Let history say that this was the moment when we chose to invest not only in roads
and bridges, schools and hospitals, or programs and projects – but in the limitless potential of the Filipinos.”

        Through our collective efforts, we can ensure that the budget for FY 2027 is passed in a timely, constitutional
and responsible manner – enabling government programs to proceed without disruption and delivering the greatest
benefit to the Filipino people whom we are sworn to serve.

51   Special Provisions Applicable to the Congress of the Philippines                                                                                                     51
52        1. Augmentation of Any Item in the Appropriations of the Congress of the Philippines. Pursuant to Section 25(5) of Article VI of the                            52
53   Constitution, the Senate President, with respect to the Senate and the Speaker, with respect to the House of Representatives, are hereby authorized to augment any   53
54   item in the general appropriations law for their respective offices from any savings in other items of their respective appropriations.                              54
55        2. Organizational Structure of the Senate, the House of Representatives, the Senate and House of Representatives Electoral Tribunals                            55
56   and the Commission on Appointments. Notwithstanding any provision of law to the contrary and within the limits of the appropriations authorized in this              56
57   Act, the Senate President, with respect to the Senate and the Commission on Appointments, the Speaker, with respect to the House of Representatives, and the         57
58   Chairpersons of the Senate and House of Representatives Electoral Tribunals are authorized to:                                                                       58
       14 GENERAL APPROPRIATIONS BILL, FY 2027



 1         (a) formulate and implement the organizational structures of their respective offices;                                                                                1
 2         (b) fix and determine the salaries, allowances and other benefits of their Members, employees and consultants, subject to Section 10, Article VI of the               2
 3             Constitution, and whenever public interest so requires, make adjustments and reorganization of positions in the regular personnel with the corresponding          3
 4             transfer of items of appropriations; and                                                                                                                          4
 5         (c) create new positions in their respective offices:                                                                                                                 5
 6   Provided, That officers and employees whose positions are affected by such adjustments or reorganization shall be granted retirement gratuities and separation              6
 7   pay in accordance with existing laws, which shall be payable from any unexpended balance of, or savings in the appropriations of their respective offices: Provided,        7
 8   further, That the foregoing changes, reorganization and modifications shall be submitted to the DBM for proper documentation.                                               8
 9         3. Release of Appropriations. All appropriations authorized for the Senate, the House of Representatives, the Commission on Appointments, the Senate                  9
10   and House of Representatives Electoral Tribunals shall be automatically and regularly released.                                                                            10
11          4. Modification of Allocation for Operational Expenses. Subject to the approval of the Senate President or the Speaker of the House of                              11
12   Representatives, as the case may be, a Member of Congress may modify his allocation for operational expenses to any other expense category: Provided , That the            12
13   total of said allocation is not exceeded.                                                                                                                                  13
14         5. Revolving Fund for the Reproduction of Legislative Records and Sale of Publications and Products. The revolving fund constituted from                             14
15   the income derived from business-type activities of the Senate and the House of Representatives including sale of publications and other institutional products shall      15
16   be used to cover the expenses incurred for the said activities in accordance with accounting and auditing rules and regulations.                                           16
17         6. Availability of Appropriations and Cash Allocations. Unexpended quarterly and year-end balances of approved appropriations and cash allocations                   17
18   for the Senate, the House of Representatives, the Senate and the House of Representatives Electoral Tribunals and the Commission on Appointments shall remain              18
19   valid appropriations and shall continue to be available for expenditure until fully spent and shall remain under their control and accountability, subject to accounting   19
20   and auditing rules and regulations.                                                                                                                                        20
21         7. Constitutional Guarantee. In the implementation of the foregoing provisions, the constitutional guarantee of the independence of Congress as a co-equal           21
22   branch of government must be maintained.                                                                                                                                   22

42         1. Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Program. The total amount of Fifteen Billion Nine Hundred Fifty Three Million One Hundred Seven Thousand Pesos                                                         42
43   (P15,953,107,000) shall be used in support of the programs and projects of the DAR and other implementing agencies of the Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Program                                               43
44   (CARP), which are duly approved by the Presidential Agrarian Reform Council (PARC) in accordance with E.O. No. 229, s. 1987 and R.A. No. 6657, as amended, and                                                44
45   endorsed by the PARC Executive Committee to the DBM, with their corresponding amounts:                                                                                                                        45
46         (a) Five Billion Three Hundred Ten Million One Hundred Seventy Six Thousand Pesos (P5,310,176,000) for Land Tenure Security and for Agrarian Justice Delivery, of                                       46
47             which One Hundred Million Pesos (P100,000,000) for Landowners' Compensation shall be released to the Land Bank of the Philippines (LBP), through the Bureau of                                      47
48             the Treasury (BTr).                                                                                                                                                                                 48
49                                                                                                                                                                                                                 49
50              This amount shall be supplemented by specific appropriations in this Act lodged under the budgets of the following CARP implementing agencies:                                                     50

 8        2. Agrarian Reform Fund. In addition to the amounts appropriated herein, the amount chargeable against the SAGF reflected in the BESF Table B.15 under FY               8
 9   2027 Proposed Expenditures shall be used for the just compensation payments to landowners, including execution of judgments therefor, and allocation for support             9
10   services, agrarian justice delivery, and operational requirements of the DAR and other CARP implementing agencies consistent with Section 21 of R.A. No. 9700, amending     10
11   R.A. No. 6657: Provided , That such programs and projects shall be approved by the PARC in accordance with E.O. No. 229 and R.A. No. 6657, as amended, and endorsed         11
12   by the PARC Executive Committee to the DBM for fund release.                                                                                                                12
13         Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of a budget request and other relevant budgetary requirements, and in accordance with judicious fiscal            13
14   programming by the National Government, as well as applicable laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                 14
15        3. Agri-Agra Special Fund. In addition to the amounts appropriated herein, the amount chargeable against the SAGF reflected in the BESF Table B.15 under FY            15
16   2027 Proposed Expenditures shall be used for titling and parcelization of landholdings covered with collective Certificate of Land Ownership Awards (CLOA) consistent       16
17   with Section 11 of R.A. No. 11901.                                                                                                                                          17
18         Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of a budget request and other relevant budgetary requirements, and in accordance with judicious fiscal            18
19   programming by the National Government, as well as applicable laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                 19
20         4. Land Distribution Security Program. The DAR, in consultation with the DEPDev, shall initiate the review and evaluation of DAR land distribution                    20
21   targets as mandated under the Philippine Development Plan and shall ensure land distribution and farmers installation in provinces where private land distribution          21
22   records the lowest achievement and largest backlogs. A report on the result of the review and evaluation shall be submitted to Congress and posted in the DAR's             22
23   website.                                                                                                                                                                    23
24         5. Exclusion of Lands Owned and Occupied by Public Schools from the Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Program. Consistent with R.A.                                       24
25   No. 6657, as amended, lands actually, directly and exclusively used and found to be necessary for school sites and campuses including experimental farm stations operated   25
26   by public schools for educational purposes shall be exempt from acquisition and distribution under the CARP.                                                                26
27        6. Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation. The DAR, in coordination with other relevant agencies, shall provide as much as possible, support to all                  27
28   Agrarian Reform Communities (ARCs) to strengthen their climate resilience, including the conduct of climate and disaster risk assessments, provision of capacity-building   28
29   on value-adding activities and non-farm livelihood options, enhancing access to innovative agricultural insurance coverage such as weather index-based insurance, and       29
30   enhancing their capacity to adopt climate-resilient technologies. The DAR, in coordination with other relevant agencies, shall also capacitate the ARCs in the use of       30
31   renewable energy and energy efficiency, ecological solid waste management, and sustainable land use such as organic farming approaches, and the use of rainwater            31
32   catchments.                                                                                                                                                                 32
33        7. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The DAR shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments through the Unified Reporting              33
34   System (URS) or other electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, unitl such time that the agency has fully adopted the Budget and Treasury Management             34
35   System (BTMS), within thirty (30) days after the end of every quarter.                                                                                                      35
36        Likewise, the DAR shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                              36
37        The DAR shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the House of Representatives, Senate of the Philippines, House     37
38   Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, and regulations. The    38
39   date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                                           39

15   R.A. No. 1556 and Section 5 of R.A. No. 1578.                                                                                                                                          15

21   safeguard duties, constituted into the Remedies Fund in accordance with Section 34 of R.A. No. 8800.                                                                                   21
22          Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of a budget request and other relevant budgetary requirements, and in accordance with judicious fiscal                      22

24         5. Competitiveness Enhancement Measures Fund. In addition to the amounts appropriated herein, the amount chargeable against the SAGF reflected in                                24
25   the BESF Table B.15 under the FY 2027 Proposed Expenditures shall be earmarked for competitiveness enhancement measures for agri-fishery industries affected by                        25
26   increased imports, sourced from fifty percent (50%) of the revenues collected from fees, charges, and safeguard duties, constituted into the Competitiveness Enhancement               26
27   Measures Fund in accordance with Section 34 of R.A. No. 8800: Provided , That such fund shall be utilized for the implementation of agricultural and fisheries programs,               27
28   projects, and activities that promote competitiveness, such as, but not limited to, the following: (i) development and accreditation of nurseries for plants and stock                 28
29   farms for livestock; (ii) organization of farmers into cooperatives and associations, especially those engaged in coffee farming; (iii) selection and distribution of site-            29
30   specific planting varieties; (iv) repopulation and enhancement of multiplier farms; (v) establishment of postharvest facilities; and (vi) provision of market access and               30
31   branding support.                                                                                                                                                                      31

34   programming by the National Government, as well as applicable laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                            34

53         8. Quick Response Fund. The amount of One Billion Pesos (P1,000,000,000) appropriated herein for the Quick Response Fund (QRF) shall serve as a stand-by fund                    53
54   to be used for: (i) provision of various production inputs for crops, livestock, and poultry; (ii) repair of production, post-production facilities, small-scale irrigation systems,   54
55   equipment, and machinery; (iii) provision of other assistance in the form of cash for culled live animals, and fuel assistance to farmers, subject to guidelines issued by the         55
     DA; and (iv) provision of necessary tools and supplies directly used to mitigate the effects of an ongoing disaster, in order that the situation and living conditions of
     people in communities or areas affected by natural or human-induced calamities, epidemics, crises and catastrophes, which occurred in the last quarter of the immediately
     preceding year and those occurring during the current year may be normalized as quickly as possible. In no case shall the QRF be used for pre-disaster activities, such as
     conduct of training, insurance of assets, and public information and education initiatives, or any other purpose not authorized in this provision.

27          10. National Programs of the Department of Agriculture. The amount of Thirty Nine Billion Two Hundred Nineteen Million Two Hundred Sixty Seven 27
28   Thousand Pesos (P39,219,267,000) appropriated herein for the National Programs for Rice, Corn, High Value Crops Development, Organic Agriculture, and Urban and Peri- 28
29   Urban Agriculture shall be implemented with priority given to: (i) major rice, corn, high value crops-producing provinces, organic agriculture practicing provinces, and 29
30   provinces with areas suitable for conversion to organic and urban and peri-urban agriculture; (ii) areas where the majority of the small farmers and fisherfolk registered 30
31   under the Registry System for Basic Sectors in Agriculture (RSBSA) are located; and (iii) provinces or regions where the absolute number of poor farmers or fisherfolk and 31
32   the incidence of poverty are high as identified in the latest official poverty statistics of the PSA.                                                                                32
33          11. Farm-to-Market Road Projects. The amount of Sixteen Billion Pesos (P16,000,000,000) appropriated herein for Farm-to-Market Road (FMR) projects shall be 33
34   used for the construction, improvement, rehabilitation, and repair of FMRs in accordance with the National FMR Network Plan (2023-2028). For this purpose, the DA through 34
35   its Bureau of Agriculture and Fisheries Engineering (BAFE) and Regional Field Units (RFUs) shall undertake the planning and implementation of the program and may enter 35
36   into a MOA with the DPWH, qualified LGUs or through Public Private Partnerships. The DA shall ensure that: (i) the FMR network plan shall include the scope of work, 36
37   estimated length in kilometers, and specific location for each of the FMR projects, as well as a list of priority FMR projects, which must lead to arterial or secondary 37
38   roads and key production areas; (ii) the detailed engineering design and program of works have passed technical review; (iii) prior to the procurement of any FMR project, 38
39   the approved budget for the contract is subjected to cost validation by the DA-BAFE, taking into account prevailing market prices, standard unit costs, and site-specific 39
40   conditions; and (iv) the FMRs implemented are properly geo-tagged.                                                                                                                   40
41          The approved FMR network plan shall be regularly updated to prioritize: (i) major rice, corn, high value commercial crops, livestock, and fishery producing provinces; 41
42   (ii) areas where the majority of small farmers and agrarian reform beneficiaries registered under the RSBSA are located; and (iii) provinces or regions where the absolute 42
43   number of poor farmers and the incidence of poverty are high as identified in the latest official poverty statistics of the PSA.                                                     43
44          Upon completion of the construction, improvement, rehabilitation, and repair of FMRs, the DA shall turn over the management and ownership thereof to the LGUs 44
45   concerned, which shall commit to shoulder the maintenance and repair costs.                                                                                                          45
46          Implementation of FMR projects shall be subject to DA A.0. No. 4 dated March 6, 2026 and such other guidelines as may be issued by the DA. The DA shall maintain 46
47   and regularly update a publicly accessible online dashboard on its official website containing information on FMR projects, including but not limited to the project timeline 47
48   and status of each project, location, list of contracts awarded and corresponding contractors, funding source, amounts obligated and disbursed, and such other relevant 48
49   details as may be necessary to ensure transparency and accountability.                                                                                                               49
50          The DA-BAFE shall, within thirty (30) days after the end of each quarter, submit to the House Committee on Appropriations and the Senate Committee on Finance, a 50
51   report on the status and implementation of FMR projects, including financial and physical accomplishments and issues affecting implementation.                                       51
52          The details of the FMR projects, including the coordinates, are provided in Volume I-B of this Act.                                                                           52

18         14. Engineering and Administrative Overhead Expenses. The DA is authorized to deduct engineering and administrative overhead (EAO) expenses not                             18
19   exceeding one percent (1%) of the project funds for small-scale irrigation projects, and other infrastructure projects costing more than One Million Pesos (P1,000,000).          19
20         The authorized EAO expenses shall be limited to: (i) administrative overhead including the hiring of individuals engaged as job orders or contracts of service or such      20
21   other engagement of personnel without any employer-employee relationship; (ii) pre-construction activities such as topographic survey, and detailed engineering design,           21
22   among others; (iii) construction project supervision, monitoring and project management; (iv) conduct of Constructors’ Performance Evaluation System; and (v) testing,            22
23   evaluation, and quality control. The EAO expenses shall be treated or booked-up as capitalized expenditures and form part of the project cost. Implementation of this             23
24   provision shall be subject to DA-DBM J.M.C. No. 4 dated May 27, 2021, and such other guidelines as may be issued jointly by the DA and DBM.                                       24
25         Disbursements or expenditures by the DA in violation of the above requirements shall be void and shall subject the erring officials and employees to disciplinary           25
26   actions in accordance with Section 43, Chapter 5, and Section 80, Chapter 7, Book VI of E.O. No. 292, s. 1987, and to appropriate civil and criminal actions under                26
27   existing laws.                                                                                                                                                                    27
28         15. Rice-for-All Program. The amount of Ten Billion Pesos (P10,000,000,000) appropriated herein for the Rice-for-All (RFA) Program shall be released directly to            28
29   the Food Terminal, Inc. (FTI).                                                                                                                                                    29
30         The amount shall be used for: (i) procurement of rice to be sold at affordable prices; (ii) logistics and nationwide distribution, including costs for warehouse leasing;   30
31   and (iii) other operational expenses relative to the implementation, expansion, and monitoring of the RFA Program.                                                                31
32         16. Seed Buffer Stocking. The amount of Nine Hundred Forty One Million Four Hundred Forty One Thousand Pesos (P941,441,000) appropriated herein under                       32
33   Production Support Services Sub-Program on Rice, Corn, and High Value Crops shall be used for the purchase of seeds for buffer stocking to ensure the availability of high        33
34   quality seeds of rice, corn, and high value crops to be used in times of calamities and unforeseen events affecting the production. In the distribution of seeds, the DA shall    34
35   prioritize major rice, corn, and high value crops producing provinces in geographically isolated and disadvantaged areas (GIDA), as well as those affected by the typhoons        35
36   and natural calamities.                                                                                                                                                           36
37         17. Resilience of Agricultural Communities. The DA shall endeavor to increase the resilience of agricultural communities through the implementation of                      37
38   disaster-resilient agricultural infrastructure projects, and the distribution and development of seeds which are optimally adaptive to present and future climate conditions.     38
39         The DA shall also conduct seminars and trainings for LGUs and farmers on the importance of water catchments and organic farming approaches, among the other                 39
40   elements of sustainable land use.                                                                                                                                                 40
41         18. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The DA shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments through the Unified Reporting                   41
42   System (URS) or other electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the Budget and Treasury Management                   42
43   System (BTMS), within thirty (30) days after the end of every quarter.                                                                                                            43
44         Likewise, the DA shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                                    44
45         The DA shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the House of Representatives, Senate of the Philippines, House           45
46   Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, and regulations. The          46
47   date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                                                 47

47   appropriated herein for Agro-Industry Modernization Credit and Financing Program Administration includes the amount of Two Billion Seven Hundred Fifty Million Pesos                                                   47
48   (P2,750,000,000) which shall be transferred to GFIs, cooperative banks, rural banks and viable non-government organizations, to be used exclusively for the establishment of                                           48

38   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                               38
39        1. Wildlife Management Fund. In addition to the amounts appropriated herein, the amount chargeable against the SAGF reflected in the BESF Table B.15 under                    39
40   the FY 2027 Proposed Expenditures shall be used for the rehabilitation or restoration of declared aquatic critical habitats, all aquatic resources and all marine mammals          40
41   except dugong, as well as scientific research support, and enforcement and monitoring activities of the BFAR, sourced from donations, contributions, endowments and fines          41
42   imposed for violations within its jurisdiction, constituted into the Wildlife Management Fund pursuant to Section 29 in relation to Section 4 of R.A. No. 9147.                    42
43         Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of a budget request and other relevant budgetary requirements, and in accordance with judicious fiscal                   43
44   programming by the National Government, as well as applicable laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                        44
45        2. Fisheries Management Fund. In addition to the amounts appropriated herein, the amount chargeable against the SAGF reflected in the BESF Table B.15 under                   45
46   the FY 2027 Proposed Expenditures shall be used for the conservation, preservation, protection, management, development, and regulation of fishery and aquatic resources,          46
47   research and development, and capability building of the various stakeholders ‘including provision for scholarships, supplementary livelihood for poverty alleviation, and         47
48   improvement of productivity and processes of the various stakeholders, in accordance with the allocation provided under Section 19 of R.A. No. 10654, sourced from                 48
49   proceeds of the sale of forfeited fish, fishing gears, paraphernalia, and fishing vessels, endowments, grants, donations, and administrative fines and penalties imposed under     49
50   the same Act, constituted into the Fisheries Management Fund pursuant to the same provision.                                                                                       50
51         Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of a budget request and other relevant budgetary requirements, and in accordance with judicious fiscal                   51
52   programming by the National Government, as well as applicable laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                        52
53        3. Quick Response Fund. The amount of Two Hundred Fifty Million Pesos (P250,000,000) appropriated herein for the Quick Response Fund (QRF) shall serve as                     53
54   stand-by fund to be used for: (i) provision of various production inputs for fisheries; (ii) repair of damaged or destroyed fisheries-related infrastructure and replacement of    54
55   damaged equipment; (iii) provision of fuel assistance to fisherfolk, subject to the guidelines issued by the DA; and (iv) emergency deployment, logistical support, and critical   55
56   response operations, including but not limited to rapid damage assessments, emergency clean-up of affected fishing grounds and aquaculture areas, and the establishment of         56
57   temporary facilities to ensure the continuity of fishery supply chains, in order that the situation and living conditions of fisherfolk in communities or areas affected by        57
     natural or human-induced calamities, epidemics, crises and catastrophes, which occurred in the last quarter of the immediately preceding year and those occurring during
     the current year may be normalized as quickly as possible. In no case shall the QRF be used for pre-disaster activities such as the conduct of training, insurance of
     assets, public information, or education initiatives, or any other purpose not authorized in this provision.

41         1. Public-Private Partnership Projects and Official Development Assistance. The Department of Economy, Planning, and Development (DEPDev) shall 41
42 evaluate public-private partnership projects and official development assistance loan-funded projects to determine their technical, financial, economic, and 42
43 social viability.                                                                                                                                                                                 43
44        2. Appropriations for Regional Development Councils. The amount appropriated herein for the Provision of Support Services to Regional Development 44
45 Councils (RDCs), as well as the Monitoring and Evaluation of the Implementation of Plans, Programs, Policies and Projects, One Hundred Sixty Four Million Nine Hundred 45
46 Nineteen Thousand Pesos (P164,919,000) shall be released directly to the DEPDev Regional Offices to be used for the operations of the sixteen (16) RDCs.                                          46
47       3. Public Investment Program. The DEPDev shall submit a copy of the Public Investment Program and its updates, to the House Committee on Appropriations, 47
48 Senate Committee on Finance, and Committees on Economic Affairs of both Houses of Congress.                                                                                                       48
49        4. Gross National Happiness. The DEPDev shall ensure that the implementation of projects and activities authorized under this Act should contribute towards 49
50 the improvement of the level of happiness in the country as measured through the four pillars of the Bhutanese concept of gross national happiness - good governance, 50
51 sustainable socio-economic development, preservation and promotion of culture, and environmental conservation.                                                                                    51
52        5. Grants for Innovation Programs, Activities, and Projects. Of the amount appropriated herein for the Establishment of Innovation Fund, One Hundred 52
53 4 Million Pesos (P100,000,000) shall be contributed to the Revolving Fund - Innovation Fund to be deposited in authorized government depository banks to be used for the 53
54 issuance of grants for innovation programs, activities, and projects in accordance with Section 21 of R.A. No. 11293. Public-Private Partnership shall also be encouraged in 54
55 the development and implementation of innovation initiatives in the sphere of research, development and extension, education, product development and testing, among 55
56 others.                                                                                                                                                                                           56
57         The implementation of this Program shall be subject to the guidelines to be issued by the DEPDev and confirmed by the National Innovation Council.                                        57

 7         1. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The Commission on Population and Development (CPD) shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical                  7
 8   accomplishments through the URS or other electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the BTMS, within thirty       8
 9   (30) days after the end of every quarter.                                                                                                                                     9
10         Likewise, the CPD shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                              10
11         The CPD shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the DBM, House of Representatives, Senate of the Philippines,      11
12   House Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, and regulations.   12
13   The date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                                        13

 9   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                          9
10          1. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical                         10
11   accomplishments through the URS or other electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the BTMS, within thirty      11
12   (30) days after the end of every quarter.                                                                                                                                    12
13         Likewise, the PSA shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                              13
14         The PSA shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the DBM, House of Representatives, Senate of the Philippines,      14
15   House Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, and regulations.   15
16   The date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                                        16

53    safeguard duties, constituted into the Remedies Fund in accordance with Section 34 of R.A. No. 8800.                                                                                                    53

 2   the URS or other electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the BTMS, within thirty (30) days after the end         2
 3   of every quarter.                                                                                                                                                               3
 4         Likewise, the TC shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                                  4

 6   House Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, and regulations.      6

43   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                            43
44          1. Revolving Fund of National Elementary and Secondary Schools for Instructional Programs. The revolving fund constituted from the income                                44
45   earned by national elementary and secondary schools from fees, charges, and assessments collected in the exercise of their functions shall be used to augment the schools’      45
46   instructional programs and MOOE. All income earned and corresponding disbursements shall be properly accounted for and recorded in the books of accounts of the                 46
47   implementing units. Disbursements therefrom shall be made in accordance with existing budgeting, accounting, auditing, and procurement rules and regulations.                   47
48          Disbursements or expenditures by the schools in violation of the above requirements shall be void and shall subject the erring officials and employees to disciplinary   48
49   actions in accordance with Section 43, Chapter 5, and Section 80, Chapter 7, Book VI of E.O. No. 292, s. 1987, and to appropriate civil and criminal actions under existing     49
50   laws.                                                                                                                                                                           50
51          2. Revolving Fund of National Elementary and Secondary Schools for Manufacturing and Production Programs. The revolving fund                                             51
52   constituted from the income earned by national elementary and secondary schools from manufacturing and production programs, including auxiliary services pursuant to            52
53   L.0.I. No. 1026 dated May 23, 1980 shall be used to: (i) cover expenses directly incurred in said programs; (ii) augment scholarship to students who are directly involved      53
54   in said programs; and (iii) cover student loans essential to support school-student projects or enterprises. All income earned and corresponding disbursements shall be         54
55   properly accounted for and recorded in the books of accounts of the implementing units. Disbursements therefrom shall be made in accordance with existing budgeting,            55
56   accounting, auditing, and procurement rules and regulations.                                                                                                                    56
57          Disbursements or expenditures by the schools in violation of the above requirements shall be void and shall subject the erring officials and employees to disciplinary   57
58   actions in accordance with Section 43, Chapter 5, and Section 80, Chapter 7, Book VI of E.0. No. 292, and to appropriate civil and criminal actions under existing laws.        58

 1         3. Revolving Fund of Department of Education Training Centers and Other DepEd Facilities. The revolving fund constituted from the income                                         1
 2   earned by the DepEd-managed or owned training centers and other DepEd facilities from rentals in the use of their buildings and facilities including board and lodging,                2
 3   shall be used for the MOOE and Capital Outlay requirements of the training centers and other DepEd facilities. Disbursements therefrom shall be made in accordance with                3
 4   existing budgeting, accounting, auditing, and procurement rules and regulations.                                                                                                       4
 5         Disbursements or expenditures by the said training centers and other DepEd facilities in violation of the above requirements shall be void and shall subject the erring          5
 6   officials and employees to disciplinary actions in accordance with Section 43, Chapter 5, and Section 80, Chapter 7, Book VI of E.O. No. 292, and to appropriate civil and             6
 7   criminal actions under existing laws.                                                                                                                                                  7
 8         4. Quick Response Fund. The amount appropriated herein for the Quick Response Fund (QRF) shall serve as a stand-by fund to be used for the replacement,                          8
 9   reconstruction, rehabilitation, or repair of school buildings and facilities in order that the situation of the learners affected by natural or human-induced calamities,              9
10   epidemics, crises, and catastrophes, which occurred in the last quarter of the immediately preceding year and those occurring during the current year may be normalized               10
11   as quickly as possible. In no case shall the QRF be used for pre-disaster activities, such as conduct of training, insurance of assets, and public information and education          11
12   initiatives, or any other purpose not authorized in this provision.                                                                                                                   12
13         Utilization of the QRF shall be subject to DBM-0CD J.C. No. 2025-01 dated April 2, 2025, and such other guidelines as may be issued by the OCD and DBM.                         13
14         5. Basic Education Facilities. The amount of Thirty Billion Five Hundred Fifty One Million Sixteen Thousand Pesos (P30,551,016,000) appropriated herein under                   14
15   the Basic Education Facilities shall be used for the construction, replacement, reconstruction, repair, rehabilitation, retrofitting, renovation, restoration, and completion of      15
16   kindergarten, elementary, and secondary school buildings, including site improvements, categorized under the following components:                                                    16
17         (a) Low-rise School Buildings;                                                                                                                                                  17
18         (b) Medium-rise School Buildings;                                                                                                                                               18
19         (c) Last Mile School;                                                                                                                                                           19
20         (d) Gabaldon and other Heritage School Buildings;                                                                                                                               20
21         (e) Technical-Vocational Laboratories;                                                                                                                                          21
22         (f) Library and Innovation Hubs;                                                                                                                                                22
23         (g) Inclusive Learning Resource Centers; and                                                                                                                                    23
24         (h) Alternative Learning System (ALS) - Community Learning Centers.                                                                                                             24
25         In addition, the DepEd shall ensure that the Gabaldon and Other Heritage School Buildings are fully restored according to the standards set in the IRR of R.A. No.              25
26   11194.                                                                                                                                                                                26
27         For this purpose, the DepEd shall coordinate with the National Commission for Culture and the Arts, the National Historical Commission of the Philippines, and the              27
28   National Museum of the Philippines for a review of the list of Gabaldon school buildings to be conserved and restored.                                                                28
29         Likewise, the said fund may be used for the following:                                                                                                                          29
30         (i) Conduct and revision of preliminary and detailed engineering activities such as site validation, subsoil exploration, perimeter survey, and geotechnical evaluation;        30
31         (ii) Construction, replacement, repair, rehabilitation of water systems, handwashing facilities, toilet facilities, and other health and sanitation-related facilities of the   31
32               schools and their adaptation for accessibility of persons with disabilities to prevent disease transmission and ensure school sanitation; and                             32
33         (iii) Acquisition of school desks, furniture, and fixtures to ensure that all newly constructed and existing kindergarten, elementary, and secondary school buildings are       33
34               provided with the corresponding number of school desks, furniture, and fixtures.                                                                                          34
35         In the implementation of this provision, the DepEd may enter into a MOA with other government agencies, such as the DPWH, qualified LGUs, and the AFP Corps of                  35
36   Engineers: Provided, That the implementation by the LGUs shall be subject to the General Provision on the Implementation of Nationally Funded Projects under this Act.                36
37   The DepEd may likewise enter into a MOA with Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) or Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs) for the construction of school buildings or                  37
38   engage a contractor to implement the same but without any profit margin or mark-up on the part of the CSO or NGO, subject to the General Provision on the Fund                        38
39   Transfers to Civil Society Organizations under this Act. For this purpose, the DepEd shall identify the legal, technical and financial requirements to be complied by the             39
40   CSOs or NGOs. In any case, the CSO or NGO shall remain responsible and accountable to DepEd in the implementation of the project. To ensure timely implementation,                    40
41   DepEd or its authorized partner implementing agencies may conduct early procurement activities, short of award, in accordance with applicable laws, rules, and                        41
42   regulations.                                                                                                                                                                          42
43         Provided, That not more than one percent (1%) of this fund shall be used for engineering and administrative overhead (EAO) expenses which shall be limited to: (i)              43
44   administrative overhead including the hiring of individuals engaged through job orders or contracts of service or such other engagement of personnel without employer-                44
45   employee relationship; (ii) pre-construction activities after detailed engineering or pre-repair/rehabilitation activities such as conduct of necessary structural test to            45
46   determine the condition of the structure and the appropriate repair/rehabilitation needs; (iii) project management including the conduct of regular monitoring to ensure              46
47   quality and timely completion of the projects; (iv) testing and quality control; (v) acquisition, rehabilitation, and repair of related equipment and parts; and (vi)                 47
48   contingencies in relation to pre-construction/repair/rehabilitation activities.                                                                                                       48
49         The EAO expenses shall be treated or booked-up as capitalized expenditures and form part of the project cost.                                                                   49
50          6. Improvement and Acquisition of School Sites. The amount of Ninety Seven Million Four Hundred Sixty Thousand Pesos (P97,460,000) appropriated                                50
51   herein under Improvement and Acquisition of School Sites shall be used for the acquisition of school sites and sites with existing structures such as, but not limited to,            51

56   their difficulties and hardships while in hardship posts, multi-grade schools, and ALS areas subject to the guidelines issued by DepEd, in consultation with DBM.                     56

58   shall a qualified individual receive Special Hardship Allowance under two (2) or more categories.                                                                                     58

 7         10. Creation of Teaching Positions, Recruitment, and Appointment of Teachers. The DepEd shall ensure the timely creation and allocation of                                   7
 8   additional teaching positions and appointment of teachers for formal school system (elementary and secondary schools) and non-formal ALS. For this purpose, the DepEd              8
 9   shall observe or comply with the following:                                                                                                                                        9
10         (a) The standards and requirements for teaching positions under the Enhanced Basic Education Information System (EBEIS) for formal school system and the Learner            10
11              Information System (LIS) for the non-formal schools as of SY 2026-2027. The DepEd shall annually update the EBEIS and LIS to ensure reliability and accuracy           11
12              of data;                                                                                                                                                               12
13         (b) Submission to the DBM of a request supported by the deployment report prior to the start of the school year to ensure timely issuance of the Notice of                  13
14              Organization, Staffing and Compensation Action (NOSCA);                                                                                                                14
15         (c) Selection of teachers based on the Comparative Assessment Results - Registry of Qualified Applicants and their subsequent appointment upon issuance of the              15
16              NOSCA with priority given to those previously created but remained unfilled; and                                                                                       16
17         (d) Assignment of teachers by schools division which shall be identified as their station. Teachers may be transferred within their station to address the imbalances       17
18              resulting from excess or shortage of teachers by reason of increase or decrease in enrollment.                                                                         18
19         The appointing authorities at the Schools Division Office (SDO), through their respective official websites, shall be responsible for ensuring that all vacant (newly       19
20   created and vacated) teaching positions must be published and posted in accordance with the CSC rules and Agency Merit Selection Plan. Duly approved appointments                 20
21   issued to the new teachers within the current year shall likewise be announced and/or posted on the DepEd bulletin boards of respective SDOs and through other modes              21
22   for at least fifteen (15) calendar days after the issuance of the appointment.                                                                                                    22

24   31, 2027.                                                                                                                                                                         24
