46   Special Provision(s) Applicable to the State Universities and Colleges                                                                                                        46
47         1. Appropriations of State Universities and Colleges. The appropriations authorized herein for SUCs shall be released and disbursed in accordance with                  47
48   budgeting, accounting, and auditing rules and regulations.                                                                                                                    48
49         2. Tuition Fees and School Charges. The SUCs are authorized to collect tuition fees and other necessary school charges in accordance with R.A. No. 8292,                49
50   without prejudice to the provisions of R.A. No. 10931.                                                                                                                        50
51         All income from tuition fees and other school charges shall be retained and deposited by SUCs in an authorized government depository bank. In case there are no         51
52   government banks in the locality, such income may be deposited in non-government banks, subject to BSP Circular No. 110 dated June 14, 1996.                                  52
53         Said income, including the amounts appropriated herein, shall be used primarily for programs and projects that directly support the core mandate of SUCs and            53
54   creation of additional positions as well as payments of magna carta benefits of public health workers subject to the guidelines issued by the CHED. In no case shall said     54
55   income be used for the payment of allowances and other benefits not authorized by law.                                                                                        55
56         Disbursements or expenditures by the SUCs in violation of the above requirements shall be void and shall subject the erring officials and employees to disciplinary     56
57   actions in accordance with Section 43, Chapter 5, and Section 80, Chapter 7, Book VI of E.O. No. 292, s. 1987, and to appropriate civil and criminal actions under existing   57
58   laws.                                                                                                                                                                         58
                                                                                                                             STATE UNIVERSITIES AND COLLEGES 845



 1         3. Hospital Income. In addition to the amounts appropriated herein, all income generated from the operations of hospitals or medical centers under SUCs shall               1
 2   be deposited in an authorized government depository bank and used to augment the hospital's MOOE and Capital Outlay requirements, subject to the following conditions:            2
 3   (i) at least twenty five percent (25%) of said income shall be utilized to purchase and upgrade hospital equipment used directly in the delivery of health services; and (ii)     3
 4   income sourced from PhilHealth reimbursements from availment of medical services shall be used exclusively by said hospitals for the improvement of its facilities, and           4
 5   the replenishment of drugs, medicines and vaccines, including medical and dental supplies used in government health care facilities.                                              5
 6         In no case shall said amount be used for the payment of salaries, allowances, and other benefits.                                                                           6
 7          Disbursements or expenditures by the hospitals in violation of the above requirements shall be void and shall subject the erring officials and employees to                7
 8   disciplinary actions in accordance with Section 43, Chapter 5, and Section 80, Chapter 7, Book VI of E.O. No. 292, and to appropriate civil and criminal actions under            8
 9   existing laws.                                                                                                                                                                    9
10           4. Free Higher Education for State Universities and Colleges. The appropriation for the implementation of the Free Higher Education (FHE) Program                        10
11   under R.A. No. 10931 shall be based on the projected enrollment submitted by SUCs during the preparation of the annual National Expenditure Program by the DBM. In no            11
12   case shall prior-year enrollment be used as a basis for appropriations and releases.                                                                                             12
13           Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of: (i) the Program of Receipts and Expenditures duly approved by the respective governing board of SUCs             13
14   pursuant to R.A. No. 8292 or their enabling charters; (ii) the list of the actual number of enrollees and fees authorized under R.A. No. 10931 certified correct by the Chief    14
15   Accountant and approved by the head of the SUC; and (iii) budget request and other relevant budgetary requirements in accordance with applicable laws, rules, and                15
16   regulations.                                                                                                                                                                     16
17           The SUCs and CHED shall ensure that the enrollment capacity is strictly observed in the implementation of this Program pursuant to R.A. No. 10931 and its IRR.           17
18   The amount appropriated herein shall not be used to cover any increase in tuition and other school fees notwithstanding the lapse of the moratorium thereon.                     18
19           In case the appropriation is depleted, the SUCs may charge the funding requirements against their internally generated funds, subject to accounting and auditing         19
20   rules and regulations.                                                                                                                                                           20
21         5. Income from Intellectual Property. Income derived from the sale, marketing, and commercialization of intellectual property created by the faculty and                   21
22   personnel of SUCs shall accrue to the SUCs in accordance with Sections 30 and 178 of R.A. No. 8293.                                                                              22
23          6. State Universities and Colleges Infrastructure Projects. The SUCs shall ensure that their infrastructure projects shall conform to the applicable                      23
24   standards of the DPWH, ensuring structural quality, safety, and reliability.                                                                                                     24
25           Whenever applicable and cost effective, the SUCs shall endeavor to use indigenous and sustainable materials in the implementation of infrastructure projects.            25
26         7. State Universities and Colleges Programs and Course Offerings. The SUCs shall maintain only programs and courses that directly support their                            26
27   core mandate and may open only programs and courses aligned with global innovation platforms as well as the priorities of the government in key growth areas, subject            27
28   to the approval of their governing boards and the CHED in accordance with R.A. No. 8292 and guidelines issued by CHED. The funding requirements shall be charged                 28
29   against internally generated income, subject to the guidelines issued by the CHED. In no case shall said income be used for the payment of allowances and other benefits         29
30   not authorized by law.                                                                                                                                                           30
31         8. Program of Receipts and Expenditures. The SUCs shall submit to the DBM and CHED not later than November 15 of the preceding year a copy of their                        31
32   Program of Receipts and Expenditures (PREs) for the current year as approved by their respective governing boards pursuant to R.A. No. 8292. They shall likewise submit          32
33   to the DBM not later than March 1 of the current year their respective audited financial statements for the immediately preceding year.                                          33
34         The PREs shall include: (i) a statement of receipts and expenditures consistent with the COA Chart of Accounts; (ii) all receipts from internally generated income and     34
35   the proposed appropriations under the FY 2027 National Expenditure Program; and (iii) proposed expenditures.                                                                     35
36         9. Research and Development Projects. The funds intended for new research and development projects undertaken by SUCs shall be used for research and                       36
37   development projects that are consistent with, and directly related to, the priority programs of the government under the Philippine Development Plan. This may include          37
38   the promotion and enhancement of protected areas through sustainable management and ecotourism development, and accelerating climate change adaptation and                       38
39   mitigation.                                                                                                                                                                      39
40         For this purpose, the SUCs shall coordinate with other government agencies concerned that are relevant to the research and development projects being undertaken:          40
41   Provided, That the SUCs, in coordination with the LGUs and with the technical assistance of the DENR, may consider in their research program the mapping and inventory           41
42   of the biodiversity of the province.                                                                                                                                             42
43         The Presidents of the SUCs and the SUCs' web administrator or their equivalent shall be responsible for ensuring that the annual report on the utilization of funds,       43
44   including the list of recipient public or private entities, status of research being undertaken, and the amount released and utilized for each project are posted on the SUCs’   44
45   websites.                                                                                                                                                                        45
46         10. Creation, Conversion, or Reclassification of Positions. The SUCs may be allowed to create, convert, or reclassify positions as long as there is an                     46
47   authorized allocation for the purpose as appearing in their respective PREs or through scrap and build policy. The SUCs shall likewise observe the following in the              47
48   creation, conversion, or reclassification of positions: (i) the number of positions to be created shall be the same or less than the number of positions abolished except with   48
49   respect to teaching positions; (ii) the staffing modifications which will increase the number of lower level teaching positions may be allowed to augment inadequate             49
50   teaching personnel; and (iii) there shall be no increase in the total amount of Personnel Services of the SUC.                                                                   50
51         11. Laboratory Classes of State Universities and Colleges. The SUCs are allowed to maintain laboratory classes for their teaching education program in                     51
52   accordance with the policy of the CHED. The SUCs operating laboratory classes shall maintain one (1) teacher for every twenty five (25) students in each laboratory class        52
53   but not exceeding seven hundred fifty (750) students per SUC.                                                                                                                    53
54         Secondary school teaching positions in excess of the required number of teachers for laboratory classes shall be transferred to the DepEd. Pending actual transfer, the    54
55   funding requirements for said positions shall continually be paid by the host SUC.                                                                                               55
56         12. Vocational and Practicum Training of Students. The SUCs are authorized to avail the voluntary services of their students in the construction or                        56
57   repair of buildings and the fabrication or repair of equipment subject to the payment of hourly rate as may be determined by the SUCs but not to exceed four (4) hours a         57
58   day.                                                                                                                                                                             58
     846 GENERAL APPROPRIATIONS BILL, FY 2027



 1         They may likewise utilize services of students for academic, research, extension, and administrative matters as part of practicum training subject to the payment of    1
 2   hourly rate as may be determined by the SUCs.                                                                                                                                 2
 3         13. Release of Funds for Branches of State Universities and Colleges. The SUCs shall release the allocations identified in the PREs directly to their                   3
 4   branches without any reduction by the main campus.                                                                                                                            4
 5         14. Employment of Qualified Contractual and Part-time Faculty. In the hiring of new faculty, whether to fill unfilled or newly created positions,                       5
 6   priority shall be given to qualified contractual or part-time faculty.                                                                                                        6
 7         15. Inclusion of Environment, Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation, and Culture in the Curriculum. The SUCs, in coordination with the                               7
 8   Commission on Climate Change (CCC), shall ensure that the following are integrated in the school curriculum to be taught and promoted:                                        8
 9          (a) Laws on the protection of the environment, and climate change adaptation and mitigation;                                                                           9
10          (b) Environmental awareness and protection;                                                                                                                           10
11          (c) The National Service Training Program;                                                                                                                            11
12          (d) Indigenous knowledge systems pertaining to agriculture, environment, and cultural heritage, both tangible and intangible; and                                     12
13          (e) Climate and Disaster Risk Assessment.                                                                                                                             13
14         16. Technical Support to Local Government Units. The SUCs, in coordination with the CCC and the Department of the Interior and Local Government, shall                 14
15   support LGUs in the preparation and enhancement of Local Climate Change Action Plans and Comprehensive Land Use and Development Plans, including the conduct of the          15
16   Climate and Disaster Risk Assessment, and cascading of relevant climate-related capacities and technologies.                                                                 16
17         The SUCs shall coordinate with the Department of Economy, Planning, and Development and Department of Human Settlements and Urban Development in providing             17
18   support to provinces in the preparation and enhancement of their Provincial Development and Physical Framework Plan.                                                         18
19         17. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The SUCs shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments through the URS or other                 19
20   electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the BTMS, within thirty (30) days after the end of every quarter.     20
21         Likewise, the SUCs shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                             21
22         The SUCs shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on their websites to the House of Representatives, Senate of the Philippines,       22
23   House Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, and regulations.   23
24   The date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                                        24
25         18. Appropriations for Activities or Projects. The amounts appropriated herein shall be used specifically for the following activities or projects in the              25
26   indicated amounts and conditions:                                                                                                                                            26

43   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                                                 43
44        1. Proceeds from the Exploration, Development, and Exploitation of Energy Resources. In addition to the amounts appropriated herein, the amount 44
45   chargeable against the SAGF reflected in the BESF Table B.15 under the FY 2027 Proposed Expenditures shall be used to finance energy resource development, and 45
46   exploitation programs, and projects in accordance with Section 8 of P.D. No. 910: Provided , That twenty percent (20%) of the outstanding balance of this Fund may be 46
47   disbursed for expenses necessary for the effective discharge of the powers and functions of the DOE in accordance with Section 21 of R.A. No. 7638. The utilization of 47
48   funds for the Total Electrification Project shall be subject to the submission of a National Total Electrification Roadmap.                                                                          48
49         Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of a budget request and other relevant budgetary requirements, and in accordance with judicious fiscal 49
50   programming by the National Government, as well as applicable laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                                          50
51         2. Renewable Energy. The DOE shall strengthen the development, utilization, and commercialization of renewable energy resources through the establishment of 51
52   Renewable Energy Market, establishment of a Green Energy Option Program, and encouraging the adoption of waste-to-energy facilities in accordance with R.A. No. 9513.                                52
53         3. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The DOE shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments through the Unified Reporting 53
54   System (URS) or other electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the Budget and Treasury Management 54
55   System (BTMS), within thirty (30) days after the end of every quarter.                                                                                                                               55
56        Likewise, the DOE shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                                                       56

42          1. Integrated Protected Areas Fund. In addition to the amounts appropriated herein, the following funding sources, constituted into the                                 42
43   Integrated Protected Areas Fund shall be used to finance projects and activities of the National Integrated Protected Areas System (NIPAS) in accordance with                  43
44   Section 16 of R.A. No. 7586, as amended:                                                                                                                                       44
45         (a) The amount chargeable against the SAGF reflected in the BESF Table B. 15 under the FY 2027 Proposed Expenditures from the twenty five percent (25%)                  45
46              income generated by each protected area from the operations of the NIPAS and management of wild flora and fauna, deposited with the National                        46
47              Treasury and released subject to the submission of a budget request and other relevant budgetary requirements, and in accordance with judicious fiscal              47
48              programming by the National Government, as well as applicable laws, rules, and regulations; and                                                                     48
49         (b) Seventy five percent (75%) income retained by each Protected Area Management Board (PAMB), deposited in an authorized government depository bank.                    49
50         In no case shall said amount be used for the payment of Personnel Services.                                                                                              50
51         2. Wildlife Management Fund. In addition to the amounts appropriated herein, the amount chargeable againsts the SAGF reflected in the BESF Table B.                      51
52   15 under the FY 2027 Proposed Expenditures shall be used for the conservation and protection of wildlife resources sourced from fines, damages, fees, charges,                 52
53   donations, endowments, grants or contributions collected or granted within the jurisdiction of the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR),                     53
54   constituted into the Wildlife Management Fund in accordance with Sections 4 and 29 of R.A. No. 9147.                                                                           54
55          Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of a budget request, and other relevant budgetary requirements and in accordance with judicious fiscal              55
56   programming by the National Governmet, as well as applicable laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                     56
57         3. Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Program. The amounts of Fifty Five Million Two Hundred Fifteen Thousand Pesos (P55,215,000) and One Hundred                             57
58   Ninety Two Million One Hundred Twenty Nine Thousand Pesos (P192,129,000) appropriated herein shall be used exclusively in support of the Land Survey and                       58
     Distribution and Program Beneficiaries Development, respectively, under the Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Program.

 860 GENERAL APPROPRIATIONS BILL, FY 2027
          3. Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Program. The amounts of Fifty Five Million Two Hundred Fifteen Thousand Pesos (P55,215,000) and One Hundred
    Ninety Two Million One Hundred Twenty Nine Thousand Pesos (P192,129,000) appropriated herein shall be used exclusively in support of the Land Survey and
 1  Distribution and Program Beneficiaries Development, respectively, under the Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Program.                                                             1
 2        4. Operational Plan for the Manila Bay Coastal Management Strategy. The amount of One Billion One Hundred Forty Four Million Five                                        2
 3  Hundred Twenty Six Thousand Pesos (P1,144,526,000) appropriated herein shall be used for the implementation of the Operational Plan for the Manila Bay                         3
 4  Coastal Management Strategy pursuant to the Supreme Court (SC) Decision in Metropolitan Manila Development Authority, et al. vs. Concerned Citizens of Manila                  4
 5  Bay, G.R. No. 171947-48 promulgated on December 18, 2008. The DENR shall submit the following documents to the DBM to facilitate the preparation and                           5
 6  submission to the SC of the quarterly progress report on the utilization of funds: (i) quarterly reports of Statement of Appropriations, Allotments, Obligations,              6
 7  Disbursements, and Balances; and (ii) Work and Financial Plan.                                                                                                                 7
 8        5. National Greening Program. The amount of One Billion Six Hundred Seventeen Million Six Hundred Seventy Nine Thousand Pesos (P1,617,679,000)                           8
 9  appropriated under Forest Development, Rehabilitation, Maintenance, and Protection shall be used for the implementation of the National Greening Program (NGP):                9
10  Provided , That in the implementation of the NGP, priority shall be given to the maintenance and protection of established plantations, operation and maintenance of          10
11  established forest nurseries, social enterprise development, and pilot implementation of the Forest and Landscape Restoration (FLR) within Sierra Madre mountain range        11
12  and baselining of other priority landscape.                                                                                                                                   12
13        6. Climate Change Information Management System. The DENR, pursuant to its mandate under the Climate Change Act, shall oversee the establishment                        13
14  and maintenance of a Climate Change Information Management System and Network, including climate change risks, activities, and investments. The DENR, in                      14
15  coordination with the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) and other concerned agencies, shall integrate climate change-related information,        15
16  including climate and disaster risk assessments, in the Philippine Geoportal to enhance understanding of climate risks and apply them in national and local development       16
17  planning and program implementation.                                                                                                                                          17
18        7. Adaptation of Nature-Based Solution. The DENR shall ensure that nature-based solutions form an essential component of national environmental policy                  18
19  and flood mitigation strategy. All programs, projects, and activities related to watershed management, river and wetland rehabilitation, coastal protection, reforestation,   19
20  land restoration, and climate adaptation shall incorporate nature-based approaches, whenever technically feasible and ecologically appropriate.                               20
21          The DENR shall prioritize interventions such as native-species reforestation, assisted natural regeneration, bamboo and vetiver stabilization, contour farming, and   21
22  the establishment of catchment ponds to restore degraded uplands and strengthen watershed functions. The DENR shall likewise protect forests from illegal logging,            22
23  mining, encroachment, and land conversion, and rehabilitate rivers, riparian buffers, wetlands, and floodplains to allow natural water retention and reduce downstream        23
24  flooding.                                                                                                                                                                     24
25         In urban areas, the DENR shall support the use of green and sponge-city infrastructure, including permeable pavements, bioswales, rain gardens, rainwater              25
26  harvesting systems, retention parks, and green roofs, alongside the strict enforcement of solid waste laws to prevent waterway obstruction and restore natural drainage       26
27  systems.                                                                                                                                                                      27
28          For coastal zones, the DENR shall prioritize the restoration and protection of mangroves, beach forests, dunes, and seagrass beds as natural defenses against storm   28
29  surge, coastal erosion, and saline intrusion.                                                                                                                                 29
30         All planning and implementation shall be aligned with an integrated flood management and river basin framework and guided by updated multi-hazard maps to              30
31  ensure that interventions are science-based, risk-informed, and climate-aligned.                                                                                              31
32        The DENR shall submit to Congress, within the first quarter of the ensuing year, an annual report detailing the integration of nature-based solutions into its key      32
33  programs, including accomplishments, challenges, and recommendations for further policy and institutional strengthening.                                                      33
34        8. Implementation of Early Warning Systems for Water Infrastructure. The DENR, in coordination with the Climate Change Commission (CCC),                                34
35  Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH), Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG), and Department of Science and Technology (DOST), shall                35
36  implement early warning systems and forecasting tools to anticipate potential challenges related to water shortages, contamination, and infrastructure damage caused by       36
37  climate change-related disasters.                                                                                                                                             37
38        9. Identification, Assessment, and Monitoring of Vulnerable Habitats. The DENR, in coordination with the CCC, shall conduct regular identification,                     38
39  assessment, and monitoring of vulnerable habitats and ecosystems to ensure timely protection against degradation resulting from both natural and anthropogenic                39
40  activities. Further, the DENR shall implement rehabilitation measures for critical habitats and ecosystems and enhance ecosystem service outputs in response to climate       40
41  hazards.                                                                                                                                                                      41
42        The DENR shall closely coordinate with the Department of Economy, Planning, and Development (DEPDev) in ensuring convergence with the implementation of R.A.            42
43  No. 11995 or the Philippine Ecosystem and Natural Capital Accounting System (PENCAS) Act.                                                                                     43
44        10. Unified River Basin and Flood Management Database. The DENR, in coordination with the DPWH, shall jointly develop and maintain a unified                            44
45  river basin and flood management database to support integrated and science-based planning for watershed rehabilitation. Such coordination shall ensure that flood            45
46  control projects complement environmental protection and climate resilience goals.                                                                                            46
47        11. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The DENR shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments through the Unified                       47
48  Reporting System (URS) or other electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the Budget and Treasury                48
49  Management System (BTMS), within thirty (30) days after the end of every quarter.                                                                                             49
50        Likewise, the DENR shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                              50
51        The DENR shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the House of Representatives, Senate of the                        51
52  Philippines, House Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules,        52
53  and regulations. The date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                        53

 6   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                            6
 7         1. Air Quality Management Fund. In addition to the amounts appropriated herein, the amount chargeable against the SAGF reflected in the BESF Table B.                     7
 8   15 under the FY 2027 Proposed Expenditures shall be used to finance air quality rehabilitation, research, enforcement, monitoring, and technical assistance activities          8
 9   sourced from the fines imposed and damages awarded to the Republic of the Philippines by the Pollution Adjudication Board (PAB), proceeds of licenses and permits               9
10   issued, emission fees, donations, endowments, and contributions, constituted into the Air Quality Management Fund in accordance with Section 14 of R.A. No. 8749.              10
11         Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of a budget request and other relevant budgetary requirements, and in accordance with judicious fiscal               11
12   programming by the National Government, as well as applicable laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                    12
13         2. National Water Quality Management Fund. In addition to the amounts appropriated herein, the amount chargeable against the SAGF reflected in                           13
14   the BESF Table B. 15 under the FY 2027 Proposed Expenditures shall be used for: (i) finance containment and clean-up operations of the government in water pollution           14
15   cases; (ii) guarantee restoration of ecosystems and rehabilitation of affected areas; (iii) support research, enforcement, and monitoring activities; (iv) provide technical   15
16   assistance to the implementing agencies; (v) grant rewards and incentives; (vi) support information and educational campaign; and (vii) such other disbursements made          16
17   solely for the prevention, control or abatement of water pollution and management, and administration of the management areas, sourced from the collections of fines           17
18   imposed and damages awarded to the government by the PAB, proceeds of permits issued by the Department, donations, endowments, and grants in the form of                       18
19   contributions to the National Government under R.A. No. 9275, in accordance with Section 9 of the same Act.                                                                    19
20         Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of a budget request and other relevant budgetary requirements, and in accordance with judicious fiscal               20
21   programming by the National Government, as well as applicable laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                    21
22         3. Area Water Quality Management Fund. In addition to the amounts appropriated herein, the amount chargeable against the SAGF reflected in the BESF                      22
23   Table B.15 under the FY 2027 Proposed Expenditures shall be used for: (i) grant of rewards and incentives for entities whose effluent discharges are better than the           23
24   water quality criteria of the target classification of the receiving body of water; (ii) loans for acquisitions and repairs of facilities to reduce quantity and improve       24
25   quality of wastewater discharges; and (iii) regular maintenance of the water bodies within the management area, sourced from the fines incurred by the establishments          25
26   located in rural areas, fees collected under the wastewater charge system established under Section 13 of R.A. No. 9275, donations, endowments, and grants for water           26
27   quality management of the area, in accordance with Section 10 of the same Act.                                                                                                 27
28         Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of a budget request and other relevant budgetary requirements, and in accordance with judicious fiscal               28
29   programming by the National Governemnt, as well as applicable laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                    29
30         4. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The EMB shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments through the URS or                           30
31   other electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the BTMS, within thirty (30) days after the end of every          31
32   quarter.                                                                                                                                                                       32
33         Likewise, the EMB shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                                33
34         The EMB shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the House of Representatives, Senate of the                          34
35   Philippines, House Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws,                35
36   rules, and regulations. The date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                  36

22   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                          22
23          1. Income from Royalties. In addition to the amounts appropriated herein, the amount chargeable against the SAGF reflected in the BESF Table B. 15                     23
24   under the FY 2027 Proposed Expenditures shall be used for the MOOE and Capital Outlay requirements of the Mines and Geosciences Bureau (MGB) sourced from ten                 24
25   percent (10%) of royalties and revenues derived from the development and utilization of mineral resources within mineral reservations in accordance with Section 5            25
26   of R.A. No. 7942., as amended                                                                                                                                                 26
27         Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of a budget request and other relevant budgetary requirements, and in accordance with judicious fiscal              27
28   programming by the National Government, as well as applicable laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                   28
29         2. Quick Response Fund. The amount of Ten Million Pesos (P10,000,000) appropriated herein for the Quick Response Fund (QRF) shall serve as a stand-by                   29
30   fund to be used for rapid and post-disaster geohazard assessments, post-disaster evaluation, and identification of safe sites for relocation of displaced people in order     30
31   that the situations and living conditions of people living in communities or areas affected by natural or human-induced calamities, epidemics, crises, and catastrophes       31
32   which occurred in the last quarter of the immediately preceding year and those occurring during the current year may be normalized as quickly as possible. In no case         32
33   shall the QRF be used for pre-disaster activities, such as conduct of training, insurance of assets, and public information and education initiatives, or any other purpose   33
34   not authorized in this provision.                                                                                                                                             34
35         Utilization of the QRF shall be subject to DBM-OCD J.C. No. 2025-01 dated April 2, 2025, and such other guidelines as may be issued by the OCD and DBM.                 35
36         3. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The MGB shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments through the URS or                          36
37   other electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the BTMS, within thirty (30) days after the end of every         37
38   quarter.                                                                                                                                                                      38
39         Likewise, the MGB shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                               39
40         The MGB shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the House of Representatives, Senate of the                         40
41   Philippines, House Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws,               41
42   rules, and regulations. The date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                 42
43         4. Appropriations for Activities or Projects. The amounts appropriated herein shall be used specifically for the following activities or projects in the                43
44   indicated amounts and conditions:                                                                                                                                             44

32         1. Fees and Other Receipts of the Securities and Exchange Commission. The amount collected by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) from                                            32
33   fees, fines, and other charges pursuant to R.A. No. 11232 and its rules and regulations, shall be deposited and maintained in a separate account to be used for its                              33
34   modernization and to augment its operational expenses such as, but not limited to, Capital Outlays, increase in compensation and benefits comparable with prevailing rates                       34
35   in the private sector, reasonable employee allowance, employee health care service and other insurance, employee career advancement and professionalization, legal                               35
36   assistance, seminars and other professional fees in accordance with Section 175 of the said law.                                                                                                 36
37         In addition, the SEC is authorized to retain and utilize the amount of One Hundred Million Pesos (P100,000,000) from its income from the registration of securities and                    37
38   other collection pursuant to R.A. No. 8799.                                                                                                                                                      38
39         The use of income shall be in accordance with DBM-SEC J.C. No. 1 dated September 8, 2020, and such other guidelines issued thereon.                                                        39
40         Disbursements or expenditures by the SEC in violation of the above requirements shall be void and shall subject the erring officials and employees to disciplinary                         40
41   actions in accordance with Section 43, Chapter 5, and Section 80, Chapter 7, Book VI of E.O. No. 292, s. 1987, and to appropriate civil and criminal actions under existing                      41
42   laws.                                                                                                                                                                                            42
43         The SEC shall prepare and submit to the DBM not later than November 15 of the preceding year, the annual operating budget for the current fiscal year covering its                         43
44   retained income and the corresponding expenditures. Likewise, it shall submit to the DBM not later than March 1 of the current year its audited financial statements for                         44
45   the immediately preceding year.                                                                                                                                                                  45

15   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                           15
16        1. Super Green Lane Fund. In addition to the amounts appropriated herein, the amount chargeable against the SAGF reflected in the BESF Table B.15 under the               16
17   FY 2027 Proposed Expenditures shall be used for the maintenance and improvement of the operations of the Super Green Lane Facility, including the Automated Customs            17
18   Operation System and related computer systems sourced from service fees collected from importers utilizing the Facility.                                                       18
19         Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of a budget request and other relevant budgetary requirements, and in accordance with judicious fiscal               19
20   programming by the National Government, as well as applicable laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                    20
21        2. Non-Intrusive Container Inspection System Project Fund. In addition to the amounts appropriated herein, the amount chargeable against against the                      21
22   SAGF reflected in the BESF Table B.15 under the FY 2027 Proposed Expenditures shall be used for the maintenance, improvement, and upgrading of the Non-Intrusive               22
23   Container Inspection System sourced from the mandatory container security fee imposed on every 40 and 20-footer container or twenty equivalent units under the System.         23
24         Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of a budget request and other relevant budgetary requirements, and in accordance with judicious fiscal               24
25   programming by the National Government, as well as applicable laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                    25
26        3. Tax Refund. The amount of Twenty Billion Fifty Eight Million Nine Hundred Fifty Thousand Pesos (P20,058,950,000) shall be used for the following:                      26
27         (a) Refund of excess or erroneous collection of value-added tax (VAT) and other internal revenue taxes in accordance with Section 229 of R.A. No. 8424, as amended,      27
28              including legal interest thereon treated as related expense;                                                                                                        28
29         (b) Refund of excess collections of duties pursuant to Title IX of R.A. No. 10863;                                                                                       29
30         (c) Cash conversion of valid and unexpired Tax Credit Certificates (TCCs) in accordance with Section 204 of R.A. No. 8424, as amended; and                               30
31         (d) Refund of input taxes attributable to zero-rated or effectively zero-rated transactions under Section 112 of R.A. No. 8424, as amended.                              31
32         The amount intended for the payment of VAT refunds shall be limited to five percent (5%) of the total VAT collections of the BOC from the immediately preceding          32
33   year, while those for payment of the other tax refunds shall be sourced from the current year's tax revenue collections of the BOC. All tax refund payments shall be           33
34   subject to the following: (i) adjustment of the report on BOC's tax revenue collections equivalent to the tax refunds for current and prior years; and (ii) COA audit.         34
35        The amount herein shall be treated as trust receipts, subject to reversion of any unutilized amount at the end of the year to the unappropriated surplus of the General   35
36   Fund in accordance with Section 31 of R.A. No. 10963 and Section 45, Chapter 5, Book VI of E.O. No. 292, s. 1987.                                                              36
37         Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of a budget request and other relevant budgetary requirements in accordance with applicable laws, rules, and         37
38   regulations.                                                                                                                                                                   38
39        5. Informer's Reward. Twenty percent (20%) of the actual proceeds from the sale of smuggled and confiscated goods or collected penalties established by law               39
40   may be given as informer's reward to persons instrumental in the actual collections of additional revenues in accordance with Section 1512 of R.A. No. 10863.                  40
41        Said amount, sourced from the proceeds of sale of smuggled and confiscated goods or collected penalties, shall be deposited with the National Treasury and recorded       41
42   as trust receipts in accordance with E.O. No. 338, s. 1996.                                                                                                                    42
43        6. Disposition of Forfeited Motor Transport Equipment and Other Articles. Motor transport equipment and other articles forfeited or abandoned in                          43
44   favor of the government shall be sold at public auction by the BOC upon approval by the DOF. The proceeds of the sale shall be deposited with the National Treasury as         44
45   income of the General Fund in accordance with Section 44, Chapter 5, Book VI of E.O. No. 292.                                                                                  45
46         Any government agency participating in the said auction shall pay out of its programmed budget for the purpose, subject to the rules and regulations on the              46
47   acquisition and use of government motor vehicles.                                                                                                                              47
48        The Commissioner of Customs and the Bureau's web administrator or his/her equivalent shall be responsible for ensuring that the list of forfeited or abandoned motor      48
49   equipment and other articles that have been sold in auction are posted on the BOC's website.                                                                                   49
50        7. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The Bureau of Customs (BOC) shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments through                   50
51   the URS or other electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the BTMS, within thirty (30) days after the end        51
52   of every quarter.                                                                                                                                                              52
53        Likewise, the BOC shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                                 53
54        The BOC shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the DBM, House of Representatives, Senate of the Philippines,         54
55   House Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, and regulations.     55
56   The date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                                          56

10                                                                                                                                                                                   10
11   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                            11
12         1. Tax Refund. The amount of Sixty Nine Billion Seventy Nine Million Six Hundred Twenty Three Thousand Twenty Eight Pesos (P69,079,623,028) shall be used                 12
13   for the following:                                                                                                                                                              13
14         (a) Refund of excess or erroneous collection of value-added tax (VAT) and other internal revenue taxes in accordance with Section 229 of R.A. No. 8424, as amended,       14
15              including legal interest thereon treated as related expense;                                                                                                         15
16         (b) Cash conversion of valid and unexpired Tax Credit Certificates (TCCs) in accordance with Section 204 of R.A. No. 8424, as amended;                                    16
17         (c) Refund of input taxes attributable to zero-rated or effectively zero-rated transactions under Section 112 of R.A. No. 8424, as amended;                               17
18         (d) Monetization of VAT TCCs as part of the TCC Monetization Program; and                                                                                                 18
19         (e) VAT Refund for Tourists.                                                                                                                                              19
20         The amount intended for the payment of VAT refunds shall be limited to five percent (5%) of the total VAT collections of the BIR from the immediately preceding           20
21   year, while those for payment of other tax refunds shall be sourced from the current year's tax revenue collections of the BIR. All tax refund payments shall be subject to     21
22   the following: (i) adjustment of the report on BIR's tax revenue collections equivalent to the tax refunds for current and prior years; and (ii) COA audit.                     22
23         The amount herein shall be treated as trust receipts, subject to reversion of any unutilized amount at the end of the year to the unappropriated surplus of the General   23
24   Fund in accordance with Section 31 of R.A. No. 10963 and Section 45, Chapter 5, Book VI of E.O. No. 292, s. 1987.                                                               24
25         Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of a budget request and other relevant budgetary requirements in accordance with applicable laws, rules, and          25
26   regulations.                                                                                                                                                                    26
27         2. Informer's Reward. Ten percent (10%) of the revenues, surcharges or fees recovered, or fines or penalties imposed for violations of R.A. No. 8424, as                  27
28   amended, or One Million Pesos (P1,000,000) per case, whichever is lower, may be given as informer's reward to persons instrumental in the discovery and seizure of such         28
29   goods, except all public officials, whether incumbent or retired, who acquired the information in the course of performance of their duties during their incumbency and         29
30   their relatives within the sixth degree of consanguinity in accordance with Section 282 (A) of R.A. No. 8424, as amended.                                                       30
31         Said amount, sourced from the revenues, surcharges or fees recovered, or fines or penalties imposed, shall be deposited with the National Treasury and recorded as        31
32   trust receipts in accordance with E.O. No. 338, s. 1996.                                                                                                                        32
33         3. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments                  33
34   through the URS or other electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the BTMS, within thirty (30) days after         34
35   the end of every quarter.                                                                                                                                                       35
36         Likewise, the BIR shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                                 36
37         The BIR shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the DBM, House of Representatives, Senate of the Philippines,         37
38   House Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, and regulations.      38
39   The date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                                           39
40         4. Appropriations for Activities or Projects. The amounts appropriated herein shall be used specifically for the following activities or projects in the                  40
41   indicated amounts and conditions:                                                                                                                                               41

30   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                                                   30
31         1. Department of Foreign Affairs Working Fund. All income collected in foreign service posts, including rental income and proceeds from sale of used 31
32   motor vehicles and tax refund shall be recorded as income of the General Fund. All the amounts collected in foreign currency may be retained by foreign service posts as 32
33   working fund, except for honorary consulates which may only retain not more than fifty percent (50%) of such collections in foreign currency for reimbursement of their 33
34   administrative expenses. For this purpose, the total amount of income retained and the allotments released for foreign service posts shall not exceed the appropriations 34
35   authorized for the purpose.                                                                                                                                                                            35
36          2. Passport Revolving Fund. The revolving fund constituted from the fees collected for the processing and issuance of passports requiring special 36
37   consideration, waiver, or issuance beyond regular office hours shall be used to improve the passporting and consular services of the DFA in accordance with R.A. No. 37
38   11983 and augment the requirements for the purchase of passport booklets. In no case shall said fund be used for the payment of travel and transportation allowances 38
39   and expenses.                                                                                                                                                                                          39
40         Disbursements or expenditures by DFA in violation of the above requirements shall be void and shall subject the erring officials and employees to disciplinary 40
41   actions in accordance with Section 43, Chapter 5, and Section 80, Chapter 7, Book VI of E.O. No. 292, s. 1987, and to appropriate civil and criminal actions under 41
42   existing laws.                                                                                                                                                                                         42
43         3. Building Fund. The amount of One Billion Four Hundred Million Pesos (P1,400,000,000) appropriated herein for the Building Fund shall be used for the 43
44   following:                                                                                                                                                                                             44
45         (a) acquisition or construction of new properties abroad and in the Philippines for chanceries and residences, as well as office space for consular offices through 45
46              direct purchase or lease-purchase agreements;                                                                                                                                               46
47         (b) renovation of deteriorating government-owned consular offices, chanceries, and residences of the Philippine Foreign Service, as well as properties under leasehold 47
48              agreement for at least twenty (20) years;                                                                                                                                                   48
49         (c) purchase of furniture, fixtures, and equipment for chanceries, residences, and consular offices;                                                                                             49
50         (d) long-term lease of chanceries, residences, and consular offices when the terms and conditions are favorable and advantageous to the government;                                              50
51         (e) payment of the services of a highly technical consultant relative to the renovation, redevelopment, and construction of chanceries, residences, and consular 51
52              offices; and                                                                                                                                                                                52
53         (f) payment of rental of a temporary office space for use by the Philippine Foreign Service Posts during construction or major renovation of chanceries and 53
54              consular offices.                                                                                                                                                                           54
55         The DFA shall consider all previously committed undertakings and the available balance of the Building Fund in the programming for the current year and give 55
56   preference to the acquisition or construction of properties abroad and renovation of government-owned properties.                                                                                      56
57         4. Purchase of Passport Booklets. The amount of Five Billion Seven Hundred Ninety Nine Million Three Hundred Seventy Thousand Pesos (P5,799,370,000) 57
     appropriated herein shall be used for the purchase of passport booklets and cost of personalization including the next generation passport. Any deficiency for the
     purchase of passport booklets and personalization may be augmented by the Passport Revolving Fund. Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of a budget
     request and other relevant budgetary requirements in accordance with applicable laws, rules, and regulations.
                                                                                                    1005
     1006 GENERAL APPROPRIATIONS BILL, FY 2027

            4. Purchase of Passport Booklets. The amount of Five Billion Seven Hundred Ninety Nine Million Three Hundred Seventy Thousand Pesos (P5,799,370,000)
 1    appropriated herein shall be used for the purchase of passport booklets and cost of personalization including the next generation passport. Any deficiency for the 1
 2    purchase of passport booklets and personalization may be augmented by the Passport Revolving Fund. Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of a budget 2
 3    request and other relevant budgetary requirements in accordance with applicable laws, rules, and regulations.                                                               3
 4          5. Insurance Proceeds. Notwithstanding any provision of law to the contrary, the Secretary of Foreign Affairs is authorized to retain and use insurance 4
 5    proceeds covering properties in foreign posts for the replacement or restoration thereof.                                                                                   5
 6          6. Provision for Agency Attachés or Representatives and Cost Sharing Agreement. Diplomatic missions and consular offices shall furnish 6
 7    adequate office space, supplies and materials, utilities and other commonly-shared expenses such as, but not limited to, security, janitorial, other general services, and 7
 8    building insurance, to duly accredited attachés or representatives of government agencies assigned thereto: Provided , That the agencies concerned shall contribute a 8
 9    share in the cost expended by the said foreign service post.                                                                                                                9
10          7. Benefits for Alien or Local-hire Employees. The appropriations authorized for the hiring of alien or local-hire employees may be used for payment of 10
11    gratuity or separation pay to the said employees in the foreign service in accordance with local laws. This may include terminal leave and employer's share in social 11
12    security or workmen's compensation, customary in the diplomatic or consular jurisdiction.                                                                                  12
13          8. Overseas Absentee Voting. The amount of Forty Four Million Four Hundred Ninety One Thousand Pesos (P44,491,000) appropriated herein shall be used for 13
14    the implementation of R.A. No. 9189, including the conduct of continuing registration, information campaign and development, and maintenance of databases. In no case 14
15    shall said amount be used for the creation of new positions or the purchase of motor vehicles.                                                                             15
16          9. Contributions to International Organizations and Hosting of Regional or International Conferences. The amounts of Three Billion Forty 16
17    Four Million Eight Hundred Seventy Seven Thousand Pesos (P3,044,877,000) and Forty Eight Million Six Hundred Twenty Five Thousand Pesos (P48,625,000) appropriated 17
18    herein shall be used for contributions to international organizations and hosting of regional or international conferences, respectively, that have been reviewed by the 18
19    DFA and the International Commitments Fund Review Panel and approved by the President of the Philippines in accordance with M.C. No. 194 dated June 11, 2010.              19
20          10. Long-Term Lease of Motor Vehicles. Foreign Service Posts are authorized to lease motor vehicles for a period not to exceed two (2) years, with option 20
21    to renew thereafter if the lease proves to be economically advantageous to the government. However, when acquisition of motor vehicle is preferable and more 21
22    advantageous to the government, the same shall be included under the DFA's motor vehicle inventory and refleeting program.                                                 22
23          11. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The DFA shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments through the Unified 23
24    Reporting System (URS) or other electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the Budget and Treasury 24
25    Management System (BTMS), within thirty (30) days after the end of every quarter.                                                                                          25
26          Likewise, the DFA shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                            26
27          The DFA shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the House of Representatives, Senate of the Philippines, House 27
28    Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, and regulations. The 28
29    date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                                          29

23         1. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The Foreign Service Institute (FSI) shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments               23
24    through the URS or other electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the BTMS, within thirty (30) days after    24
25    the end of every quarter.                                                                                                                                                  25
26         Likewise, the FSI shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                             26
27         The FSI shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the House of Representatives, Senate of the Philippines, House    27
28    Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, and regulations. The   28
29    date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                                          29

47   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                                                                              47
48         1. Hospital and Other Health Facilities Income. In addition to the amounts appropriated herein, all income generated from the operation of specialized 48
49   hospitals, medical centers, other hospitals under the DOH, institute for disease prevention and control, drug abuse treatment and rehabilitation centers and facilities, blood 49
50   service facilities (blood stations, blood collection units, blood banks, blood centers), public health laboratories (National Reference Laboratories, Subnational Reference 50
51   Laboratories, Regional Public Health Laboratories), and such other DOH-managed health facilities, shall be deposited in an authorized government depository bank and used 51
52   to augment the hospitals' and other health facilities' MOOE and Capital Outlay requirements, to ensure the delivery of people-centered quality healthcare services and 52
53   patients' and health workers' safety as major contributor to the achievement of the Universal Health Care (UHC) goals, with priority in the UHC Integration Sites and 53
54   GIDAs, subject to the guidelines issued jointly by the DBM and DOH.                                                                                                                                                               54
55        In no case shall said amount be used for the payment of salaries, allowances, and other benefits.                                                                                                                            55
56         Disbursements or expenditures by the hospitals and other health facilities under the DOH in violation of the above requirements shall be void and shall subject the 56
57   erring officials and employees to disciplinary actions in accordance with Section 43, Chapter 5, and Section 80, Chapter 7, Book VI of E.O. No. 292, s. 1987, and to 57
58   appropriate civil and criminal actions under existing laws.                                                                                                                                                                       58
