                                                                                                                                                DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH 1025



 1          The DOH shall prepare and submit to the DBM not later than November 15 of the preceding year, the annual operating budget for the current year covering said                1
 2   income and the corresponding expenditures. Likewise, it shall submit to the DBM not later than March 1 of the current year, its audited financial statements for the               2
 3   immediately preceding year. The Secretary of Health and the Agency's web administrator or his/her equivalent shall be responsible for ensuring that the foregoing                  3
 4   documents are likewise posted on the DOH website.                                                                                                                                  4
 5          2. Fees and Charges of the Bureau of Quarantine. In addition to the amounts appropriated herein, the amount chargeable against the SAGF reflected in                        5
 6   the BESF Table B.15 under the FY 2027 Proposed Expenditures shall be used for operational requirements of the Bureau of Quarantine sourced from at least fifty percent             6
 7   (50%) of the fees and charges collected in accordance with Section 9 of R.A. No. 9271.                                                                                             7
 8          Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of a budget request and other relevant budgetary requirements, and in accordance with judicious fiscal                  8
 9   programming by the National Government, as well as applicable laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                        9
10          3. Fees, Fines, Royalties, and Other Charges of the Food and Drug Administration. In addition to the amounts appropriated herein, the amount                               10
11   chargeable against the SAGF reflected in the BESF Table B.15 under the FY 2027 Proposed Expenditures shall be used for the purposes authorized under R.A. No. 9502, as            11
12   amended, sourced from fees, fines, royalties, and other charges collected by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in accordance with the said law.                              12
13          Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of a budget request and other relevant budgetary requirements, and in accordance with judicious fiscal                 13
14   programming by the National Government, as well as applicable laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                       14
15          4. Quick Response Fund. The amount of Five Hundred Million Pesos (P500,000,000) appropriated herein for the Quick Response Fund (QRF) shall serve as a                     15
16   stand-by fund to be used for the rehabilitation and repair of health facilities, replacement of medical and health-support equipment, procurement of additional emergency         16
17   health commodities/supplies and other essential resources, provision for emergency medical assistance, emergency engagement of health personnel to provide medical and            17
18   public health services, and other operational expenses during the response phase of the emergency or disaster to ensure the rapid restoration of health services, the             18
19   delivery of critical health interventions, and the stabilization of health conditions, in order that the situation and living conditions of people in communities or areas        19
20   affected by natural or human-induced calamities, epidemics, crises, and catastrophes, which occurred in the last quarter of the immediately preceding year and those              20
21   occurring during the current year may be normalized as quickly as possible. In no case shall the QRF be used for pre-disaster activities, such as conduct of training,            21
22   insurance of assets, and public information and education initiatives, or any other purpose not authorized in this provision.                                                     22
23         Utilization of the QRF shall be subject to DBM-OCD J.C. No. 2025-01 dated April 2, 2025, and such other guidelines as may be issued by the OCD and DBM.                     23
24          5. Health Facilities Enhancement Program. The amount appropriated herein for the implementation of the Health Facilities Enhancement Program (HFEP)                        24
25   shall be used for the construction, upgrading, or expansion of government health care facilities, and purchase of medical equipment, including equipment for medical              25
26   ancillary services, and medical transport vehicles for such facilities, with priorities in the construction/completion of ongoing infrastructure projects, the establishment of   26
27   specialty centers in DOH hospitals, and the construction of Primary Care Facilities (PCFs) in the UHC Integration Sites and GIDAs, the upgrading of other DOH-managed             27
28   facilities, and the establishment of warehouses and other support infrastructure based on utmost necessity and consistent with R.A. No. 11223.                                    28
29          In the implementation of the infrastructure projects and procurement of equipment used for medical purposes and/or required for the delivery of medical ancillary          29
30   and support services under the HFEP, the DOH may enter into a MOA with the DPWH, other appropriate government agencies, or qualified LGUs in accordance with the                  30
31   General Provision on the Implementation of Nationally Funded Projects under this Act. The DOH may likewise undertake implementation through appropriate Public-Private            31
32   Partnership (PPP) arrangements.                                                                                                                                                   32
33          The implementation of the project by the implementing agencies, LGUs, or through PPP must comply with the original project scope, cost, and approved timeline of           33
34   construction except in cases of unforeseen or fortuitous events, subject to the guidelines to be issued by the DOH specifically for this purpose. The DOH shall promptly          34
35   transfer or release the funds necessary for the implementation of the projects, subject to the provisions of the MOA and to applicable budgeting, accounting, and auditing        35
36   laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                                                                                     36
37         The transfer of funds for HFEP projects under MOA with Corporate Hospitals and Ministry of Health-BARMM shall be subject to the necessary guidelines to implement           37
38   this provision, the MOA on the transfer of funds, and the existing budgeting, accounting, and auditing rules and regulations.                                                     38
39         Release of subsequent funds for the Corporate Hospitals and BARMM shall be made only when at least fifty percent (50%) of the amount previously transferred has             39
40   been liquidated in accordance with accounting and auditing rules and regulations.                                                                                                 40
41          The DOH, through the Centers for Health Development (CHDs), shall be responsible for the implementation of health infrastructure projects, procurement of medical          41
42   equipment, and medical transport vehicles, particularly the completion of project timelines and budget releases, and shall provide healthcare expertise in terms of the           42
43   specific standards and requirements of the facilities to ensure their functionality in terms of design and layout.                                                                43
44         In the implementation of infrastructure projects costing more than One Million Pesos (P1,000,000), the DOH is authorized to deduct not more than one percent (1%) of        44
45   the project cost to be used for engineering and administrative overhead (EAO) expenses. The EAO expenses shall be treated or booked-up as capitalized expenditures and            45
46   form part of the project cost.                                                                                                                                                    46
47         The details of the HFEP are provided in Volume I-B of this Act.                                                                                                             47
48         6. Medical Assistance to Indigent and Financially-Incapacitated Patients. The amount appropriated herein under Medical Assistance to Indigent and                           48
49   Financially-Incapacitated Patients (MAIFIP) shall be used for hospitalization and medical assistance to indigent or financially incapacitated patients, including but not         49
50   limited to, inpatient services, outpatient services, comprehensive checkups, emergency services, dental services, drugs and medicines as approved by the FDA, and 100%            50
51   professional fees, subject to the guidelines issued by the DOH. In no case shall more than one percent (1%) of said amount be used for administrative expenses.                   51
52          The CHDs, through their respective CHD Directors, may enter into a MOA with health facilities such as, but not limited to, DOH hospitals including the four (4)            52
53   specialty hospitals, SUC hospitals, LGU hospitals, and other medical service providers, including clinical laboratories, primary health care facilities, DOH-accredited           53
54   dental clinics, and Free-Standing Dialysis Clinics, both private and public. This shall be intended for indigent and financially incapacitated patients to ensure a               54
55   comprehensive continuum of care, subject to the guidelines issued by the DOH.                                                                                                     55
56          Likewise, the CHDs may also enter into a MOA with private hospitals and clinical laboratories for health and medical services intended for indigent or financially         56
57   incapacitated patients, which government hospitals are unable to provide, provided that such services are billed at standard or regulated rates, subject to the guidelines        57
58   issued by the DOH.                                                                                                                                                                58
     1026 GENERAL APPROPRIATIONS BILL, FY 2027



 1         The MAIFIP shall also apply to emergency cases handled by private health facilities: Provided, That the private health facility where the patient is brought is the       1
 2   closest in distance and is equipped to provide the life-saving services needed by the patient at the time of emergency, in accordance with the provisions of R.A. No.           2
 3   8344.                                                                                                                                                                           3
 4         Release of subsequent funds for the medical assistance by DOH to specialty, SUC, and LGU hospitals shall be through the CHDs and made only when at least fifty            4
 5   percent (50%) of the amount previously transferred has been liquidated in accordance with accounting and auditing rules and regulations.                                        5
 6         The DOH, in strict compliance with R.A. No. 10173, shall post on its website the names of recipient hospitals, alongside the aggregated and anonymized data               6
 7   pertaining to the age, gender, city/municipality, and disease profile of recipient indigent and financially incapacitated patients. This shall be utilized for purposes of      7
 8   public accountability, policy formulation, and research, subject to the guidelines to be issued by the DOH.                                                                     8
 9         7. Department of Health Pre-Service Scholarship Program. The amount appropriated herein for the DOH Pre-Service Scholarship Program shall be used                         9
10   to fund the scholarship of its existing scholars.                                                                                                                              10
11         After passing the board examination, the scholars of the Program shall render return service to the government in accordance with the guidelines issued by the DOH.      11
12         8. Advance Payment for Health Commodities. The DOH is authorized to deposit or pay in advance the amount necessary for the procurement of health                         12
13   commodities from the World Health Organization, United Nations Children's Fund, and other specialized agencies of the United Nations, international organizations, or          13
14   international financing institutions, subject to existing accounting, auditing, and procurement laws, rules, and regulations.                                                  14
15         9. Cancer Control Program. Of the amount appropriated herein under the Nationally-procured Commodities for Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable                    15
16   Diseases, One Billion Three Hundred Fourteen Million One Hundred Forty Six Thousand Pesos (P1,314,146,000) shall be used to cover the cost of cancer prevention,               16
17   detection, treatment, and care as components of the established National Integrated Cancer Control Program pursuant to R.A. No. 11215 and its IRR.                             17
18          The said budget will be used for the procurement and delivery of cancer, supportive care, and palliative care medicines.                                                18
19         10. Cancer Assistance Fund. The amount of Three Billion Seven Hundred Fifty Million Five Hundred Thousand Pesos (P3,750,500,000) appropriated herein for                 19
20   Cancer Assistance Fund shall be used to fund the cost of cancer prevention, screening, early detection, diagnosis, treatment, and its care-related components, including the   20
21   needed diagnostics and laboratories for cancer management of cancer patients, persons living with cancer, cancer survivors, and other individuals, subject to existing         21
22   guidelines issued by DOH.                                                                                                                                                      22
23         11. Implementation of National Health Workforce Support System. In the deployment of doctors, midwives, nurses, and other health-related workers,                        23
24   the DOH shall give priority to the following: (i) 4th and 5th class municipalities; (ii) GIDAs; (iii) Indigenous Peoples communities; (iv) where the absolute number of poor   24
25   and the incidence of poverty are high as identified in the latest official poverty statistics of the PSA; and (v) municipalities unable to achieve Human Resources for         25
26   Health standards, to include priority government health facilities.                                                                                                            26
27         12. Green Health Facilities. The DOH, through its Green and Safe Health Facilities Program, shall, as much as possible, promote the greening of hospitals and            27
28   other health facilities, including the improvement of energy and water efficiency and conservation, sustainable cooling systems, and sustainable healthcare waste              28
29   management.                                                                                                                                                                    29
30         13. Filling of Vacant Positions. The DOH shall take all appropriate measures to fill its existing vacant positions before December 31, 2027.                             30
31         For this purpose, the DOH Secretary is mandated to submit quarterly status reports to the Senate Committee on Health and Demography and the House Committee on           31
32   Health of the implementation of this provision, not later than the tenth day after the close of the quarter.                                                                   32
33         14. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The DOH shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments through the Unified                         33
34   Reporting System (URS) or other electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the Budget and Treasury                 34
35   Management System (BTMS), within thirty (30) days after the end of every quarter.                                                                                              35
36         Likewise, the DOH shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                                36
37         The DOH shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the House of Representatives, Senate of the Philippines, House       37
38   Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, and regulations. The       38
39   date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                                              39

27        1. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The National Nutrition Council (NNC) shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments 27
28   through the URS or other electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the BTMS, within thirty (30) days after 28
29   the end of every quarter.                                                                                                                                                                                  29
30        Likewise, the NNC shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                                                             30
31        The NNC shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the House of Representatives, Senate of the Philippines, House 31
32   Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, and regulations. The 32
33   date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                                                                          33

47   assistance or subsidy, and other project related costs for various 4PH modalities, to further improve the affordability of the 4PH housing packages. In no case shall more   47
48   than three percent (3%) of said amount be used for administrative expenses.                                                                                                  48

50   Government Housing Programs. Consistent with R.A. No. 7279, as amended, R.A. No. 11201, and E.O. No. 34, s. 2023, lands actually and primarily used for                      50
51   educational purposes shall be exempt from being listed as available and suitable lands for the 4PH Program and other government housing programs.                            51

25         1. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The Human Settlements Adjudication Commission (HSAC) shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and 25
26   physical accomplishments through the URS or other electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the BTMS, 26
27   within thirty (30) days after the end of every quarter.                                                                                                                                                    27
28        Likewise, the HSAC shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                                                            28
29         The HSAC shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the House of Representatives, Senate of the Philippines, 29
30   House Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, and regulations. 30
31   The date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                                                                      31

47   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                                                                        47
48        1. Free Public Internet Access Fund. In addition to the amounts appropriated herein, the amount chargeable against the SAGF reflected in the BESF Table                                                                48
49   B.15 under the FY 2027 Proposed Expenditures shall be used to provide financing for the implementation of the Free Public Internet Access Program (FPIAP), including                                                        49
50   Information and Communications Technology (ICT) infrastructure such as backbone, middle mile and last mile ICT infrastructure, construction of towers, data centers, assets                                                 50
51   and services, as may be determined by the DICT, sourced from the Spectrum Users Fees (SUF) collected by the National Telecommunications Commission, constituted into                                                        51
52   the Free Public Internet Access Fund under the management of the DICT in accordance with Section 17 of R.A. No. 10929.                                                                                                      52
53        The General Administration and Support Services in the implementation of the FPIAP shall not exceed three percent (3%) of the total financing sourced from the SUF.                                                    53
54         Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of a budget request and other relevant budgetary requirements, and in accordance with judicious fiscal                                                            54
55   programming by the National Government, as well as applicable laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                                                                 55

 1        2. E-Government Interoperability Fund. In addition to the amounts appropriated herein, the amount chargeable against the SAGF reflected in the BESF Table              1
 2   B.15 under the FY 2027 Proposed Expenditures shall be used for the implementation of the E-Government Programs and government websites, including Electronic LGU            2
 3   System, among others, primarily sourced from donations and fees as well as SUF, constituted into the E-Government Interoperability Fund (EIF) to be managed by the DICT     3
 4   in accordance with Section 33 of R.A. No. 12254. The EIF may likewise be funded through grants and loans from development and foreign partners or through applicable        4
 5   Public-Private Partnership mechanisms.                                                                                                                                      5
 6         Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of a budget request and other relevant budgetary requirements, and in accordance with judicious fiscal            6
 7   programming by the National Government, as well as applicable laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                 7

 9   provision of free public internet access in public places, subject to strategic planning and resource availability.                                                         9
10         4. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The DICT shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments through the Unified                     10
11   Reporting System (URS) or other electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the Budget and Treasury             11
12   Management System (BTMS), within thirty (30) days after the end of every quarter.                                                                                          12
13        Likewise, the DICT shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                            13
14        The DICT shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the House of Representatives, Senate of the Philippines, House   14
15   Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, and regulations. The   15
16   date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                                          16

38                                                                                                                                                                                          38
39   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                                   39
40         1. Support for the Local Governance Program. The amount of One Hundred Eighty Eight Million Three Hundred Seven Thousand Pesos (P188,307,000)                                    40
41   appropriated herein for the Support for the Local Governance Program shall be used by the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) to support the Local                  41
42   Development Councils to enable them to perform their functions under Title VI, Chapter V, Book I of R.A. No. 7160, particularly in the development of a comprehensive                  42
43   multi-sectoral development plan, and to ensure that all local development investment programs are aligned with the Philippine Development Plan 2023-2028.                              43
44         2. Monitoring and Evaluation of Assistance to Local Government Units. The amount of Five Hundred Sixty Three Million Nine Hundred Twenty                                         44
45   Five Thousand Pesos (P563,925,000) appropriated herein shall be used by the DILG in the monitoring and evaluation of the projects covered by the Local Government                      45
46   Support Fund.                                                                                                                                                                          46
47         3. Disaster Preparedness Activities. The DILG, in the exercise of its supervisory power, shall ensure that LGUs establish and maintain an efficient and                          47
48   effective impact-based early warning system with standard operating procedures for evacuation tested through drills and simulation exercises to enable communities                     48
49   threatened by typhoon, flood, storm surge, tsunami, and other impending hazards or weather-related phenomena that may cause loss of life, injury or other health impacts,              49
50   property damage, loss of livelihood and services, to respond in a timely manner and reduce the likelihood of harm or loss and damage.                                                  50
51         4. Prohibition Against New Illegal Structures. The DILG shall ensure that municipal or city government units and barangays shall prevent the                                     51
52   construction of any kind of illegal dwelling unit or structure within their respective localities.                                                                                     52
53         The head of any LGU concerned who allows, abets or otherwise tolerates the construction of any structure in violation of this Section shall be liable to                         53
54   administrative sanctions under existing laws and to penal sanctions provided for under R.A. No. 7279.                                                                                  54
55          5. Containment of the Cleared Areas. The concerned LGUs shall be responsible for preventing the construction of any kind of structures or illegal dwelling                      55
56   units in the areas that have been cleared and shall ensure that the vacated areas are not re-occupied. In case of waterways that have been cleared, it shall maintain at               56
57   least three (3) meters clearance from the riverbanks. No permit for residential or other purposes shall be issued for the site by any government agency or instrumentality.            57
     The concerned LGUs, through the National Prosecution Service of the DOJ, shall also exercise their power to prosecute professional squatters or members of a squatting
     syndicate and any individual or group who will occupy or cause other persons to occupy the cleared areas. LGU officials who failed to implement this provision shall be
     held liable under existing laws.

 7         7. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The DILG shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments through the Unified                        7

 9  Management System (BTMS), within thirty (30) days after the end of every quarter.                                                                                              9

21   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                               21
22         1. Fire Code Revenues. In addition to the amounts appropriated herein, the amount chargeable against the SAGF reflected in the BESF Table B.15 under the FY                  22
23   2027 Proposed Expenditures shall be used for the modernization of the Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP), including facility upgrades and purchase of firetrucks, firefighting,       23
24   personal protective equipment, and emergency and rescue equipment sourced from eighty percent (80%) of the taxes, fees and fines collected in accordance with Section              24
25   13 of R.A. No. 9514, as amended.                                                                                                                                                   25
26          Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of a budget request and other relevant budgetary requirements, and in accordance with judicious fiscal                  26
27   programming by the National Government, as well as applicable laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                        27
28          2. Trust Receipts from Firearms License Fees. Scholarship assistance to be extended to surviving children of deceased or permanently incapacitated                          28
29   firefighters in accordance with R.A. No. 6963 shall be allocated from the net proceeds of the firearms license fees on a "per-request-basis", subject to DBM-DILG J.M.C. No.       29
30   2024-01 dated May 10, 2024, and such other guidelines to be issued for the purpose.                                                                                                30
31         Said fees shall be deposited with the National Treasury and recorded as trust receipts in accordance with E.O. No. 338, s. 1996.                                             31
32          3. Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses of Fire Stations. The amount appropriated for the MOOE of the district, city, and municipal fire                                32
33   stations, included under the budget of the BFP's regional offices, shall be distributed within five (5) days from receipt of the allocation based on the criteria determined       33
34   jointly by the DBM, DILG, and BFP.                                                                                                                                                 34
35         4. Use of Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses for Payment of Damages. The Chief of the BFP is authorized, subject to the approval of the                                35
36   Secretary of the Interior and Local Government, to utilize MOOE for the payment of damages to property and for injury and death of civilians resulting from lawful fire            36
37   operations as determined by a competent court.                                                                                                                                     37
38         5. Quick Response Fund. The amount of Fifty Million Pesos (P50,000,000) appropriated herein for the Quick Response Fund (QRF) shall serve as a stand-by                      38
39   fund to be used for relief and rescue operations in order that the situation and living conditions of people living in communities or areas stricken by natural or human-          39
40   induced calamities, epidemics, crises, and catastrophes which occurred in the last quarter of the immediately preceding year and those occurring during the current year           40
41   may be normalized as quickly as possible.                                                                                                                                          41
42           In no case shall the QRF be used for pre-disaster activities, such as conduct of training, insurance of assets, and public information and education initiatives, or for   42
43   any other purpose not authorized in this provision.                                                                                                                                43
44           Utilization of the QRF shall be subject to DBM-OCD J.C. No. 2025-01 dated April 2, 2025, and such other guidelines as may be issued by the OCD and DBM.                    44
45         6. Rice Subsidy. The amount of Three Hundred Eleven Million Eight Hundred Seventy Five Thousand Pesos (P311,875,000) appropriated herein shall be used for                   45
46   the provision of rice subsidy, equivalent to twenty (20) kilos of rice a month, in the form of financial assistance to the uniformed personnel of BFP.                             46
47         7. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The BFP shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments through the URS or other                         47
48   electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the BTMS, within thirty (30) days after the end of every quarter.           48
49         Likewise, the BFP shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                                    49
50         The BFP shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the House of Representatives, Senate of the Philippines, House           50
51   Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, and regulations. The           51
52   date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                                                  52
53          8. Appropriations for Activities or Projects. The amounts appropriated herein shall be used specifically for the following activities or projects in the                    53
54   indicated amounts and conditions:                                                                                                                                                  54

22   shall be in proportion to the number of jails for women. Likewise, separate facilities and cells for women shall form part of the standard design in the construction and    22
23   improvement of jails and its facilities.                                                                                                                                     23
24         The implementation of the policy on the separation of management of female PDLs shall be maintained to ensure the protection and promotion of the rights and           24
25   privileges of female and minor PDLs.                                                                                                                                         25

27   Framework shall be used to enable LGUs to effectively implement disaster prevention and risk reduction measures through the strengthening of communities and people's                        27
28   capacity to anticipate, cope with, and recover from disasters.                                                                                                                               28
29         2. Prohibition on the Use of Funds. No appropriations authorized herein shall be used for the lakbay-aral and other similar activities of local government                             29
30   officials and employees.                                                                                                                                                                     30
31         3. Training Programs. The DILG, through the Local Government Academy (LGA), shall conduct training programs on (i) enhanced Local Climate Change Action                                31
32   Plans; and (ii) laws on environmental protection, ecological solid waste management, climate change adaptation and mitigation, and disaster risk reduction, including                        32
33   measures towards the preservation of the indigenous culture.                                                                                                                                 33
34         It shall also hold peer-to-peer learning exchanges on best practices for climate change adaptation and mitigation.                                                                     34
35         4. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The LGA shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments through the URS or other                                   35

40   date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                                                            40

 7         3. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The NCMF shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments through the URS or other                   7

 9         Likewise, the NCMF shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                              9

11   House Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, and regulations.   11
12   The date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                                        12

 5   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                          5
 6        1. Payment of Police Benefits. The amount of Eight Hundred Thirty Five Million One Hundred Forty Five Thousand Pesos (P835,145,000) appropriated herein                  6
 7   for the payment of police benefits shall be released upon submission by the National Police Commission (NAPOLCOM) of the list of claimants with the corresponding             7
 8   benefits and amount.                                                                                                                                                          8
 9        2. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The NAPOLCOM shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments through the URS or                      9
10   other electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the BTMS, within thirty (30) days after the end of every        10
11   quarter.                                                                                                                                                                     11
12        Likewise, the NAPOLCOM shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                          12
13        The NAPOLCOM shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the House of Representatives, Senate of the Philippines,       13
14   House Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, and regulations.   14
15   The date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                                        15

13   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                           13
14         1. Trust Receipts from Police Fees and Charges. Fees and charges collected by the Philippine National Police (PNP) by virtue of its absorption of the                    14
15   then Philippine Constabulary-Integrated National Police and AFP Units shall be used as follows:                                                                                15
16           (a)     Augment its operational requirements in accordance with E.O. No. 1002, s. 1985; and                                                                            16
17           (b)     Scholarship assistance to be extended to surviving children of deceased or permanently incapacitated police officers in accordance with R.A. No. 6963 shall    17
18                 be allocated from the net proceeds of the firearms license fees on a "per-request-basis", subject to DBM-DILG J.M.C. No. 2024-01 dated May 10, 2024, and         18
19                 such other guidelines to be issued for the purpose.                                                                                                              19
20                Said fees shall be deposited with the National Treasury and recorded as trust receipts in accordance with E. O. No. 338, s. 1996.                                 20
21          2. Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses of Police Offices. The amount of Seven Billion Two MIllion Three Hundred Thousand Pesos                                     21
22   (P7,002,300,000) appropriated herein for the MOOE of police offices shall be allocated and distributed at Two Thousand Five Hundred Pesos (P2,500) per month multiplied        22
23   by the number of police officers in each unit.                                                                                                                                 23
24         3. Quick Response Fund. The amount of Fifty Million Pesos (P50,000,000) appropriated herein for the Quick Response Fund (QRF) shall serve as a stand-by                  24
25   fund to be used for relief and rescue operations in order that the situation and living conditions of people living in communities or areas stricken by natural or human-      25
26   induced calamities, epidemics, crises, and catastrophes which occurred in the last quarter of the immediately preceding year and those occurring during the current year       26
27   may be normalized as quickly as possible.                                                                                                                                      27
28           In no case shall the QRF be used for pre-disaster activities, such as conduct of training, insurance of assets, and public information and education initiatives, or   28
29   for any other purpose not authorized in this provision.                                                                                                                        29
30          Utilization of the QRF shall be subject to DBM-OCD J.C. No. 2025-01 dated April 2, 2025, and such other guidelines as may be issued by the OCD and DBM.                 30
31         4. Personnel Services of the Internal Affairs Service. The amount of Nine Hundred Sixty Five Million Seven Hundred Thirty Eight Thousand One Hundred                     31
32   Forty Seven Pesos (P965,738,147) appropriated herein under Personnel Services shall be used for the regular pay and allowances of uniformed personnel of the Internal          32
33   Affairs Service.                                                                                                                                                               33
34         5. Payment of Back Salaries and Allowances. The Chief of the PNP, subject to approval by the Chairperson of the NAPOLCOM, is authorized to use                           34
35   available allotments for Personnel Services in payment of prior years' salaries and allowances due to uniformed members upon reinstatement into the service as                 35
36   a result of exoneration or acquittal from administrative, civil, or criminal cases by competent court, in accordance with budgeting, accounting, and auditing rules            36
37   and regulations.                                                                                                                                                               37
38         6. Use of the Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses for Payment of Damages. The Chief of the PNP is authorized, subject to the approval                               38
39   of the Secretary of the Interior and Local Government, to utilize MOOE for the payment of damages to property and for injury and death of civilians resulting from police      39
40   operations, as determined by a competent court.                                                                                                                                40
41         7. Priority in Hiring of Female Patrol Officer. The PNP shall ensure that in the hiring of new Patrol Officers, priority shall be given to qualified female              41
42   applicants to fill vacancies in women's and children's desks.                                                                                                                  42
43         8. Reimbursement of Expenses Incurred in Anti-Smuggling and Economic Subversion Operations. Expenses incurred by the PNP in anti-                                        43
44   smuggling, economic subversion or similar operations may be reimbursed out of the proceeds from the sale of items seized or confiscated by the PNP, upon the                   44
45   recommendation of the Chief of the PNP and approval by the Secretary of the Interior and Local Government.                                                                     45
46         9. Rice Subsidy. The amount of One Billion Seven Hundred Forty Two Million Ninety Nine Thousand Pesos (P1,742,099,000) appropriated herein shall be used for             46
47   the provision of rice subsidy, equivalent to twenty (20) kilos of rice a month, in the form of financial assistance to the uniformed personnel of PNP.                         47
48         10. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The PNP shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments through the URS or other                    48
49   electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the BTMS, within thirty (30) days after the end of every quarter.       49
50         Likewise, the PNP shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                                50
51         The PNP shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the House of Representatives, Senate of the Philippines, House       51
52   Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, and regulations. The       52
53   date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                                              53

13   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                               13
14         1. Revolving Fund for Agro-Industrial Products. The revolving fund constituted from the sale of agro-industrial products shall be used for: (i) payment of                   14
15   allowance to persons deprived of liberty (PDLs) working in agricultural or industrial projects at a rate of not less than One Thousand Pesos (P1,000) for each PDL per             15
16   month; (ii) payment of additional subsistence and medicine allowances of PDLs in the National Penitentiary; and (iii) purchase of additional supplies and materials, farm          16
17   tools, and equipment for the construction, maintenance, repair, and operations of agricultural or industrial projects and prison facilities. Any interest income earned shall be   17
18   deposited with the National Treasury as income of the General Fund pursuant to Section 44, Chapter 5, Book VI of E.O. No. 292, s. 1987.                                            18
19         Disbursements or expenditures by the Bureau of Corrections (BuCor) in violation of the above requirements shall be void and shall subject the erring officials and           19
20   employees to disciplinary actions in accordance with Section 43, Chapter 5, and Section 80, Chapter 7, Book VI of E.O. No. 292, and to appropriate civil and criminal actions      20
21   under existing laws.                                                                                                                                                               21
22          2. Subsistence and Medicine Allowances of Persons Deprived of Liberty. The amounts appropriated herein shall cover the daily subsistence and                                22
23   medicine allowances at One Hundred Pesos (P100) and Twenty Pesos (P20), respectively, for Fifty Six Thousand Four Hundred Fifty Four (56,454) assumed number of PDLs               23
24   for the year.                                                                                                                                                                      24
25         In the provision for the needs of PDLs covered by the subsistence allowance, preference and priority shall be given to locally produced food and refreshments, or            25
26   Philippine products consistent with Section 4 (f) of R.A. No. 6713 in relation to Section 2 (g) of R.A. No. 11981.                                                                 26
27         3. Quarters Privileges. Employees of the BuCor, COA, Philippine Postal Corporation, and public school teachers assigned at the New Bilibid Prison and Penal                  27
28   Colony Reservations, authorized to occupy or use existing quarters, shall shoulder the expenses for utilities, such as water, electricity, telephone, and similar charges.         28
29         4. Rice Subsidy. The amount of Sixty Six Million Nineteen Thousand Pesos (P66,019,000) appropriated herein shall be used for the provision of rice subsidy,                  29
30   equivalent to twenty (20) kilos of rice a month, in the form of financial assistance to the uniformed personnel of the BuCor.                                                      30
31         5. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The BuCor shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments through the URS or other                       31
32   electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the BTMS, within thirty (30) days after the end of every quarter.           32
33         Likewise, the BuCor shall post said reports on its werbsite.                                                                                                                 33
34         The BuCor shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the House of Representatives, Senate of the Philippines, House         34
35   Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, and regulations. The           35
36   date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                                                  36
37          6. Appropriations for Activities or Projects. The amounts appropriated herein shall be used specifically for the following activities or projects in the                    37
38   indicated amounts and conditions:                                                                                                                                                  38

15   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                        15
16         1. Immigration Fees and Collections. Express lane fees and charges collected by the Bureau of Immigration (BI) shall be deposited in a special trust fund 16
17   account with a government bank to be used exclusively for the following purposes:                                                                                           17
18         (a) Sixty four percent (64%) to augment the salaries of the BI's organic personnel working beyond regular office hours;                                               18
19         (b) Twenty five percent (25%) for the salaries of the BI's contractual personnel; and                                                                                 19
20         (c) The remaining eleven percent (11%) shall be remitted to the National Treasury as income of the General Fund.                                                      20
21         Travel expenses incurred by Filipino passengers who were deferred or denied boarding without a court order shall be charged from the balance of the special trust 21
22   fund account. Implementation of this provision shall be subject to the guidelines that may be issued for the purpose.                                                       22
23          Failure to comply with the above requirements shall render any disbursement from said income void, and shall subject the erring officials and employees to 23
24   disciplinary actions pursuant to Section 43, Chapter 5, and Section 80, Chapter 7, Book VI of E.O. No. 292, s. 1987, and to appropriate civil and criminal actions under 24
25   existing laws.                                                                                                                                                              25
26          2. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The BI shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments through the URS or other 26
27   electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the BTMS, within thrity (30) days after the end of every quarter.    27
28         Likewise, the BI shall post said reports on its werbsite.                                                                                                             28
29         The BI shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the House of Representatives, Senate of the Philippines, House 29
30   Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, and regulations. The 30
31   date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                                           31

 1        (a) Five percent (5%) of monetary awards by the courts to client department, agencies and instrumentalities of the government, including court-approved compromise       1
 2             agreements;                                                                                                                                                         2

 7   relevant budgetary requirements in accordance with applicable laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                   7
 8         In no case shall the trust fund be used for the payment of special allowance which had already been fully integrated in the salaries of entitled personnel.             8

13   the national government, and applicable laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                                        13

42   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                                          42
43           1. Tulong Panghanapbuhay sa Ating Disadvantaged Workers Program (TUPAD) and Government Internship Program (GIP). The 43
44   amount of Fourteen Billion Two Hundred Forty Six Million Seventy Seven Thousand Pesos (P14,246,077,000) appropriated herein under the Livelihood and Emergency 44
45   Employment shall be used for the implementation of the Tulong Panghanapbuhay sa Ating Disadvantaged Workers Program (TUPAD) and for the payment of stipend 45
46   equivalent to the minimum wage prevailing in the region of the beneficiaries who are eighteen (18) years of age and above under the Government Internship Program.                            46
47           In the implementation of the TUPAD Program, disadvantaged workers shall refer to vulnerable, marginalized, and displaced workers: Provided , That the 47
48   prioritization of the TUPAD beneficiaries shall be in accordance with the guidelines issued by the DOLE, in coordination with the agencies concerned: Provided, further, 48
49   That the DOLE shall be allowed to utilize up to five percent (5%) of the said amount to cover administrative costs of implementing the Program.                                               49
50            2. Trust Receipts from Lien on Gross Production of Sugar. The twenty percent (20%) lien imposed on the gross production of sugar remitted to 50
51   DOLE shall be used in accordance with R.A. No. 6982, as follows:                                                                                                                              51
52          (a) Nine percent (9%) for socio-economic projects of sugar workers;                                                                                                                    52
53          (b) Five percent (5%) for the death benefit program of sugar workers;                                                                                                                  53
54          (c) Three percent (3%) for maternity benefits of women sugar workers, up to the first four (4) deliveries, in addition to existing benefits granted by law or 54
55              collective bargaining agreements; and                                                                                                                                              55
56          (d) Three percent (3%) for administrative expenses.                                                                                                                                    56

54         Disbursements or expenditures by the schools in violation of the above requirements shall be void and shall subject the erring officials and employees to                         54
55   disciplinary actions in accordance with Section 43, Chapter 5, and Section 80, Chapter 7, Book VI of E.O. No. 292, s. 1987, and to appropriate civil and criminal                       55
56   actions under existing laws.                                                                                                                                                            56

 6          3. Training for Work Scholarship Program. The amount of Four Billion Three Hundred Forty Three Milllion One Hundred Forty Seven Thousand Pesos                              6

 8   Technical Education and Skills Development Scholarship and Student Assistance Programs shall be used to support rapid, inclusive, and sustained economic growth                    8
 9   through the course offerings to key employment generators in the areas of agri-fishery, agri-business, agro-industrial, tourism, information technology-business                   9
10   process management, semiconductor and electronics, automotives, other priority manufacturing industries, logistics, general infrastructure, and new and emerging                  10
11   sectors and in-demand jobs based on the Latest Market Information Report of the DOLE: Provided , That priority shall be for the training, upskilling, and reskilling of           11
12   Filipino learners, workers and professionals in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and related technologies, creative industries, semiconductors and electronics manufacturing          12
13   industry, and healthcare-related programs, including but not limited to pharmacy assistants, dental technologists, medical technologists, radiologic technologists, caregivers,   13
14   and nurses: Provided , further , That TESDA shall strengthen partnerships with industry, academe, and other government agencies to align the skills development with              14
15   labor market needs and national priorities, consistent with the current and ongoing strategies. In addition, a majority of the training programs offered to trainees shall be     15
16   those that are eligible for competency assessment and certification, and the beneficiaries thereof shall undergo mandatory assessment and certification. In no case shall         16
17   more than two percent (2%) of the said amount be used for administrative expenses.                                                                                                17
18           In the selection of students, the TESDA shall prioritize those without prior formal or vocational training as well as those coming from regions or provinces              18
19   where the absolute number of poor residents and the incidence of poverty are high, as identified in the latest official poverty statistics of the PSA. The TESDA                  19
20   shall update its existing database to effectively monitor the employment of graduates under this Program.                                                                         20
21         4. Special Training for Employment Program (STEP). The amount of One Billion Six Hundred Twenty Three Million Four Hundred Ninety Nine                                      21
22   Thousand Pesos (P1,623,499,000) appropriated herein for the Special Training for Employment Program under the Promotion, Development, and Implementation of                       22
23   Quality Technical Education and Skills Development Programs shall be used for the conduct of community-based specialty training: Provided , That at least One                     23
24   Hundred Million Pesos (P100,000,000) shall be used for the implementation of community-based livelihood programs in 4th and 5th class municipalities consistent with R.A.         24
25   No. 9509 (Barangay Livelihood and Skills Training Act of 2008). In no case shall more than two percent (2%) of the said amount be used for administrative expenses.               25
26          In the identification of beneficiaries, the TESDA shall give priority to the following, in the order of preference: (i) indigent families under the National Household     26
27   Targeting System for Poverty Reduction (NHTS-PR); (ii) Informal Sector Families; (iii) those belonging to basic sectors, as defined under Republic Act No. 11291,                 27
28   otherwise known as the "Magna Carta of the Poor"; and (iv) those under the next lower poverty level, as determined by the DSWD.                                                   28
29           TESDA shall provide and facilitate assistance to beneficiaries to access appropriate employment and to develop microenterprises.                                          29
30           Release of subsequent cash allocations shall be made only when the amount previously released has been fully liquidated in accordance with accounting and                 30
31   auditing rules and regulations.                                                                                                                                                   31

39   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                                   39
40           1. Verification Fees. In addition to the amounts appropriated herein, the amount chargeable against the SAGF reflected in the BESF Table B.15 under                            40
41   the FY 2027 Proposed Expenditures, sourced from collections of service fees for the verification of overseas employment contracts, recruitment agreements, or                          41
42   special powers of attorney, may be retained as a working fund for the administrative and operational expenses of Migrant Workers Offices, for the promotion                            42
43   of overseas employment and welfare services to Filipino workers within the area of jurisdiction of foreign missions under the administration of the Department                         43
44   of Migrant Workers (DMW) in accordance with E.O. No. 1022, s. 1985, and subject to the guidelines to be issued jointly by the DBM, DMW, and BTr.                                       44
45           Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of a budget request and other relevant budgetary requirements, and in accordance with judicious                            45
46   fiscal programming by the National Government, as well as applicable laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                     46
47           2. Hospital Income. In addition to the amounts appropriated herein, all income generated from the operations of the Overseas Filipino Workers (OFW)                            47
48   Hospital shall be deposited in an authorized government depository bank and used to augment the hospital's MOOE and Capital Outlay requirements, to ensure                             48
49   the provision of quality healthcare services to OFWs, their dependents, and other patients needing laboratory testing and medical treatment.                                           49
50           In no case shall said amount be used for the payment of salaries, allowances, and other benefits.                                                                              50
51           Disbursements or expenditures by the hospital in violation of the above requirements shall be void and shall subject the erring officials and employees to                     51
52   disciplinary actions in accordance with Section 43, Chapter 5, and Section 80, Chapter 7, Book VI of E.O. No. 292, s. 1987, and to appropriate civil and criminal                      52
53   actions under existing laws.                                                                                                                                                           53
54           The DMW shall prepare and submit to the DBM not later than November 15 of the preceding year, the annual operating budget for the current year                                 54
55   covering said income and the corresponding expenditures. Likewise, it shall submit to the DBM not later than March 1 of the current year, its audited financial                        55
     statements for the immediately preceding year. The Secretary of Migrant Workers and the agency's web administrator or his/her equivalent shall be responsible
     for ensuring that the foregoing documents are likewise posted on the DMW website.

            The DMW shall prepare and submit to the DBM not later than November 15 of the preceding year, the annual operating budget for the current year

 3          3. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The DMW shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments through the                    3
 4  Unified Reporting System (URS) or other electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the Budget and      4
 5  Treasury Management System (BTMS), within thirty (30) days after the end of every quarter.                                                                         5
 6          Likewise, the DMW shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                  6
 7          The DMW shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the House of Representatives, Senate of the            7
 8  Philippines, House Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws,    8
 9  rules, and regulations. The date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                      9

44   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                                        44
45         1. Overseas Workers Welfare Administration Fund. The Overseas Workers Welfare Administration (OWWA) Fund constituted from the 45
46   sum total of the amounts under the management and fiscal administration of the OWWA Board and Secretariat, membership contributions, investment and 46
47   interest income, and income from other sources shall be used to serve the welfare of member-Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs) and their families, including 47
48   the reintegration of OFWs, repatriation assistance, loan and other credit assistance, workers assistance and on-site services, and social benefits, and to finance 48
49   core programs and services of the OWWA in accordance with Section 35 and 38 of R.A. No. 10801.                                                                                              49
50          Disbursements or expenditures by OWWA in violation of the above requirements shall be void and shall subject the erring officials and employees to 50
51   disciplinary actions in accordance with Section 43, Chapter 5, and Section 80, Chapter 7, Book VI of E.O. No. 292, s. 1987, and to appropriate civil and 51
52   criminal actions under existing laws.                                                                                                                                                       52
53         2. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The OWWA shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments through the URS or 53
54   other electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the BTMS, within thirty (30) days after the end 54
55   of every quarter.                                                                                                                                                                           55
56         Likewise, the OWWA shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                                            56
57         The OWWA shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the House of Representatives, Senate 57
58   of the Philippines, House Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under 58
     existing laws, rules, and regulations. The date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.
1282 GENERAL APPROPRIATIONS BILL, FY 2027
         The OWWA shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the House of Representatives, Senate
   of the Philippines, House Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under

33   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                                                           33
34         1. Hospital Income. In addition to the amounts appropriated herein, all income generated from the operations of the Government Arsenal (GA) infirmary shall be 34
35   deposited in an authorized government depository bank and used to augment the infirmary's MOOE and Capital Outlay requirements, subject to the following conditions: (i) 35
36   at least twenty five percent (25%) of said income shall be utilized to purchase and upgrade hospital equipment used directly in the delivery of health services; and (ii) 36
37   income sourced from PhilHealth reimbursements from availment of medical services shall be used exclusively by said hospital for the improvement of its facilities, and the 37
38   replenishment of drugs, medicines, and vaccines, including medical and dental supplies used in government health care facilities.                                                                              38
39         In no case shall said amount be used for the payment of salaries, allowances, and other benefits.                                                                                                        39
40         Disbursements or expenditures by the hospital in violation of the above requirements shall be void and shall subject the erring officials and employees to disciplinary 40
41   actions in accordance with Section 43, Chapter 5, and Section 80, Chapter 7, Book VI of E.O. No. 292, s. 1987, and to appropriate civil and criminal actions under existing 41
42   laws.                                                                                                                                                                                                          42
43         The GA shall prepare and submit to the DBM not later than November 15 of the preceding year, the annual operating budget for the current year covering said 43
44   income and the corresponding expenditures. Likewise, it shall submit to the DBM not later than March 1 of the current year its audited financial statements for the 44
45   immediately preceding year. The Director of GA and the agency's web administrator or his/her equivalent shall be responsible for ensuring that the foregoing documents 45
46   are likewise posted on the GA's website.                                                                                                                                                                       46
47         2. Authority to Barter and Sell Scrap Items. The Director of GA, upon approval of the Secretary of National Defense, may barter or sell scrap items in 47
48   accordance with E.O. No. 888, s. 1983, as amended. The barter and sale of scrap items shall be subject to the COA rules on the disposal of government properties and sale 48
49   through public auction. The items acquired from barter shall be recorded or booked-up as government property while proceeds from the sale shall accrue to the Revised 49
50   AFP Modernization Act Trust Fund pursuant to Section 6 of R.A. No. 10349.                                                                                                                                      50
51         3. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The GA shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments through the URS or other 51
52   electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the BTMS, within thirty (30) days after the end of every quarter.                                       52
53         Likewise, the GA shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                                                                 53
54         The GA shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the House of Representatives, Senate of the Philippines, House 54
55   Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, and regulations. The 55
56   date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                                                                              56
