18   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                             18
19         1. Quick Response Fund. The amount of One Billion Pesos (P1,000,000,000) appropriated herein for the Quick Response Fund (QRF) shall serve as a stand-by                   19
20   fund to be used for the rehabilitation and relief programs and projects in order that the situation and living conditions of people in communities or areas affected by          20
21   natural or human-induced calamities, epidemics, crises, and catastrophes, which occurred in the last quarter of the immediately preceding year and those occurring during        21
22   the current year may be normalized as quickly as possible. This includes the pre-positioning of resources and other anticipatory actions for emergency situations.               22
23         In no case shall the QRF be used for pre-disaster activities, such as conduct of training, insurance of assets, and public information and education initiatives, or any   23
24   other purpose not authorized in this provision.                                                                                                                                  24
25         Utilization of the QRF shall be subject to DBM-OCD J.C. No. 2025-01 dated April 2, 2025, and such other guidelines as may be issued by the Office of Civil Defense         25
26   (OCD) and DBM.                                                                                                                                                                   26
27         2. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The OCD shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments through the URS or other                       27
28   electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the BTMS, within thirty (30) days after the end of every quarter.         28
29         Likewise, the OCD shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                                  29
30         The OCD shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the House of Representatives, Senate of the Philippines, House         30
31   Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, and regulations. The         31
32   date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                                                32

33         1. Hospital Income and Other Revenues from Golf Course Operations. In addition to the amounts appropriated herein, all income generated from the 33
34   operations of the Veterans Memorial Medical Center (VMMC) shall be deposited in an authorized government depository bank and used to augment the hospital's MOOE and 34
35   Capital Outlay requirements, subject to the following conditions: (i) at least twenty five percent (25%) of said income shall be utilized to purchase and upgrade hospital 35
36   equipment used directly in the delivery of health services; and (ii) income sourced from PhilHealth reimbursements from availment of medical services shall be used 36
37   exclusively by said hospital for the improvement of its facilities, and the replenishment of drugs, medicines, and vaccines, including medical and dental supplies used in 37
38   government health care facilities.                                                                                                                                                                            38

40   golf course shall be deposited in an authorized government depository bank and used to cover the expenses incurred in its operations. Any excess income from the 40
41   operations of the golf course may be used to augment the hospital's MOOE and Capital Outlay requirements.                                                                                                     41
42         In no case shall income from hospital and golf course operations be used for the payment of salaries and allowances of the hospital's permanent and regular                                             42
43   employees.                                                                                                                                                                                                    43

45   income and the corresponding expenditures. Likewise, it shall submit to the DBM not later than March 1 of the current year its audited financial statements for the 45
46   immediately preceding year. The Director of VMMC and the hospital's web administrator or his/her equivalent shall be responsible for ensuring that the foregoing 46
47   documents are likewise posted on the VMMC's website.                                                                                                                                                          47

46   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                                                          46
47         1. Hospital Income and Other Revenues from Golf Course Operations. In addition to the amounts appropriated herein, all income generated from the 47
48   operations of the Philippine Air Force General Hospital shall be deposited in an authorized government depository bank and used to augment the hospital's MOOE and 48
49   Capital Outlay requirements, subject to the following conditions: (i) at least twenty five percent (25%) of said income shall be utilized to purchase and upgrade hospital 49
50   equipment used directly in the delivery of health services; and (ii) income sourced from PhilHealth reimbursements from availment of medical services shall be used 50
51   exclusively by said hospital for the improvement of its facilities, and the replenishment of drugs, medicines, and vaccines, including medical and dental supplies used in 51
52   government health care facilities.                                                                                                                                                                            52
53         Likewise, all revenues derived from the Philippine Air Force Golf Club membership dues, green fees, concession fees, and such other income from business-related 53
54   operations of the golf course shall be deposited in an authorized government depository bank and shall be used to cover the expenses incurred in its operations. Any excess 54
55   income from the operations of the golf course may be used to augment the MOOE and Capital Outlay requirements of Philippine Air Force General Hospital and other 55
56   Philippine Air Force treatment facilities, subject to the guidelines issued by the DBM and the DND.                                                                                                           56
57         In no case shall said amount be used for the payment of salaries, allowances, and other benefits.                                                                                                       57
                                                                                                                            DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENSE 1309



 1         Disbursements or expenditures by the hospital in violation of the above requirements shall be void and shall subject the erring officials and employees to disciplinary    1
 2   actions in accordance with Section 43, Chapter 5, and Section 80, Chapter 7, Book VI of E.O. No. 292, s. 1987, and to appropriate civil and criminal actions under existing      2
 3   laws.                                                                                                                                                                            3
 4         The Philippine Air Force shall prepare and submit to the DBM not later than November 15 of the preceding year, the annual operating budget for the current year            4
 5   covering said income and the corresponding expenditures. Likewise, it shall submit to the DBM not later than March 1 of the current year its audited financial statements        5
 6   for the immediately preceding year. The Commanding General of the Philippine Air Force and the agency's web administrator or his/her equivalent shall be responsible for         6
 7   ensuring that the foregoing documents are likewise posted on the Philippine Air Force's website.                                                                                 7
 8         2. Trust Receipts from the Use of Equipment and Facilities. Fees and charges from the use of equipment and facilities collected by the Philippine Air                      8
 9   Force shall be used to augment its operating requirements in accordance with Section 1 of E.O. No. 1002, s. 1985. Said fees and charges shall be deposited with the              9
10   National Treasury and recorded as trust receipts in accordance with E.O. No. 338, s. 1996.                                                                                      10
11         3. Combat Expenses. An amount not exceeding Two Hundred Thousand Pesos (P200,000) per quarter for each Philippine Air Force squadron may be utilized by                   11
12   its tactical units for incidental and necessary expenses during operational exigencies. Such amount, chargeable against MOOE for combat expenses, shall be treated as cash      12
13   advance subject to disbursement and liquidation in accordance with COA Circular Nos. 97-002 and 2004-006 dated February 10, 1997 and September 9, 2004,                         13
14   respectively.                                                                                                                                                                   14
15         4. Restriction on Armed Forces of the Philippines Expenditures. No amount appropriated herein shall be used to fund expenditures of military                              15
16   personnel in excess of those authorized and required based on the actual troop strength of the Philippine Air Force.                                                            16
17         5. Rice Subsidy. The amount of One Hundred Seventy Six Million Eight Hundred Fifty Eight Thousand Pesos (P176,858,000) appropriated herein shall be used for              17
18   the provision of rice subsidy, equivalent to twenty (20) kilos of rice a month, in the form of financial assistance to the military personnel of the Philippine Air Force.      18
19         6. Restriction on Use of Funds Allotted for Petroleum, Oil, and Lubricants. The amounts appropriated herein for the purchase or acquisition of                            19
20   petroleum, oil, and lubricants for the Philippine Air Force shall be used exclusively for said purposes.                                                                        20
21         7. Reimbursement of Expenses Incurred in Anti-Smuggling and Economic Subversion Operations. Expenses incurred by the Philippine Air Force                                 21
22   in anti-smuggling, economic subversion or similar operations may be reimbursed out of the proceeds from the sale of items seized or confiscated by the Philippine Air           22
23   Force upon recommendation of the Secretary of National Defense and approval by the President of the Philippines, subject to the submission of a budget request and other        23
24   relevant budgetary requirements in accordance with applicable laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                     24
25         8. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The Philippine Air Force shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments through the                  25
26   URS or other electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the BTMS, within thirty (30) days after the end of          26
27   every quarter.                                                                                                                                                                  27
28         Likewise, the Philippine Air Force shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                28
29         The Philippine Air Force shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the House of Representatives, Senate of the          29
30   Philippines, House Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, and      30
31   regulations. The date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                              31

 1   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                             1
 2         1. Hospital Income and Other Revenues from Golf Course Operations. In addition to the amounts appropriated herein, all income generated from the                           2
 3   operations of the Philippine Navy hospitals shall be deposited in an authorized government depository bank and used to augment the hospital's MOOE and Capital Outlay            3
 4   requirements, subject to the following conditions: (i) at least twenty five percent (25%) of said income shall be utilized to purchase and upgrade hospital equipment used       4
 5   directly in the delivery of health services; and (ii) income sourced from PhilHealth reimbursements from availment of medical services shall be used exclusively by said         5
 6   hospitals for the improvement of its facilities, and the replenishment of drugs, medicines, and vaccines, including medical and dental supplies used in government health        6
 7   care facilities.                                                                                                                                                                 7
 8          Likewise, all revenues derived from the Philippine Navy Golf Club membership dues, green fees, concession fees, and such other income from business-related               8
 9   operations of the golf course shall be deposited in an authorized government depository bank and shall be used to cover the expenses incurred in its operations. Any excess      9
10   income from operations of the golf course may be used to augment the MOOE and Capital Outlay requirements of the Philippine Navy hospitals and other Philippine Navy            10
11   treatment facilities, subject to the guidelines issued by the DBM and the DND.                                                                                                  11
12         In no case shall said amount be used for the payment of salaries, allowances, and other benefits.                                                                         12
13         Disbursements or expenditures by the hospital in violation of the above requirements shall be void and shall subject the erring officials and employees to disciplinary   13
14   actions in accordance with Section 43, Chapter 5, and Section 80, Chapter 7, Book VI of E.O. No. 292, s. 1987, and to appropriate civil and criminal actions under existing     14
15   laws.                                                                                                                                                                           15
16         The Philippine Navy shall prepare and submit to the DBM not later than November 15 of the preceding year, the annual operating budget for the current year                16
17   covering said income and the corresponding expenditures. Likewise, it shall submit to the DBM not later than March 1 of the current year its audited financial statements       17
18   for the immediately preceding year. The Flag-Officer-In-Command of the Philippine Navy and the agency's web administrator or his/her equivalent shall be responsible for        18
19   ensuring that the foregoing documents are likewise posted on the Philippine Navy's website.                                                                                     19
20         2. Trust Receipts from the Use of Equipment and Facilities. Fees and charges from the use of equipment and facilities collected by the Philippine Navy                    20
21   shall be used to augment its operating requirements in accordance with Section 1 of E.O. No. 1002, s. 1985. Said fees and charges shall be deposited with the National          21
22   Treasury and recorded as trust receipts in accordance with E.O. No. 338, s. 1996.                                                                                               22
23         3. Combat Expenses. An amount not exceeding Two Hundred Thousand Pesos (P200,000) per quarter for each company or its equivalent in the Philippine Navy                   23
24   may be utilized by its tactical units for incidental and necessary expenses during operational exigencies. Such amount, chargeable against MOOE for combat expenses, shall      24
25   be treated as cash advance subject to disbursement and liquidation in accordance with COA Circular Nos. 97-002 and 2004-006 dated February 10, 1997 and September 9,            25
26   2004, respectively.                                                                                                                                                             26
27          4. Restriction on Armed Forces of the Philippines Expenditures. No amount appropriated herein shall be used to fund expenditures of military                             27
28   personnel in excess of those authorized and required based on the actual troop strength of the Philippine Navy.                                                                 28
29         5. Rice Subsidy. The amount of Two Hundred Thirty One Million Seven Hundred Thirty One Thousand Pesos (P231,731,000) appropriated herein shall be used for                29
30   the provision of rice subsidy, equivalent to twenty (20) kilos of rice a month, in the form of financial assistance to the military personnel of the Philippine Navy.           30
31         6. Restriction on Use of Funds Allotted for Petroleum, Oil, and Lubricants. The amounts appropriated herein for the purchase or acquisition of                            31
32   petroleum, oil, and lubricants for the Philippine Navy shall be used exclusively for said purposes.                                                                             32
33         7. Reimbursement of Expenses Incurred in Anti-Smuggling and Economic Subversion Operations. Expenses incurred by the Philippine Navy in                                   33
34   anti-smuggling, economic subversion or similar operations may be reimbursed out of the proceeds from the sale of items seized or confiscated by the Philippine Navy upon        34
35   recommendation of the Secretary of National Defense and approval by the President of the Philippines, subject to the submission of a budget request and other relevant          35
36   budgetary requirements in accordance with applicable laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                              36
37         8. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The Philippine Navy shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments through the URS                   37
38   or other electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the BTMS, within thirty (30) days after the end of every        38
39   quarter.                                                                                                                                                                        39
40         Likewise, the Philippine Navy shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                     40
41         The Philippine Navy shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the House of Representatives, Senate of the               41
42   Philippines, House Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, and      42
43   regulations. The date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                              43

25  Headquarters of the AFP may be utilized by its tactical units for incidental and necessary expenses during operational exigencies. Such amount, chargeable against MOOE        25
26  for combat expenses, shall be treated as cash advance subject to disbursement and liquidation in accordance with COA Circular Nos. 97-002 and 2004-006 dated February          26
27  10, 1997 and September 9, 2004, respectively.                                                                                                                                  27
28        8. Restriction on Use of Funds Allotted for Petroleum, Oil, and Lubricants. The amounts appropriated herein for the purchase or acquisition of                           28
29  petroleum, oil, and lubricants for the General Headquarters of the AFP shall be used exclusively for said purposes.                                                            29
30         9. Restriction on Armed Forces of the Philippines Expenditures. No amount appropriated herein shall be used to fund expenditures of military                            30
31  personnel in excess of those authorized and required based on the actual troop strength of the General Headquarters of the AFP.                                                31
32        10. Reimbursement of Expenses Incurred in Anti-Smuggling and Economic Subversion Operations. Expenses incurred by the General                                            32
33  Headquarters of the AFP in anti-smuggling, economic subversion or similar operations may be reimbursed out of the proceeds from the sale of items seized or confiscated        33
34  by the AFP upon recommendation of the Secretary of National Defense and approval by the President of the Philippines, subject to the submission of a budget request and        34
35  other relevant budgetary requirements in accordance with applicable laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                              35
36       11. Rice Subsidy. The amount of Twenty Three Million Three Hundred Fifty Four Thousand Pesos (P23,354,000) appropriated herein shall be used for the provision            36
37  of rice subsidy, equivalent to twenty (20) kilos of rice a month, in the form of financial assistance to the military personnel of the General Headquarters of the AFP.        37
38       12. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The AFP shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments through the URS or other                     38
39  electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the BTMS, within thirty (30) days after the end of every quarter.       39
40        Likewise, the AFP shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                                40
41        The AFP shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the House of Representatives, Senate of the Philippines, House       41
42  Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, and regulations. The       42
43  date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                                              43

48            1. Assessments and Other Collections. The DPWH is authorized to assess service utilities and franchise holders or any other corporation, entity, or person, 48
49   which may cause damage to public works or highway projects, the estimated amount for the reconstruction, restoration, or renovation of the damaged infrastructure. The 49
50   proceeds therefrom shall be deposited with the National Treasury and recorded as trust receipts in accordance with E.O. No. 338, s. 1996.                                                                                  50
51               Other collections by the DPWH such as liquidated damages due from suppliers, consultants, or contractors shall be deposited with the National Treasury as 51
52   income of the General Fund pursuant to Section 44, Chapter 5, Book VI of E.O. No. 292, s. 1987.                                                                                                                            52

56   GOCCs, LGUs, and the courts for the transfer of land titles in the name of the Republic of the Philippines or annotation of its liens and encumbrances, certification fee, 56
57   and fee for issuance of certified true copy of documents; (iv) just compensation and other expenses related to expropriation proceedings, notarization of documents, land 57
     appraisal, subdivision and titling of partially affected lots; (v) fees and/or expenses for variation orders, transaction advisors, feasibility studies, business case studies, or
     independent consultants; and (vi) reimbursements to the Project Development and Monitoring Facility Fund for the following projects:

25            3. Basic Infrastructure Program. The amount appropriated herein for the implementation of the Basic Infrastructure Program shall be subject to the                        25
26 following:                                                                                                                                                                           26
27         (a) engineering and administrative overhead (EAO) expenses shall not exceed one percent (1%) of the project cost;                                                            27
28         (b) compliance with the standards, designs, or specifications set by law and the following agencies: (i) DPWH for local roads and bridges, flood control and drainage        28
29              systems, multi-purpose buildings, or government buildings; or (ii) DPWH and DepEd or CHED, as the case may be, for classrooms, school buildings, or academic            29
30              buildings; and                                                                                                                                                          30
31         (c) turnover of the management and ownership of the infrastructure projects upon completion thereof to LGUs, which shall shoulder the maintenance and repair                 31
32              costs.                                                                                                                                                                  32
33           4. Water Supply System. The amount appropriated herein for the construction of Water Supply Systems (Levels II and III) shall be used for the construction,                33
34 reconstruction, upgrading, and improvement of water supply systems based on the technical criteria and guidelines issued by the DPWH, and relevant policies and                      34
35 issuances of the Water Resources Management Office under the DENR. The said amount shall cover all costs for the project, including water source identification and                  35
36 development, and all other project preparation and construction costs.                                                                                                               36
37         The implementation of water supply system projects shall be subject to the following:                                                                                        37
38         (a) availability of an adequate water source for the particular water supply system project;                                                                                 38
39         (b) availability of project location, which must be government-owned, free from any right-of-way claim or any other claim for resettlement or relocation; and                39
40         (c) turnover of the operation and maintenance of the water supply system shall be for the LGU, unless such responsibility is transferred by the local government to          40
41              another entity in accordance with existing laws.                                                                                                                        41
42            5. Integrated, Environmentally-validated, and Nature-based Flood and Water Resources Management Planning. The DPWH, in                                                    42
43 coordination with the DENR, the DEPDev, the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council, and other concerned agencies, shall formulate and adopt an                      43
44 Integrated Water Resources and Flood Management Masterplan (IWRFMP) consistent with the principles of Integrated Water Resources Management and ridge-to-reef                        44
45 planning. The IWRFMP shall:                                                                                                                                                          45
46         (a) integrate all flood-control, drainage, bridge, and road projects into a programmatic, basin-wide, and network-based framework that crosses political and                 46
47              administrative boundaries, ensuring that flood-control infrastructure is planned and implemented as part of an interconnected system rather than as isolated or         47
48              piecemeal projects;                                                                                                                                                     48
49         (b) incorporate nature-based and ecosystem-based solutions, such as mangrove reforestation, wetland and river restoration, watershed rehabilitation, and sediment            49
50              management, as core components of flood mitigation;                                                                                                                     50
51         (c) ensure that all DPWH flood-control and water-related infrastructure projects are supported by scientific hydrologic and geospatial studies, vulnerability                51
52              assessments, and environmental impact analyses;                                                                                                                         52
53         (d) consult and collaborate with stakeholders and independent experts such as Project Noah and the University of the Philippines Institute of Civil Engineering that         53
54              can provide scientific and data-driven insights on hydrology, climate modelling, and risk assessments to ensure that flood control plans are technically sound,         54
55              sustainable, and responsive to community needs; and                                                                                                                     55
56         (e) establish mechanisms for data-sharing, validation, and technical cooperation with development partners such as the Asian Development Bank, Japan International           56
57              Cooperation Agency, World Bank, and Academnic Institututions to formulate and implement a comprehensive, science-based national flood management strategy.              57
                                                                                                                 DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC WORKS AND HIGHWAYS 3



 1            6. Infrastructure Projects. In the implementation of infrastructure projects, the DPWH may consider the following:                                                        1
 2         (a) clustering or de-clustering in the procurement of infrastructure projects for cost efficiency and effective management with due compliance with existing                 2
 3              government procurement laws, rules, and regulations, and the guidelines issued by the GPPB;                                                                             3
 4         (b) adoption of standards for various hazards, global warming or climate change in the feasibility study, design, and detailed engineering works of all infrastructure       4
 5              projects, in coordination with the CCC;                                                                                                                                 5
 6         (c) provision of pedestrian-safe sidewalks as well as roadside tree planting;                                                                                                6
 7         (d) use of available and cost effective Coconet Bio-Engineering Solution for soil erosion control and slope stabilization; and                                               7
 8         (e) integrated flood control management approaches to reduce flood vulnerability and risks.                                                                                  8
 9            7. Assessment and Retrofitting of National Bridges. The amount appropriated for retrofitting/strengthening of permanent bridges under the DPWH                            9
10   bridge program shall include the cost of conducting an assessment of the structural strength, repair, and retrofitting of all national bridges in accordance with the             10
11   structural code of the Philippines and existing DPWH guidelines. In the assessment, repair, and retrofitting of national bridges, priority shall be given to bridges in areas     11
12   considered highly vulnerable to seismic activities, as identified by the DOST-Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS), and those damaged by                 12
13   typhoons.                                                                                                                                                                         13
14           8. Integration of Active Transportation and Road Transformation in Infrastructure Projects. Pursuant to E.O. No. 774, s. 2008, NEDA Board                                 14
15   Resolution No. 5, s. 2017, the DOH active transport playbook, and all other applicable laws, rules, and regulations, and executive issuances, the DPWH, in coordination with      15
16   the DOTr and cities where public transport supply is severely insufficient, shall aim to establish proper public transport stops for the benefit of commuters, and ensure         16
17   that all projects and activities pertaining to the construction, preventive maintenance, rehabilitation, reconstruction, upgrading, off-carriageway improvement, widening, or     17
18   paving of primary, secondary, tertiary, bypass, and diversion roads, and the construction, widening or replacement of bridges, shall be so designed and implemented as to         18
19   allocate, insofar as practicable, at least fifty percent (50%) of the road space for public transport, pedestrians, and bicycles/light mobility devices rather than the           19
20   throughput of private vehicles.                                                                                                                                                   20
21          All pedestrian crossings and/or footpaths and sidewalks to be constructed in accordance with this provision shall, by default, be at grade for the inclusion of            21
22   persons with disabilities, senior citizens, pregnant women, children with strollers, tourists with luggage, and parents with children, consistent with public health and safety   22
23   regulations.                                                                                                                                                                      23
24         For commuter safety and comfort, wherever feasible, all pedestrian and cycling infrastructure to be constructed in accordance with this provision shall be protected        24
25   or grade-separated and include shaded walkways including urban shade trees, consistent with environmental laws and public health and safety regulations.                          25
26          The DPWH shall, in coordination with DOTr, issue or update policies on road use classification, road space allocation, and road design, in accordance with the             26
27   National Transport Policy or NEDA Board Resolution No. 5.                                                                                                                         27
28         The DPWH shall regularly publish the list of road transformation and active transportation infrastructure projects and pertinent details thereof on its website and         28
29   shall furnish copies to the DOTr.                                                                                                                                                 29
30           9. Restriction on Delegation of Project Implementation. To ensure the efficient implementation of infrastructure projects, the DPWH may delegate in                       30
31   the following instances: (i) the AFP Corps of Engineers in high transportation security risk areas; (ii) inter-department or inter-agency projects; and (iii) LGUs with the       31
32   capability to implement projects either by administration or contract as determined by DPWH, subject to the overall technical supervision of the DPWH.                            32
33         In addition, for the National Sewerage and Septage Management Program, the DPWH shall: (i) provide the technical requirements; (ii) ensure that the contractors to          33
34   be engaged by the LGUs are technically capable; and (iii) regularly monitor the Program.                                                                                          34
35           10. Disposition of the Motor Vehicle User's Charge Collections. Of the amounts appropriated herein, Fifteen Billion Two Hundred Three Thousand                            35
36   Pesos (P15,000,203,000) constituting the amount collected by virtue of R.A. No. 8794, as amended by R.A. No. 11239, shall be remitted to the National Treasury as                 36
37   SAGF, and shall be earmarked solely for the construction, upgrading, repair, and rehabilitation of roads, bridges, and road drainage, specifically included under the Asset       37
38   Preservation Program: Provided , That the DPWH shall disaggregate the Asset Preservation Program and submit to Congress the list of the regular and Motor Vehicle                 38
39   User's Charge-Funded Asset Preservation Projects within fifteen (15) days from the effectivity of this Act. The DPWH shall likewise post the list on its website.                 39
40           11. National Building Code Development Fund. In addition to the amounts appropriated herein, the amount chargeable against the SAGF reflected in the                      40
41   BESF Table B.15 under the FY 2027 Proposed Expenditures shall be used to cover necessary operating expenses of the National Building Code Development Office, sourced             41
42   from the five percent (5%) share of the DPWH from the building permit fees and other charges nationwide accruing to the DPWH, pursuant to P.D. No. 1096.                          42
43           Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of a budget request and other relevant budgetary requirements, and in accordance with judicious fiscal                43
44   programming by the National Government, as well as applicable laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                       44
45           12. Right-of-Way Acquisitions and Payments of Contractual Obligations. The amount appropriated herein shall be used exclusively for right-of-                             45
46   way acquisition expenses in accordance with R.A. No. 10752 and for payment of other contractual obligations of the DPWH, relative to the implementation of                        46
47   infrastructure projects. The DPWH is charged with the responsibility to ensure that all right-of-way issues are resolved before the initiation of any infrastructure project.     47
48           13. Flood Control Projects. In line with the principles of the Integrated Water Resources Management as outlined in P.D. No. 1067, the DPWH may integrate                 48
49   water management strategies in all its flood control projects. In addition to flood control, these infrastructure projects may include water impoundment that can be              49
50   utilized for various purposes such as irrigation, potable water supply, aquaculture, hydropower generation, and other beneficial uses.                                            50
51           14. Unified River Basin and Flood Management Database. The DPWH, in coordination with the DENR, shall jointly develop and maintain a unified                              51
52   river basin and flood management database to support integrated and science-based planning for watershed rehabilitation. Such coordination shall ensure that flood control        52
53   projects complement environmental protection and climate resilience goals.                                                                                                        53
54           15. Flood Control Project Monitoring and Geospatial Validation. The DPWH, in colaboration with the DENR and Philippine Space Agency (PhilSA),                             54
55   shall implement the flood control project monitoring and evaluation program, which shall be used for the satellite-based and geospatial validation of its flood control           55
56   projects, including the classification, documentation, and publication of findings through an online dashboard shared with the DBM, DEPDev, and the COA.                          56
57           For this purpose, the DPWH shall coordinate with the PhilSA for the sharing of technical expertise, satellite imagery, analytical tools, and data infrastructure to       57
58   support timely monitoring and validation of projects. The collaboration shall include: (a) mutual access to remote-sensing and other geospatial data for project validation       58
59   and tracking, with PhilSA providing space-enabled products; (b) joint development or subscription to AI-assisted flood-mapping systems; and (c) technical training for            59
60   DPWH personnel in geospatial analytics.                                                                                                                                           60
     4 GENERAL APPROPRIATIONS BILL, FY 2027



 1          16. Project Related Expenses. For infrastructure projects costing more than One Million Pesos (P1,000,000), the DPWH is authorized to deduct, but not to                     1
 2   exceed the following percentages of the project cost, to be used for: (i) EAO expenses and (ii) MOOE:                                                                               2
 3         (a) three and one half percent (3.5%) for releases to the Central Office;                                                                                                     3
 4         (b) two and one half percent (2.5%) for releases to the Regional Offices (ROs);                                                                                               4
 5         (c) two percent (2%) for releases to the District Engineering Offices (DEOs);                                                                                                 5
 6         (d) one percent (1%) for infrastructure projects under the Basic Infrastructure Program undertaken by the Central Office, ROs, and DEOs: Provided , That the one              6
 7               percent (1%) EAO shall be given only to the implementing unit, regardless where the fund was released; or                                                               7
 8         (e) one half percent (0.5%) for infrastructure projects of other agencies undertaken by the Central Office, ROs, or DEOs, unless otherwise provided in the special            8
 9               provision of the agency concerned.                                                                                                                                      9
10         For EAO expenses, the same shall be limited to: (i) administrative overhead including the hiring of individuals engaged through job orders or contracts of service or        10
11   such other engagement of personnel without any employer-employee relationship; (ii) pre-construction activities after detailed engineering; (iii) construction project             11
12   management; (iv) testing and quality control; (v) acquisition, rehabilitation, and repair of related equipment and parts; and (vi) contingencies in relation to pre-construction   12
13   activities. The EAO expenses shall be treated or booked-up as capitalized expenditures and form part of the project cost.                                                          13
14         Disbursements or expenditures by DPWH in violation of the above requirements shall be void and shall subject the erring officials and employees to disciplinary              14
15   actions in accordance with Section 43, Chapter 5, and Section 80, Chapter 7, Book VI of E.O. No. 292, and to appropriate civil and criminal action under existing laws.            15
16          17. Implementation of Flood Control Projects in the National Capital Region. The DPWH shall implement foreign-assisted flood control projects                               16
17   and transfer the same to the MMDA only upon completion thereof or revision of the loan agreement indicating the MMDA as the implementing agency.                                   17
18          18. Geo-tagging of Infrastructure Projects. The DPWH shall undertake the geo-tagging of all its completed and ongoing infrastructure projects subject to                    18
19   the guidelines issued by DPWH.                                                                                                                                                     19
20         The Secretary of Public Works and Highways and the Agency's web administrator or his/her equivalent shall be responsible for ensuring that the status of                     20
21   accomplishments, including the geo-tagged photos taken at a spatial resolution of 2-4 cm per pixel with time stamp of the sites, are posted in the DPWH website.                   21
22          19. Quick Response Fund. The amount of One Billion Pesos (P1,000,000,000) appropriated herein for the Quick Response Fund (QRF) shall serve as a stand-by                   22
23   fund to be used for reconstruction and rehabilitation programs, activities, or projects, including pre-positioning of goods and equipment in order that the situation and          23
24   living conditions of people living in communities or areas stricken by natural or human-induced calamities, epidemics, crises, and catastrophes, which occurred in the last        24
25   quarter of the immediately preceding year and those occurring during the current year may be normalized as quickly as possible. In no case shall the QRF be used for               25
26   pre-disaster activities, such as conduct of training, insurance of assets, and public information and education initiatives, or for any other purpose not authorized in this       26
27   provision.                                                                                                                                                                         27
28         Utilization of the QRF shall be subject to DBM-OCD J.C. No. 2025-01 dated April 2, 2025, and such other guidelines as may be issued by the OCD and DBM.                      28
29          20. Green Evacuation Centers. The amount appropriated herein for the construction, rehabilitation, retrofitting, strengthening, or reconstruction of evacuation             29
30   centers shall take into account, climate risk, geohazard and vulnerability information, as well as green building standards set forth under the Philippine Green Building          30
31   Code, and other applicable laws, policies, rules, and regulations in the siting, design, and construction of evacuation centers.                                                   31
32         To ensure the judicious allocation of funds and the safety of evacuees in disaster-prone areas, the DBM shall release the funds to the DPWH and/or the appropriate           32
33   implementing unit: Provided, That priority is given to the high-risk areas in the Philippines identified through the GeoRisk Philippines, a multi-agency initiative led by the     33
34   DOST-PHIVOLCS.                                                                                                                                                                     34
35          21. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The DPWH shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments through the URS or                            35
36   other electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the BTMS, within thirty (30) days after the end of every              36
37   quarter.                                                                                                                                                                           37
38         Likewise, the DPWH shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                                   38
39         The DPWH shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the House of Representatives, Senate of the Philippines,                39
40   House Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, and regulations.         40
41   The date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                                              41

28   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                                  28
29          1. Priority Research Program. The DOST, in coordination with the CCC, DEPDev, and DILG, shall give priority to research on disaster risk reduction and                         29
30   climate change adaptation and mitigation, including climate impact models and climate-related technologies, to ensure that policy and technology development and                      30
31   application are consistent with local and international development initiatives and are based on science and contribute to resilience-building, promote inclusive and                 31
32   sustainable industrialization, and foster innovation.                                                                                                                                 32
33         The DOST shall also facilitate research on integrated approaches for an efficient shift to a low-carbon development.                                                            33
34         2. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The DOST shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments through the Unified                                34
35   Reporting System (URS) or other electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the Budget and Teasury                         35
36   Management System (BTMS), within thirty (30) days after the end of every quarter.                                                                                                     36
37         Likewise, the DOST shall post said reports on its official website.                                                                                                             37
38         The DOST shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the House of Representatives, Senate of the                                38
39   Philippines, House Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules,                39
40   and regulations. The date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                                40
41         3. Appropriations for Activities or Projects. The amounts appropriated herein shall be used specifically for the following activities or projects in the                        41
42   indicated amounts and conditions:                                                                                                                                                     42

40         1. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The Philippine Nuclear Research Institute (PNRI) shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical 40
41   accomplishments through the URS or other electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the BTMS, within thirty 41
42   (30) days after the end of every quarter.                                                                                                                                                      42
43         Likewise, the PNRI shall post said reports on its official website.                                                                                                                      43
44         The PNRI shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the House of Representatives, Senate of the 44
45   Philippines, House Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, 45
46   and regulations. The date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                                         46

31         1. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The Philippine Textile Research Institute (PTRI) shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical                  31
32   accomplishments through the URS or other electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the BTMS, within thirty     32
33   (30) days after the end of every quarter.                                                                                                                                   33
34         Likewise, the PPTRI shall post said reports on its official website.                                                                                                  34
35         The PTRI shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the House of Representatives, Senate of the                      35
36   Philippines, House Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules,      36
37   and regulations. The date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                      37

49   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                          49
50         1. Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program. The amount of Ninety Nine Billion Seventy Five Million Four Hundred Ninety Eight Thousand Pesos                                 50
51   (P99,075,498,000) appropriated herein for the Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program (4Ps) shall be used to support the poverty reduction and social development strategy        51
52   of the National Government: Provided , That the 4Ps shall cover the eligible beneficiaries under Section 6 of R.A. No. 11310. The said amount shall cover cash grants, rice   52
53   subsidy, Enhanced Support Services Intervention (ESSI) grants, and cash grants for the first 1,000-day health monitoring during pregnancy until the child has turned two      53
54   (2) years old.                                                                                                                                                                54
55         The above-mentioned beneficiaries who are compliant to program conditions shall continue to receive educational and health grants, including the ESSI grants, as        55
56   well as other social protection programs such as, but not limited to, livelihood assistance and health services through PhilHealth.                                           56
57         The DSWD shall provide beneficiaries direct and secured access to cash grants through an authorized government depository bank (AGDB). In case there is no              57
     AGDB in the locality, the DSWD may enter into contracts with rural banks, thrift banks, cooperative banks, and Financial Service Providers (FSPs), including institutions
     engaged in money remittances, registered with the BSP.


                                                                                        161
     162 GENERAL APPROPRIATIONS BILL, FY 2027

           The DSWD shall provide beneficiaries direct and secured access to cash grants through an authorized government depository bank (AGDB). In case there is no
 1   AGDB in the locality, the DSWD may enter into contracts with rural banks, thrift banks, cooperative banks, and Financial Service Providers (FSPs), including institutions          1
 2   engaged in money remittances, registered with the BSP.                                                                                                                             2
 3         2. Quick Response Fund. The amount of One Billion Two Hundred Fifty Million Pesos (P1,250,000,000) appropriated herein for the Quick Response Fund (QRF)                     3
 4   shall serve as a stand-by fund to be used for rehabilitation and relief programs, including the pre-positioning of goods and equipment, in order that the situations and           4
 5   living conditions of people in communities or areas affected by natural or human-induced calamities, epidemics, crises, and catastrophes which occurred in the last quarter        5
 6   of the immediately preceding year and those occurring during the current year may be normalized as quickly as possible. In no case shall the QRF be used for pre-                  6
 7   disaster activities, such as conduct of training, insurance of assets, and public information and education initiatives, or any other purpose not authorized in this provision.    7
 8         Utilization of the QRF shall be subject to DBM-OCD J.C. No. 2025-01 dated April 2, 2025, and such other guidelines as may be issued by the OCD and DBM.                      8
 9         3. Social Pension for Indigent Senior Citizens. The amount of Fifty One Billion Six Hundred Forty Four Million Three Hundred Forty Four Thousand Pesos                       9
10   (P51,644,344,000) appropriated herein for the Social Pension for Indigent Senior Citizens shall be used for the monthly stipend of One Thousand Pesos (P1,000) to                 10
11   augment the daily subsistence and other medical needs of indigent senior citizens, as determined by the DSWD, in accordance with R.A. No. 11916. In no case shall more            11
12   than five percent (5%) of said amount be used for administrative expenses.                                                                                                        12
13         The monthly stipend shall be released to target beneficiaries either in cash, direct remittance through the engagement of a service provider duly accredited by the         13
14   BSP, electronic transfer, or other modes of delivery, whichever is more practical and acceptable to the beneficiary, ensuring its release in the most expeditious and             14
15   efficient manner.                                                                                                                                                                 15
16         4. Trust Receipts from the Proceeds from the Sale of the Welfareville Property. Proceeds derived from the sale of the Welfareville Property, net of                         16
17   lawful expenses, including the cost of relocation of the National Center for Mental Health, Center for Health Development-National Capital Region, and DOJ Correctional           17
18   Institution for Women shall be used to promote the welfare of indigent children, constituted as the Children's Welfare and Development Fund in accordance with R.A. No.           18
19   5260. Said proceeds shall be deposited with the National Treasury in accordance with E.O. No. 338, s. 1996, and shall be recorded as trust receipts.                              19
20         5. PAyapa at MAsaganang PamayaNAn Program. The amount of One Billion Four Hundred Million One Hundred Twelve Thousand Pesos (P1,400,112,000)                                20
21   appropriated herein for the PAyapa at MAsaganang PamayaNAn (PAMANA) Program shall be used exclusively to implement projects in conflict-affected and conflict-                    21
22   vulnerable areas already identified by the OPAPRU.                                                                                                                                22
23         7. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The DSWD shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments through the Unified                            23
24   Reporting System (URS) or other electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the Budget and Treasury                    24
25   Management System (BTMS) , within thirty (30) days after the end of every quarter.                                                                                                25
26         Likewise, the DSWD shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                                  26
27         The DSWD shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the House of Representatives, Senate of the Philippines,               27
28   House Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, and regulations.        28
29   The date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                                             29
30         8. Appropriations for Activities or Projects. The amounts appropriated herein shall be used specifically for the following activities or projects in the                    30
31   indicated amounts and conditions:                                                                                                                                                 31

52         1. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The Council for the Welfare of Children (CWC) shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical 52
53   accomplishments through the URS or other electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the BTMS, within thirty 53
54   (30) days after the end of every quarter.                                                                                                                                                           54
55         Likewise, the CWC shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                                                     55
56        The CWC shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the House of Representatives, Senate of the Philippines, House 56
57   Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, and regulations. The 57
58   date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                                                                   58

 7   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                          7
 8         1. Cash Gifts for Octogenarians, Nonagenarians, and Centenarians. The amount of Three Billion Four Hundred Forty One Million Seven Hundred                              8
 9   Seventy Six Thousand Pesos (P3,441,776,000) appropriated herein under Implementation of the Expanded Centenarians Act pursuant to Republic Act No. 11982 shall be used        9
10   to provide cash gift of Ten Thousand Pesos (P10,000) to Filipino octogenarians and nonagenarians upon reaching the milestone ages of 80, 85, 90, and 95 years old, and       10
11   cash gift of One Hundred Thousand Pesos (P100,000) to Filipino centenarians upon reaching the age of one hundred (100) years old, as determined by the National              11
12   Commission of Senior Citizens (NCSC) based on the Elderly Data Management System, in accordance with R.A. No. 11982. In no case shall more than five percent (5%) of         12
13   said amount be used for administrative expenses.                                                                                                                             13
14        Implementation of this program shall be subject to the guidelines to be issued by the NCSC.                                                                             14
15         2. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The National Commission of Senior Citizens (NCSC) shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical                  15

17   days after the end of every quarter.                                                                                                                                         17

44   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                                          44
45         1. Tourism Development Fund. In addition to the amounts appropriated herein, the amount chargeable against the SAGF reflected in the BESF Table B.15 45
46   under the FY 2027 Proposed Expenditures shall be used for the development, promotion, and marketing of tourism in the country sourced from accreditation, identification 46
47   card, sticker and code fees in accordance with Section 16 of R.A. No. 9593.                                                                                                                   47
48          Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of a budget request and other relevant budgetary requirements, and in accordance with judicious 48
49   fiscal programming by the National Government, as well as applicable laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                            49
50          2. Trust Receipts from Income in Merchandising Operations. The amount of Seventeen Million Seven Hundred Thirty Thousand Pesos (P17,730,000) 50
51   sourced from the net profits of the merchandising operations of the Duty Free Philippines shall be used for tourism related projects and activities in accordance with E.O. 51
53   No. 46, s. 1986. Said amount shall be deposited with the National Treasury and recorded as trust receipts in accordance with E.O. No. 338, s. 1996.                                           53
54         3. Income and Unexpended Funds for Expositions and Similar Events. All income and any unexpended funds in connection with government 54
55   participation in expositions and other similar events shall be deposited with the National Treasury as income of the General Fund in accordance with Section 44, Chapter 5, 55
56   Book VI of E.O. No. 292, s. 1987.                                                                                                                                                             56
57         4. Traditional Art and Craft. The DOT shall include weaving, artisan crafts, and other Schools of Living Traditions in all its promotion, market, and tourism 57
58   development. The DOT shall coordinate with the National Museum of the Philippines and the National Commission for Culture and the Arts for the implementation of this 58
59   provision.                                                                                                                                                                                    59

 8   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                           8
 9           1. Revolving Fund for the Operations of Intramuros Administration. The revolving fund constituted from the revenues generated from operations                          9
10   and commercial transactions of the Intramuros Administration (IA) shall be used for expenses incurred in such commercial operations, including minor repairs of buildings     10
11   and other structures and facilities used directly in its commercial operations, subject to the provisions of P.D. No. 1616, and N.B.C. No. 377 dated August 27, 1984.         11
13         Disbursements or expenditures by the IA in violation of the above requirements shall be void and shall subject the erring officials and employees to disciplinary       13
14   actions in accordance with Section 43, Chapter 5, and Section 80, Chapter 7, Book VI of E.O. No. 292, s. 1987, and to appropriate civil and criminal actions under existing   14
15   laws.                                                                                                                                                                         15
16             2. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The IA shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments through the URS or other                 16
17     electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the BTMS, within thirty (30) days after the end of every quarter.    17
19         Likewise, the IA shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                                19
20         The IA shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the House of Representatives, Senate of the Philippines, House       20
21   Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, and regulations. The      21
22   date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                                             22
23          3. Appropriations for Activities or Projects. The amounts appropriated herein shall be used specifically for the following activities or projects in the               23
24   indicated amounts and conditions:                                                                                                                                             24
