46         1. Micro, Small and Medium Enterprise Development Council Fund. In addition to the amounts appropriated herein, the amount chargeable against the                                                         46
47   Special Account in the General Fund (SAGF) reflected in the Budget of Expenditures and Sources of Financing (BESF) Table B.15 under the FY 2027 Proposed Expenditures                                           47
48   shall be used for the development of the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) sector sourced from ninety percent (90%) of the total penalties collected by the                                           48
49   BSP from lending institutions, constituted into the MSME Development Council Fund in accordance with Section 20 of R.A. No. 9501.                                                                               49
50         Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of a budget request and other relevant budgetary requirements, and in accordance with judicious fiscal                                                50
51   programming by the National Government, as well as applicable laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                                                     51
52         2. Remedies Fund. In addition to the amounts appropriated herein, the amount chargeable against the SAGF reflected in the BESF Table B.15 under the FY 2027                                               52
53   Proposed Expenditures shall be used for the implementation of remedies or safeguard measures for the protection of the domestic industries and producers from increased                                         53
54   imports which cause or threaten to cause serious injury to the local industry, sourced from fifty percent (50%) of the revenues collected from fees, charges, and safeguard                                     54
55   duties, constituted into the Remedies Fund in accordance with Section 34 of R.A. No. 8800.                                                                                                                      55
56         Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of a budget request and other relevant budgetary requirements, and in accordance with judicious fiscal                                                56
57   programming by the National Government, as well as applicable laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                                                     57
58         3. Fees and Other Receipts of the Intellectual Property Office of the Philippines. The income of the Intellectual Property Office of the Philippines                                                      58
     (IPOPHIL) shall be used for its operational requirements, including acquisition of office space and equipment, upgrading of facilities, and human resource development
     sourced from fees, fines, royalties, and other charges in accordance with Section 14.1 of R.A. No. 8293, as amended.

                                                                                                             219
     220 GENERAL APPROPRIATIONS BILL, FY 2027

           3. Fees and Other Receipts of the Intellectual Property Office of the Philippines. The income of the Intellectual Property Office of the Philippines
 1   (IPOPHIL) shall be used for its operational requirements, including acquisition of office space and equipment, upgrading of facilities, and human resource development           1
 2   sourced from fees, fines, royalties, and other charges in accordance with Section 14.1 of R.A. No. 8293, as amended.                                                             2
 3         Disbursements or expenditures by the IPOPHIL in violation of the above requirement shall render any disbursement from said income void and shall subject the               3
 4   erring officials and employees to disciplinary actions in accordance with Section 43, Chapter 5, and Section 80, Chapter 7, Book VI of E.O. No. 292, s. 1987, and to             4
 5   appropriate civil and criminal actions under existing laws.                                                                                                                      5
 6         4. Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Program. The amount of One Hundred Forty Two Million Seven Hundred Forty Seven Thousand Pesos (P142,747,000)                              6
 7   appropriated herein shall be used in support of the Program Beneficiaries Development component of the Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Program.                                    7
 8         5. Implementation of Shared Service Facilities. The amount of Four Hundred Sixty Four Million Nine Hundred Twenty Nine Thousand Pesos (P464,929,000)                       8
 9   appropriated herein for the implementation of the Shared Service Facilities (SSF) shall be used for projects that aim to improve the quality and productivity of MSMEs.          9
10   Its implementation shall be primarily based on priority industry clusters identified by the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) in consultation with key stakeholders.       10
11         Upon the procurement of the machinery and equipment for the SSF, the DTI shall turn over the management thereof to the Cooperators, which shall commit to                 11
12   shoulder maintenance and repair costs upon acceptance thereof. After the period of two (2) years, the DTI may either: (i) transfer ownership of the SSF to the Cooperators      12
13   that demonstrated successful management of the facilities; (ii) extend the usufruct period for another two (2) years if the Cooperator needs additional period to establish     13
14   the successful operation of the SSF; or (iii) transfer the management of the SSF equipment to another Cooperator for failure to secure, operate, properly maintain, or repair   14
15   the SSF equipment upon acceptance.                                                                                                                                              15
16         6. Negosyo Centers. The amount of Four Hundred Seventy Two Million Four Hundred Sixty Eight Thousand Pesos (P472,468,000) appropriated herein shall be used               16
17   for the establishment and management of Negosyo Centers in accordance with Section 3 of R.A. No. 10644. All existing similar activities undertaken by the DTI shall now         17
18   be implemented by the Negosyo Centers.                                                                                                                                          18
19         7. Competitiveness Enhancement Measures Fund. In addition to the amounts appropriated herein, the amount chargeable against the SAGF reflected in                         19
20   the BESF Table B.15 under the FY 2027 Proposed Expenditures shall be utilized for the issuance of grants relative to the implementation of non-agricultural programs,           20
21   projects, and activities that promote the competitiveness of the domestic industries affected by increased imports, sourced from fifty percent (50%) of the revenues            21
22   collected from fees, charges, and safeguard duties, constituted into the Competitiveness Enhancement Measures Fund in accordance with Section 34 of R.A. No. 8800.              22
23         Administration of the fund shall be subject to DA and DTI J.M.C. No. 23-01 dated March 22, 2023, and such other guidelines that may be issued for the purpose.            23
24         Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of a budget request and other relevant budgetary requirements, and in accordance with judicious fiscal                24
25   programming by the National Government, as well as applicable laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                     25
26         8. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The DTI shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments through the Unified                           26
27   Reporting System (URS) or other electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the Budget and Treasury                  27
28   Management System (BTMS), within thirty (30) days after the end of every quarter.                                                                                               28
29         Likewise, the DTI shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                                 29
30         The DTI shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the House of Representatives, Senate of the Philippines, House        30
31   Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, and regulations. The        31
32   date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                                               32

42   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                                     42
43         1. Requirements of the Cooperative Development Authority and Reversion of Balances from Revolving Funds. The amounts appropriated                                                  43
44   herein for the programs, activities, and projects of the Cooperative Development Authority (CDA) shall be used exclusively for regulation of cooperatives and provision of               44
45   technical advisory services. In no case shall said amounts be used for providing credit services in accordance with E.O. No. 138, s. 1999.                                               45
46         Balances of the Cooperative Development Loan Fund, Cooperative Marketing Project Fund, Cooperative Support Fund, and Cooperative Rehabilitation Development Fund,                  46
47   including payments from debtors arising from outstanding loans shall revert to the unappropriated surplus of the General Fund pursuant to Section 45, Chapter 5, Book VI                 47
48   of E.O. No. 292, s. 1987.                                                                                                                                                                48
49         2. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The CDA shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments through the URS or other                               49
50   electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the BTMS, within thirty (30) days after the end of every quarter.                 50
51         Likewise, the CDA shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                                          51
52         The CDA shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the House of Representatives, Senate of the Philippines,                       52
53   House Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, and regulations.               53
54   The date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                                                    54
55         3. Appropriations for Activities or Projects. The amounts appropriated herein shall be used specifically for the following activities or projects in the                           55

54   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                                                       54
55         1. Design Innovation. As the design innovation arm of the government, the Design Center of the Philippines (DCP) shall conduct continuing research and 55
56   development on the different design strengths and assets of the Philippines to create innovative and globally competitive Philippine products, while advocating for 56
57   economic and environmental sustainability. This shall be implemented through: (i) materials research and development; (ii) design research and development; and (iii) 57
58   product development.                                                                                                                                                                                       58
                                                                                                                        DEPARTMENT OF TRADE AND INDUSTRY 253



 1         The DCP shall work with relevant stakeholders from both the design and manufacturing industries who have extensive experience in design, materials, and market            1
 2   exploration in the optimum development of these materials and utilization of the same into innovative and market competitive products.                                          2
 3         2. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The DCP shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments through the URS or other                      3
 4   electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the BTMS, within thirty (30) days after the end of every quarter.        4
 5         Likewise, the DCP shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                                 5
 6         The DCP shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the House of Representatives, Senate of the Philippines,              6
 7   House Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, and regulations.      7
 8   The date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                                           8

45   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                                                   45
46         1. Seat Belt Use Promotions and Child Restraint Systems Installation, Use, and Maintenance Promotions. In addition to the amounts 46
47   appropriated for the Land Transportation Office (LTO), the amount chargeable against the SAGF reflected in the BESF Table B.15 under the FY 2027 Proposed Expenditures 47
48   shall be used for the implementation of the provisions of R.A. No. 8750 and R.A. No. 11229, including the necessary promotion campaigns on the use of seat belt devices 48
49   and the installation, use, and maintenance of child restraint systems sourced from fines imposed by LTO against drivers, operators, vehicle owners, manufacturers, 49
50   assemblers, importers, or distributors for violation of the rules and regulations on the use and installation of seat belts in accordance with Section 13 of R.A. No. 8750, 50
51   and Sections 11 and 14 of R.A. No. 11229.                                                                                                                                                              51
52         Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of a budget request and other relevant budgetary requirements, and in accordance with judicious fiscal 52
53   programming by the National Government, as well as applicable laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                                            53
54         2. Engineering and Administrative Overhead Expenses. The Department of Transportation (DOTr) is authorized to deduct engineering and administrative 54
55   overhead (EAO) expenses for infrastructure projects costing more than Five Million Pesos (P5,000,000) but not to exceed three percent (3%) of the project cost.                                        55




                                                                                                   261
 262 GENERAL APPROPRIATIONS BILL, FY 2027



 1         The authorized EAO expenses shall be limited to: (i) administrative overhead including the hiring of individuals engaged through job orders or contracts of service or        1
 2   such other engagement of personnel without any employer-employee relationship; (ii) pre-construction activities after detailed engineering; (iii) construction project              2
 3   management; (iv) testing and quality control; (v) acquisition, rehabilitation, and repair of related equipment and parts; and (vi) contingencies in relation to pre-construction    3
 4   activities. The EAO expenses shall be treated or booked-up as capitalized expenditures and form part of the project cost.                                                           4
 5         Disbursements or expenditures by the DOTr in violation of the above requirements shall be void and shall subject the erring officials and employees to disciplinary           5
 6   actions in accordance with Section 43, Chapter 5, and Section 80, Chapter 7, Book VI of E.O. No. 292, s. 1987, and to appropriate civil and criminal actions under existing         6
 7   laws.                                                                                                                                                                               7
 8          3. Construction of Various Airports and Navigational Facilities. The amount appropriated herein for the construction of various airports and                                 8
 9   navigational facilities, and acquisition of navigational equipment shall be recorded in the books of accounts of the DOTr and transferred to the Civil Aviation Authority of        9
10   the Philippines as equity contribution of the National Government in accordance with Section 14 of R.A. No. 9497.                                                                  10
11         4. Inventory of Rail System Spare Parts. The DOTr, Philippine National Railways, Light Rail Transit Authority, and all other rail offices and agencies are                   11
12   authorized to maintain and ensure continued availability of adequate spare parts inventory. The purchase of spare parts exceeding the agency's one-year requirement shall          12
13   be subject to the approval of the President of the Philippines, upon the joint recommendation of the Chairperson of the COA and the Secretary of the DOTr.                         13
14         5. Payment of Right-of-Way and Value-Added Tax Obligations. The amount of Two Billion Seven Hundred Eighty Nine Million Six Hundred Sixty Five                               14
15   Thousand Pesos (P2,789,665,000) appropriated herein shall be used exclusively for Right-of-Way expenses authorized under R.A. No. 10752, relative to the implementation of         15
16   infrastructure projects of the DOTr, and value-added tax obligations.                                                                                                              16
17         6. Active Transport Bike Share System and Safe Pathways Program. The amount of Thirty Three Million Eight Hundred Fifty Six Thousand Pesos                                   17
18   (P33,856,000) appropriated herein for the active transport program shall be used to construct, maintain, and improve protected bike lanes and pedestrian walkways,                 18
19   procure bike racks, construct and improve end-of-trip cycling and other support facilities, and upgrade existing pop-up bike lanes to permanent bike lanes in accordance           19
20   with DOTr Department Order (D.0.) No. 2020-014, DPWH D.0. No. 263, s. 2022, and other applicable guidelines promoting and prioritizing active transportation. This shall           20
21   include the planting of urban shade trees consistent with environmental laws.                                                                                                      21
22         The DOTr, in coordination with the DPWH, shall also establish proper public transport stops for the benefit of commuters, and ensure that all projects pertaining to         22
23   the construction, preventive maintenance, rehabilitation, reconstruction, upgrading, off-carriageway improvement, widening and/or paving of primary, secondary, tertiary,          23
24   bypass and diversion roads, and the construction, widening, or replacement of bridges, shall be so designed and implemented so as to allocate, insofar as practicable, at          24
25   least fifty percent (50%) of the road space for public transport, pedestrians, and bicycles/light mobility devices.                                                                25
26         Bike lanes should have smooth pavement, be free of hazards, and with durable physical separation from mixed traffic lanes. Pedestrian walkways and pedestrian                26
27   crossings shall, by default, be at-grade for the inclusion of persons with disability (PWD), senior citizens, pregnant women, children with strollers, tourists with luggage,      27
28   and parents with children. For commuter safety and comfort, pedestrian and cycling infrastructure shall be protected or grade-separated and include shaded walkways and            28
29   urban shade trees wherever feasible.                                                                                                                                               29
30         7. Payment of Arrears of the Land Transportation Office for Information Technology Services. The amount of Eight Hundred Ninety Million                                      30
31   Seven Hundred Seventy Eight Thousand Pesos (P890,778,000) appropriated herein under the General Management and Supervision of the LTO-Central Office shall be used                 31
32   exclusively to cover the payment of arrears of LTO IT services (IT fees) actually rendered by Stradcom Corporation.                                                                32
33          8. Public Transport Modernization Program. The amount of One Hundred Seventy Six Million Eight Hundred Thirty Thousand Pesos (P176,830,000)                                 33
34   appropriated herein for the Public Transport Modernization Program (PTMP) shall be used for the implementation of its nine (9) components, enumerated as follows:                  34
35         (a) Regulatory and institutional support;                                                                                                                                    35
36         (b) Industry consolidation and development;                                                                                                                                  36
37         (c) Local public transport route plan;                                                                                                                                       37
38         (d) Route rationalization;                                                                                                                                                   38
39         (e) Fleet modernization and vehicle useful life, with priority given to the acquisition and deployment of units utilizing low-emission or zero-emission propulsion           39
40              technologies, including battery electric vehicles (BEVs), and units designed or retrofitted to be accessible to PWD as well as the development or support of            40
41              associated depot-based or terminal-based charging facilities necessary for the operation of such electric fleets;                                                       41
42         (f) Financing;                                                                                                                                                               42
43         (g) Stakeholder support mechanism;                                                                                                                                           43
44         (h) Communications; and                                                                                                                                                      44
45         (i) Monitoring and evaluation.                                                                                                                                               45
46         The program shall be implemented in a manner that promotes sustainable, inclusive, and accessible public transportation systems.                                             46
47         The implementation of this provision shall be subject to the guidelines to be issued by the DOTr and other concerned agencies.                                               47
48         9. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The DOTr shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments through the Unified                             48

45   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                                                       45
46         1. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The Civil Aeronautics Board (CAB) shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments 46
47   through the URS or other electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the BTMS, within thirty (30) days after 47
48   the end of every quarter.                                                                                                                                                                                  48
49        Likewise, the CAB shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                                                             49
50        The CAB shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the House of Representatives, Senate of the Philippines, House 50
51   Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, and regulations. The 51
52   date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                                                                          52
53         2. Appropriations for Activities or Projects. The amounts appropriated herein shall be used specifically for the following activities or projects in the 53

28         1. Tonnage Fees. In addition to the amounts appropriated herein, the amount chargeable against the SAGF reflected in the BESF Table B.15 under the FY 2027 28
29   Proposed Expenditures shall be used for the promotion and development of the domestic shipping industry, enhancement of maritime safety, and promotion of the ship 29
30   building and ship repair industry in the country sourced from the annual tonnage fees collected by the Maritime Industry Authority (MARINA) from ship owners or 30
31   operators in accordance with Section 17, Chapter VII of R.A. No. 9295.                                                                                                                                31
32         Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of a budget request and other relevant budgetary requirements, and in accordance with judicious fiscal 32
33   programming by the National Government, as well as applicable laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                                           33
34         2. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The MARINA shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments through the URS or 34
35   other electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the BTMS, within thirty (30) days after the end of every 35
36   quarter.                                                                                                                                                                                              36
37         Likewise, the MARINA shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                                                    37
38         The MARINA shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the House of Representatives, Senate of the Philippines, 38
39   House Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, and regulations. 39
40   The date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                                                                 40

49   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                         49
50        1. Rice Subsidy. The amount of Two Hundred Ninety Five Million Three Hundred Seventy Eight Thousand Pesos (P295,378,000) appropriated herein shall be used 50
51   for the provision of rice subsidy, equivalent to twenty (20) kilos of rice a month, in the form of financial assistance to the uniformed personnel of the Philippine Coast 51
52   Guard (PCG).                                                                                                                                                                 52
53        2. Quick Response Fund. The amount of Seventy Five Million Pesos (P75,000,000) appropriated herein for the Quick Response Fund (QRF) shall serve as a stand- 53
54   by fund to be used for relief and rescue operations, in order that the situation and living conditions of people living in communities or areas stricken by natural or 54
55   human-induced calamities, epidemics, crises, and catastrophes which occurred in the last quarter of the immediately preceding year and those occurring during the current 55
56   year may be normalized as quickly as possible. In no case shall the QRF be used for pre-disaster activities, such as conduct of training, insurance of assets, and public 56
57   information and education initiatives, or for any other purpose not authorized in this provision.                                                                            57

 1   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                             1
 2         1. Higher Education Development Fund. In addition to the amounts appropriated herein, the amount chargeable against the SAGF reflected in the BESF                         2
 3   Table B.15 under the FY 2027 Proposed Expenditures shall be used for the requirements of the Commisssion, sourced from the following in accordance with Section 10 of            3
 4   R.A. No. 7722: shall be used for the requirements of the Commission, sourced from the following in accordance with Section 10 of R.A. No. 7722:                                  4
 5         (i) Travel tax collections of the Tourism Infrastructure and Enterprise Zone Authority;                                                                                    5
 6         (ii) Sales from the lotto operations of PCSO; and                                                                                                                          6
 7         (iii) Collections of the Professional Regulation Commission.                                                                                                               7
 8         Further, the share from the proceeds from any sale, after deducting all expenses related to the sale, of portions of Metro Manila military camps by the Bases              8
 9   Conversion and Development Authority authorized under R.A. No. 7227, as amended, shall also be contributed to the Higher Education Development Fund (HEDF).                      9
10         Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of a budget request and other relevant budgetary requirements, in accordance with judicious fiscal programming        10
11   by the National Government, as well as applicable laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                                 11
12         In the overall programming of the HEDF, the CHED shall ensure that the full requirements of existing scholars are considered to guarantee their continuing funding        12
13   and to prioritize support for courses or programs aligned with global innovation platforms, as well as the priorities of the government in key growth areas in the grant        13
14   of research extension and scholarships, implementation and support to presidential directives, newly promulgated laws on higher education, workforce development and            14
15   priority developments for tourism education and regional education tourism hubs.                                                                                                15
16         The CHED En Banc is authorized to use the HEDF to fund qualified new Tertiary Education Subsidy (TES) grantees, prioritizing those from low income households             16
17   consistent with R.A. No. 10931, who cannot be covered by the current year's appropriations for TES. Likewise, all outstanding deficiencies for SUCs' FHE may be charged         17
18   against their respective internally generated funds. In case of insufficiency thereof, the same shall be charged against the HEDF, subject to accounting and auditing rules     18
19   and regulations.                                                                                                                                                                19
20         2. Rationalization of State Universities and Colleges and Local Universities and Colleges Programs and Course Offerings. The CHED                                         20
21   shall evaluate and rationalize all existing programs and course offerings of the SUCs and local universities and colleges (LUCs), particularly LUCs-beneficiaries of R.A. No.   21
22   10931, prioritizing programs which are oversubscribed or programs identified by the National Government to be priority programs, to ensure that they are directly aligned       22
23   with the SUCs'/LUCs' core mandate, consistent with its supervisory and regulatory functions. The CHED shall also ensure that the number of students admitted by the             23
24   SUCs and LUCs does not exceed the optimal number of students that can be enrolled in each program offered and the number of students that the existing resources and            24
25   capacity of the SUCs and LUCs can carry, based on predetermined parameters to be determined by the CHED. The CHED shall likewise evaluate applications for the                  25
26   opening of new programs and course offerings if they are within the core mandate of the SUCs/LUCs or fall under the fields of the priority programs.                            26
27         3. Universal Access to Quality Tertiary Education. The amount appropriated for Universal Access to Quality Tertiary Education (UAQTE) shall be used to                    27
28   cover the cost of tertiary education for all Filipino students enrolled in SUCs, LUCs, and private higher education institutions (HEIs), subject to prioritization and          28
29   availability of funds, pursuant to R.A. No. 10931 and its IRR:                                                                                                                  29
30         (a) For the Implementation of the TES which shall likewise cover the existing grantee under the Tulong Dunong Program. A list of participating HEIs in the TES            30
31   shall be posted in the Unified Student Financial Assistance System for Tertiary Education (UniFast) website: Provided, That the implementation thereof shall be subject to      31
32   the guidelines issued by the UniFast Board.                                                                                                                                     32
33         The UniFast Board shall administer the amount appropriate herein: Provided, That the same shall be used to cover tuition and other school fees based on 2024 rates:       33
34   Provided, further, That in no case shall more than one and a half percent (1.5%) of the amount for TES and student loan program be used for administrative cost.                34
35         (b) For the implementation of the Free Higher Education (FHE), as determined by the respectivegovernng boards of LUCs based on the actual number of enrollees for         35
36   each academic year, shall be immediately released to such LUCs: Provided, That such determination of the actiual number of enrollees and the amount to be reimbursed            36
37   shall be subject to the validation of CHED.                                                                                                                                     37
38         The CHED shall ensure that the enrollment capacity is strictly observed by the LUCs in the implementation of this Program. In the case of SUCs, the FHE Program of        38
39   the UAQTE shall be lodged in their respective budgets.                                                                                                                          39
40        4. Bagong Pilipinas Merit Scholarship Program. The amount of One Billion Five Hundred Eighty Nine Million Seven Hundred Thirty Seven Thousand Pesos                        40
41   (P1,589,737,000) appropriated herein under the Provision of Assistance and Incentives, Scholarships and Grants through Student Financial Assistance Programs shall be used      41
42   for the implementation of the Bagong Pilipinas Merit Scholarship Program as educational support for ongoing and incoming college students. The scholarship shall be given       42
43   to those coming from lower middle income households and below who graduated with highest honors or equivalent academic distinction in Senior High Schools and with              43
44   successful admission to priority Philippine HEIs identified by CHED.                                                                                                            44
45         The implementation of the Program shall be subject to guidelines to be issued jointly by the CHED, TESDA, and DepEd, in coordination with relevant government             45
46   agencies.                                                                                                                                                                       46
47         5. Scholarship Grants for Dependents of Sugar Industry Workers. The amount of Sixty Five Million One Hundred Forty Seven Thousand Pesos                                   47
48   (P65,147,000) under Provision of Assistance and Incentives, Scholarships and Grants through Student Financial Assistance Programs shall be used as scholarship grants for       48
49   dependents of sugar industry workers and small farmers pursuant to R.A. No. 10659.                                                                                              49
50          6. Agriculture and Fisheries Modernization Program. The amount of Fifteen Million Three Hundred Ninety Seven Thousand Pesos (P15,397,000)                                50
51   appropriated herein under the Development of Standards of Excellence for Higher Education Programs and Institutions shall be used in support of the programs and                51
52   projects under the Agriculture and Fisheries Modernization Program.                                                                                                             52

55   quarter.                                                                                                                                                                        55

 9   Section 20 of R.A. No. 7356. In no case shall more than twenty percent (20%) of said amount be used for Personnel Services.                                                  9
10         Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of a budget request, and other relevant budgetary requirements, in accordance with judicious fiscal programming   10
11   by the National Government, as well as applicable laws, rules and regulations.                                                                                              11
12         2. Revolving Fund for Fabrication of Cultural Items and Printing Publications. The revolving fund in the amount of Five Hundred Thousand                              12
13   Pesos (P500,000) constituted from the sale of cultural items and publications shall be used to cover the fabrication of cultural items and printing of publications. The    13
14   income collected in excess of said amount shall be deposited with the National Treasury as income of the General Fund pursuant to Section 22 of R.A. No. 7356.              14
15         Disbursements or expenditures by the NCCA in violation of the above requirements shall be void and shall subject the erring officials and employees to disciplinary   15
16   actions in accordance with Section 43, Chapter 5 and Section 80, Chapter 7, Book VI of E.O. No. 292 s. 1987, and to appropriate civil and criminal actions under existing   16
17   laws.                                                                                                                                                                       17
18          3. Fees Collected from Registrations, Licenses, Inspections, Certifications, Authorizations, and Permits of Dealers of Cultural                                      18
19   Property. The amounts collected by the NCCA from fees for registration, licenses, inspections, certifications, authorizations, and permits issued shall be deposited and    19
20   maintained in a separate account, to be used for its operating expenses pursuant to R.A. No. 10066, as amended.                                                             20
21         The implementation of this provision shall be in accordance with the guidelines to be issued jointly by DBM and NCCA.                                                 21
22         Disbursements or expenditures by the NCCA in violation of the above requirements shall render any disbursements from said income void and shall subject the erring    22
23   officials and employees to disciplinary actions in accordance with Section 43, Chapter 5 and Section 80, Chapter 7, Book VI of E.O. No. 292, and to appropriate civil and   23
24   criminal actions under existing laws.                                                                                                                                       24
25         4. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The NCCA shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments through the URS or other                 25
26   electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the BTMS, within thirty (30) days after the end of every quarter.    26
27         Likewise, the NCCA shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                            27

29   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                                                        29
30         1. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The National Intelligence Coordinating Agency (NICA) shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and 30
31   physical accomplishments through the URS or other electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the BTMS, 31
32   within thirty (30) days after the end of every quarter.                                                                                                                                                     32
33         Likewise, the NICA shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                                                            33
34         The NICA shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the House of Representatives, Senate of the 34
35   Philippines, House Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, 35
36   and regulations. The date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                                                      36

18        In no case shall the foregoing amounts be used for any other purpose.                                                                                                     18

20         (a) Eighty Eight Million Nine Hundred Forty Six Thousand Pesos (P88,946,000) for General Management and Supervision;                                                     20
21         (b) Ninety Three Million Six Hundred Forty Nine Thousand Pesos (P93,649,000) for Policy and Program Formulation and Amateur Sports Development and Promotion;            21
22             and                                                                                                                                                                  22
23         (c) Sixty Three Million Four Hundred Eighty Four Thousand Pesos (P63,484,000) for National Sport for All-Grassroot Centerpiece Program.                                  23
24        In no case shall said amounts be used as assistance to national sports associations and entities, civil service organizations, and individuals.                           24
25        3. Basic and Meal Allowances of Athletes. The PSC shall ensure that all qualified national athletes are uniformly granted basic and meal allowances which                 25
26   should be charged against the NSDF. For this purpose, regular national athletes shall receive the monthly meal allowance of Five Thousand Pesos (P5,000), in addition to       26
27   the basic training allowance which shall be based on their classification, as follows:                                                                                         27
28         (a) Class A - Thirty Thousand Pesos (P30,000);                                                                                                                           28
29         (b) Class B - Twenty Seven Thousand Pesos (P27,000);                                                                                                                     29
30         (c) Class C - (i) Silver Medalist - Twenty Four Thousand Pesos (P24,000); and (ii) Bronze Medalist - Twenty One Thousand Pesos (P21,000);                                30
31         (d) Class C (Team Sports) - Medalist - Seventeen Thousand Pesos (P17,000);                                                                                               31
32         (e) Training Pool A - Seventeen Thousand Pesos (P17,000);                                                                                                                32
33         (f) Training Pool B - (i) Former Medalist (Team Sports/Event) - Fifteen Thousand Pesos (P15,000); and (ii) New Entries/Alternates/Sparring Partners - Ten                33
34             Thousand Two Hundred Pesos (P10,200).                                                                                                                                34
35         For athletes who garnered medals in the Olympics and World Championship shall be allowed the following allowance scheme under the Priority Athletes Program of           35
36         the Commission, with the following rates:                                                                                                                                36
37         (a) Platinum - Fifty Thousand Pesos (P50,000);                                                                                                                           37
38         (b) Priority A - Forty Three Thousand Pesos (P43,000);                                                                                                                   38
39         (c) Priority B - Thirty Six Thousand Pesos (P36,000); and                                                                                                                39
40         (d) Priority C - Thirty Three Thousand Pesos (P33,000).                                                                                                                  40
41        The scheme shall cover athletes who are qualified and endorsed by their respective National Sports Associations to be part of the said program. Implementation of         41
42   this provision shall be in accordance with PSC Resolution No. 924-2024 dated September 26, 2024, PSC Board Resolution No. 692-2025 dated July 8, 2025, and such other          42
43   guidelines that may be issued for the purpose.                                                                                                                                 43
44                                                                                                                                                                                  44

36   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                                                                  36
37         1. Judiciary Trust Fund. In addition to the amounts appropriated herein, all legal fees collected by the Judiciary under Rule 141 of the Rules of Court, as                                                     37
38   amended, including interests and income that may be derived therefrom and as may be determined by the Supreme Court of the Philippines, shall be deposited in the                                                     38
39   Judiciary Trust Fund established under Republic Act No. 12233 from which funds needed for its operations shall be drawn. The said trust fund shall be administered by                                                 39
40   the Chief Justice in accordance with the said law and the implementing rules and regulations promulgated by the Supreme Court.                                                                                        40
41        Income and disbursements of the Judiciary Trust Fund shall be subject to post-audit by the Commission on Audit under pertinent laws, rules, and regulations.                                                     41
42         2. Administration of Appropriations. The appropriations provided herein for the Supreme Court of the Philippines and the Lower Courts shall be                                                                  42
43   administered by the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court, subject to the provisions of P.D. No. 985, as amended, E.O. No. 292, s. 1987, and other budgeting, accounting, and                                            43
44   auditing rules and regulations.                                                                                                                                                                                       44
45        3. Organizational Structure. Notwithstanding any provision of law to the contrary and within the limits of appropriations in this Act, the Chief Justice of the                                                  45
46   Supreme Court as Head of the Judiciary and as Chairperson of the Presidential Electoral Tribunal is hereby authorized to:                                                                                             46
47         (a) formulate and implement the organizational structure of the Judiciary and the Presidential Electoral Tribunal;                                                                                              47
48         (b) fix and determine the salaries, allowances and other benefits of the personnel of the Judiciary and the Presidential Electoral Tribunal in accordance with the                                              48
49             rates and levels authorized under R.A. No. 6758, as amended, and R.A. No. 6686, as amended; and                                                                                                             49
50         (c) create new positions, transfer an item, or make other adjustments in the Personnel Services Itemization, whenever public interest so requires.                                                              50
51        Implementation of the foregoing shall be subject to: (i) compliance with organization, staffing, and position classification and compensation standards of the DBM; (ii)                                         51
52   scrap and build policy; and (iii) submission to DBM of a resolution stating the changes in the organization and staffing in accordance with the foregoing standards and                                               52
53   policy for proper documentation.                                                                                                                                                                                      53
54        The officials and employees whose positions are affected by a reorganization shall be granted retirement benefits or separation pay in accordance with existing laws,                                            54
55   which shall be payable from any unexpended balance of, or savings in the appropriations of the Judiciary and the Presidential Electoral Tribunal.                                                                     55

 1          4. Use of Savings. The Chief Justice of the Supreme Court is authorized to use savings to augment actual deficiencies in accordance with Section 25(5), Article           1
 2    VI of the Constitution and the General Provisions of this Act.                                                                                                                  2
 3          5. Non-Recurring Expenses. All non-recurring items of appropriations authorized herein such as, but not limited to, foreign-assisted projects and locally-funded          3
 4    projects, shall not form part of the Judiciary's appropriations that may not be reduced by Congress under Section 3, Article VIII of the Constitution. The Supreme Court en     4
 5    banc, through a resolution, shall affirm the items of appropriation in the Judiciary's budget that are non-recurring, as defined above, and which shall not be considered in    5
 6    the total appropriations that may not be reduced.                                                                                                                               6
 7          6. Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses of the Lower Courts. The amount of Three Billion Nine Hundred Fifty Nine Million Seven Hundred                                7
 8    Eighty Three Thousand Pesos (P3,959,783,000) appropriated herein shall be used for the MOOE of the lower courts: Provided , That the Supreme Court shall continuously           8
 9    ensure the equitable allocation and prompt release of the MOOE allocations to the lower courts for the effcient administration of justice.                                      9
10          To facilitate the utilization of said MOOE allocation and ensure that the requirements of lower courts are readily available and provided, the Procurement Service       10
11    (PS), through its Regional Depots, shall provide an easy access facility for lower courts to source all their MOOE requirements from the PS.                                   11
12          The Chief Justice of the Supreme Court and the Court's web administrator or his/her equivalent shall be responsible for ensuring that the utilization of funds           12
13    allocated for each lower court is posted on the Supreme Court's website.                                                                                                       13
14          7. Expenses for Official Travel. The Chief Justice of the Supreme Court may authorize the reimbursement of actual and reasonable expenses incurred during                14
15    official travel in carrying out the supervisory functions of the Supreme Court over the lower courts, subject to the limits prescribed under E.O. No. 77, s. 2019 and duly     15
16    supported by receipts pursuant to accounting and auditing rules and regulations.                                                                                               16
17          8. Payment of Adjusted Pension. The amounts appropriated herein for payment of pensions to retired Justices and Judges shall be adjusted at the rates                    17
18    authorized under Section 3-A of R.A. No. 910, as amended, and implemented by SC A.M. No. 91-8-225-C.A.                                                                         18
19          9. Public-Private Partnership for Major Infrastructure Projects and/or Procurements. The Supreme Court may consider entering into Public-                                19
20    Private Partnership arrangements with respect to its major infrastructure projects and/or procurements, as may be appropriate or allowed by law, in order to facilitate        20
21    the attainment of its objectives for a more efficient, innovative and accessible judicial system.                                                                              21
22          10. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The Supreme Court shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments, within thirty                    22
23    (30) days after the end of every quarter, through the following:                                                                                                               23
24          (a) Unified Reporting System (URS) or other electronic means for reports not covered by the URS until such time that all agencies have fully migrated to the Budget      24
25               and Treasury Management System (BTMS); and                                                                                                                          25
26          (b) Supreme Court's website.                                                                                                                                             26
27          The Supreme Court shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the DBM, House of Representatives, Senate of the           27
28    Philippines, House Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, and     28
29    regulations. The date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                             29

54          1. Administration of Appropriations. The appropriations provided herein for the Sandiganbayan shall be administered by the Presiding Justice of the 54
55    Sandiganbayan, subject to the provisions of P.D. No. 985, as amended, E.O. No. 292, s. 1987, and other budgeting, accounting, and auditing rules, and regulations.                                    55
                                                                                                                                                       THE JUDICIARY 443



 1         2. Non-Recurring Expenses. All non-recurring items of appropriations authorized herein such as, but not limited to, foreign-assisted projects and locally-              1
 2   funded projects, shall not form part of the Sandiganbayan's appropriations that may not be reduced by Congress under Section 3, Article VIII of the Constitution. The         2
 3   Supreme Court en banc, through a resolution, shall affirm the items of appropriation in the Judiciary's budget that are non-recurring, as defined above, and which shall      3
 4   not be considered in the total appropriations that may not be reduced.                                                                                                        4
 5         3. Payment of Adjusted Pension. The amounts appropriated herein for payment of pensions to retired Justices shall be adjusted at the rates authorized under             5
 6   Section 3-A of R.A. No. 910, as amended, and implemented by SC A.M. No. 91-8-225-C.A.                                                                                         6
 7         4. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The Sandiganbayan shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments, within thirty                    7
 8   (30) days after the end of every quarter, through the following:                                                                                                              8
 9         (a) URS or other electronic means for reports not covered by the URS until such time that all agencies have fully migrated to the BTMS; and                             9
10         (b) Sandiganbayan's website.                                                                                                                                           10
11         The Sandiganbayan shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the DBM, House of Representatives, Senate of the         11
12   Philippines, House Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, and   12
13   regulations. The date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                           13

43   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                                                                     43
44         1. Organizational Structure. Notwithstanding any provision of law to the contrary and within the limits of appropriations in this Act, the Chairperson of the                                                      44
45   Civil Service Commission (CSC) is hereby authorized to:                                                                                                                                                                  45
46         (a) formulate and implement the CSC's organizational structure;                                                                                                                                                    46
47         (b) fix and determine the salaries, allowances, and other benefits of personnel of the CSC in accordance with the rates and levels authorized under R.A. No. 6758, as                                              47
48              amended, and R.A. No. 6686, as amended; and                                                                                                                                                                   48
49         (c) create new positions, transfer an item, or make other adjustments in the Personnel Services Itemization, whenever public interest so requires.                                                                 49
50         Implementation of the foregoing shall be subject to: (i) compliance with organization, staffing, and position classification and compensation standards of the DBM; (ii)                                           50
51   scrap and build policy; and (iii) submission to DBM of a resolution stating the changes in the organization and staffing in accordance with the foregoing standards and                                                  51
52   policy for proper documentation.                                                                                                                                                                                         52
53         The officials and employees whose positions are affected by a reorganization shall be granted retirement benefits or separation pay in accordance with existing laws,                                              53
54   which shall be payable from any unexpended balance of, or savings in the appropriations of the CSC.                                                                                                                      54
55         2. Use of Savings. The Chairperson of CSC is hereby authorized to use savings to augment actual deficiencies in its appropriations in accordance with Section                                                      55
56   25(5), Article VI of the Constitution and the General Provisions of this Act.                                                                                                                                            56

30   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                                    30
31         1. Organizational Structure. Notwithstanding any provision of law to the contrary and within the limits of appropriations in this Act, the Chairperson of the                     31
32   Commission on Audit (COA) is hereby authorized to:                                                                                                                                      32
33         (a) formulate and implement the COA's organizational structure;                                                                                                                   33
34         (b) fix and determine the salaries, allowances and other benefits of the COA personnel in accordance with the rates and levels authorized under R.A. No. 6758, as                 34
35              amended, and R.A. No. 6686, as amended; and                                                                                                                                  35
36         (c) create new positions, transfer an item, or make other adjustments in the Personnel Services Itemization, whenever public interest so requires.                                36
37         Implementation of the foregoing shall be subject to: (i) compliance with organization, staffing, and position classification and compensation standards of the DBM; (ii)          37
38   scrap and build policy; and (iii) submission to DBM of a resolution stating the changes in the organization and staffing in accordance with the foregoing standards and                 38
39   policy for proper documentation.                                                                                                                                                        39
40         The officials and employees whose positions are affected by a reorganization shall be granted retirement benefits or separation pay in accordance with existing laws,             40
41   which shall be payable from any unexpended balance of, or savings in the appropriations of the COA.                                                                                     41
42         2. Use of Savings. The Chairperson of COA is hereby authorized to use savings to augment actual deficiencies in accordance with Section 25(5), Article VI of the                  42
43   Constitution and the General Provisions of this Act.                                                                                                                                    43
44         3. Appropriations for Auditing Services to Local Government Units (LGUs). The amounts appropriated herein include the requirements for the audit                                  44
45   of LGU accounts. The cost of auditing services rendered to LGUs shall be deducted from the national tax collections and recorded in the National Treasury as income of                  45
46   the General Fund in accordance with Section 24(3) of P.D. No. 1445.                                                                                                                     46
47         4. Assessments from Auditing Services to Government-Owned or-Controlled Corporations (GOCCs). The COA shall assess GOCCs for the                                                  47
48   cost of audit services rendered in accordance with the provisions of E.O. No. 271, s. 1987. Proceeds from such assessments, including receipts derived from other                       48
49   sources authorized under P.D. No. 1445 shall be deposited with the National Treasury as income of the General Fund in accordance with Section 44, Chapter 5, Book VI                    49
50   of E.O. No. 292, s. 1987.                                                                                                                                                               50
51         5. Submission of Annual Reports of the Commission on Audit. The COA shall submit within one hundred twenty (120) days after the end of every                                      51
52   fiscal year, the Annual Report on Appropriations, Allotments, Obligations, and Disbursements (ARAAOD) of National Government Agencies (NGAs) and Government                             52
53   Corporations (GCs) receiving subsidies from the national government and maintaining Special Accounts in the General Fund (SAGFs), which includes the approved budget,                   53
54   utilizations, and disbursements for off-budgetary funds and trust receipts, to the Congress and the President of the Philippines.                                                       54
55         Furthermore, the COA shall submit the Annual Financial Reports (AFRs) for national government, local government, and GCs, including recommended measures necessary                55
56   to improve their effectiveness and efficiency, on or before September 30 of each fiscal year.                                                                                           56




                                                                                               469

34   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                                                  34
35         1. Organizational Structure. Notwithstanding any provision of law to the contrary and within the limits of appropriations in this Act, the Chairperson of the 35
36   Commission on Elections (COMELEC) is hereby authorized to:                                                                                                                                            36
37         (a) formulate and implement the COMELEC's organizational structure;                                                                                                                             37
38         (b) fix and determine the salaries, allowances, and other benefits of personnel of the COMELEC in accordance with the rates and levels authorized under R.A. No. 38
39              6758, as amended, and R.A. No. 6686, as amended; and                                                                                                                                       39
40         (c) create new positions, transfer an item, or make other adjustments in the Personnel Services Itemization, whenever public interest so requires.                                              40
41         Implementation of the foregoing shall be subject to: (i) compliance with organization, staffing and position classification and compensation standards of the DBM; (ii) 41
42   scrap and build policy; and (iii) submission to DBM of a resolution stating the changes in the organization and staffing in accordance with the foregoing standards and 42
43   policy for proper documentation.                                                                                                                                                                      43
44         The officials and employees whose positions are affected by a reorganization shall be granted retirement benefits or separation pay in accordance with existing laws, 44
45   which shall be payable from any unexpended balance of, or savings in the appropriations of the COMELEC.                                                                                               45
46         2. Use of Savings. The Chairperson of COMELEC is authorized to use savings to augment actual deficiencies in accordance with Section 25(5), Article VI of the 46
47   Constitution and the General Provisions of this Act.                                                                                                                                                  47
48         3. Special Audit of Printing Expenditures. The amounts appropriated herein for registration, plebiscite, referendum and election related expenditures, 48
49   including those incurred for printing of ballots and similar paraphernalia shall be used exclusively for said purposes. A special audit on all expenditures incurred for 49
50   printing jobs and materials used during said activities shall be undertaken by the COA within six (6) months from the conduct thereof.                                                                50
51         The COA shall submit to the DBM, the Speaker of the House of Representatives, and the President of the Senate of the Philippines, copies of the COA Special Audit 51
52   report within one (1) month after the said audit.                                                                                                                                                     52
53         4. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The COMELEC shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments through the Unified 53
54   Reporting System (URS) or other electronic means for reports not coveredby the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the Budget and Treasury 54
55   Management System (BTMS), within thirty (30) days after the end of every quarter.                                                                                                                     55
56         Likewise, the COMELEC shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                                                   56

40   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                                          40
41         1. Organizational Structure. Notwithstanding any provision of law to the contrary and within the limits of appropriations in this Act, the Ombudsman is 41
42   hereby authorized to:                                                                                                                                                                         42
43         (a) formulate and implement the Office of the Ombudsman's organizational structure;                                                                                                     43
44         (b) fix and determine the salaries, allowances, and other benefits of personnel of the Office of the Ombudsman in accordance with the rates and levels authorized 44
45              under R.A. No. 6758, as amended, and R.A. No. 6686, as amended; and                                                                                                                45
46         (c) create new positions, transfer an item, or make other adjustments in the Personnel Services Itemization, whenever public interest so requires.                                      46
47         Implementation of the foregoing shall be subject to: (i) compliance with organization, staffing, and position classification and compensation standards of the DBM; (ii) 47
48   scrap and build policy; and (iii) submission to DBM of a resolution stating the changes in the organization and staffing in accordance with the foregoing standards and 48
49   policy for proper documentation.                                                                                                                                                              49
50         The officials and employees whose positions are affected by a reorganization shall be granted retirement benefits or separation pay in accordance with existing laws, 50
51   which shall be payable from any unexpended balance of, or savings in the appropriations of the Office of the Ombudsman.                                                                       51
52         2. Non-Recurring Expenses. All non-recurring appropriations authorized herein such as, but not limited to, foreign-assisted projects and locally-funded projects, 52
53   shall not form part of the Office of the Ombudsman's appropriations that may not be reduced by Congress under Section 38 of R.A. No. 6770.                                                    53
54         3. Reporting and Posting Requirements. The Office of the Ombudsman shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments through 54
55   the Unified Reporting System (URS) or other electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the Budget and 55
56   Treasury Management System (BTMS), within thirty (30) days after the end of every quarter.                                                                                                    56

39         1. Subsidy to the National Dairy Authority. The amount of Two Billion One Hundred Ninety Four Million Seven Hundred Fifty Eight Thousand Pesos                                39
40   (P2,194,758,000) appropriated herein under the subsidy to the National Dairy Authority (NDA) shall be used for the implementation of the Dairy Industry Development                 40
