42         The NDA shall ensure that the implementation of the foregoing shall directly benefit farmers registered under the Registry System for Basic Sectors in Agriculture            42
43   (RSBSA), with priority given to the provinces or regions where the absolute number of poor farmers and the incidence of poverty are high as identified in the latest                43
44   official poverty statistics of the PSA.                                                                                                                                             44
45         2. Milk Feeding Component of the Department of Education's School-Based Feeding Program. The amount of Two Billion Thirty Seven Million                                       45
46   Three Hundred Ninety Five Thousand Pesos (P2,037,395,000) appropriated herein for the milk feeding component of the Department of Education's School-Based Feeding                  46
47   Program shall be used exclusively as mandated by R.A. No. 11037, specifically for the (i) procurement of fresh milk and (ii) packaging, storage, cold-chain logistics, and          47
48   distribution to designated drop-off schools. The procurement of local milk and milk-based products shall strictly comply with the provisions of R.A. No. 11037 and R.A. No.         48
49   12009, and all applicable guidelines.                                                                                                                                               49
50         The NDA shall coordinate with DepEd, Philippine Carabao Center (PCC), local dairy cooperatives, and other appropriate agencies to ensure quality, safety, and stable          50
51   supply and efficient and timely delivery of milk to all eligible designated drop-off schools.                                                                                       51
52         The NDA shall maintain a separate accounting and reporting of all funds utilized for this program, including any revenue generated and savings realized from its              52
53   implementation.                                                                                                                                                                     53
54         The NDA and PCC shall jointly submit to the DepEd, the Senate Committee on Finance, and the House Committee on Appropriations an implementation and fund                      54
55   utilization report within thirty (30) days from the start of the milk feeding component, and every quarter thereafter, including key implementation metrics and financial           55
56   status.                                                                                                                                                                             56

17   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                                   17
18        1. Subsidy to the National Electrification Administration. The amount of Five Billion Six Hundred Thirty Five Million Seven Hundred Sixty Thousand                                18
19   Pesos (P5,635,760,000) appropriated herein under the subsidy to NEA shall be used for the implementation of the National Rural Electrification Program.                                19
20        The NEA is authorized to deduct engineering and administrative overhead (EAO) expenses not exceeding three percent (3%) of the project cost. The authorized EAO                   20
21   expenses shall be limited to: (i) pre-construction activities after detailed engineering; (ii) construction project management; (iii) testing and quality control; (iv) acquisition,   21
22   rehabilitation, and repair of related equipment and parts; and (v) contingencies in relation to pre-construction activities. The EAO expenses shall be treated or booked-up            22
23   as capitalized expenditures and form part of the project cost.                                                                                                                         23
24        In the implementation of the Strategized Rural Electrification and Operational Reliability for Electric Cooperatives Projects, the NEA shall observe the following:               24
25        (a) Prioritize sitios where the absolute number of indigents and the incidence of poverty are high as identified in the latest official poverty statistics of the PSA as          25
26              well as those with the high probability of being energized;                                                                                                                 26
27        (b) Loans outlay to electric cooperatives shall be recorded as equity contribution of the National Government to NEA when its authorized capitalization is increased              27
28              by law, while grants thereto remain to be treated as subsidy;                                                                                                               28
29        (c) Release funds only to electric cooperatives which have fully liquidated funds from previous years' electrification projects: Provided, That non-delinquent electric           29
30              cooperatives with ongoing projects that are not yet due for liquidation are entitled to a release of subsidy upon a new MOA with NEA subject to COA Circular                30
31              No. 2012-001: Provided, further, That electric cooperatives must completely liquidate the subsidy within three (3) months from the issuance of Certificate of               31
32              Final Inspection and Acceptance (CFIA): Provided, finally, That in cases where the electric cooperatives are not qualified to implement projects for barangay and           32
33              sitio electrification, the NEA is authorized to download the subsidy to qualified electric cooperatives in strategically located neighboring areas consistent with          33
34              the National Rural Electrification Program. The electric cooperative that implements the program shall liquidate the subsidy within three (3) months from the               34
35              issuance of CFIA. This provision shall not apply to NEA releases for calamity grants and subsidies; and                                                                     35
36        (d) Prohibition on the use of subsidy for the payment of salaries, allowances, incentives, separation, or retirement benefits.                                                    36
37        2. Electric Cooperatives Emergency and Resiliency Fund. The amount of Two Hundred Million Pesos (P200,000,000) appropriated herein shall be used                                  37
38   exclusively for the Electric Cooperatives Emergency and Resiliency Fund pursuant to R.A. No. 11039.                                                                                    38
39        3. Equity from National Government. The amount of Eight Hundred Fifty Million Pesos (P850,000,000) shall be used as loans outlay to electric cooperatives                         39
40   and shall be recorded as equity contribution of the National Government to NEA.                                                                                                        40
41         4. Special Provisions Applicable to All Government-Owned or -Controlled Corporations. In addition to the foregoing special provisions, the                                       41

31          1. Subsidy for the National Health Insurance Program. The amount of Fifty Five Billion Four Hundred Sixteen Million Two Hundred Fifteen Thousand 31
32   Pesos (P55,416,215,000) appropriated herein under the subsidy for the National Health Insurance Program (NHIP) shall be used for the health insurance premiums of 32
33   indirect contributors as defined under R.A. No. 11223. Accordingly, indirect contributors refer to all others not included as direct contributors, as well as their qualified 33
34   dependents, whose premium shall be subsidized by the National Government, including those who are subsidized as a result of special laws, such as, but not limited to, 34
35   the following: (i) indigents as identified by the DSWD or the PSA through the Community-Based Monitoring System; (ii) senior citizens pursuant to R.A. No. 10645; (iii) 35
36   persons with disability registered in the Philippine Registry for Persons with Disability pursuant to R.A. No. 11228 and its IRR; (iv) solo parents as identified by the 36
37   Social Welfare Office of the LGU pursuant to R.A. No. 11861 and its IRR; and (v) financially-incapable Point-of-Service patients as identified by the social worker of 37
38   health care institutions or LGUs: Provided, That in no case shall the subsidy be used for the payment of Personnel Services.                                                                          38
39         Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of the following: (i) Board-approved Corporate Operating Budget which shall be compliant with existing 39
40   organization, staffing, and position classification, and compensation standards; and (ii) billing indicating the names of enrollees approved by the PhilHealth Board. The DOH 40
41   and PhilHealth shall ensure the conduct of special audit on the implementation of the NHIP.                                                                                                           41
42          PhilHealth shall comply with budget accountability requirements and ensure judicious utilization of its budget.                                                                                42
43          The administrative cost of implementing the NHIP shall not exceed seven and one half percent (7.5%) of the actual total premium collected from direct and indirect 43
44   contributory members during the immediately preceding year in accordance with Section 12 of R.A. No. 11223.                                                                                           44
45         2. Benefit Package Improvement Under Universal Health Care Law. The amount of Nineteen Billion Pesos (P19,000,000,000) appropriated herein for the 45
46   benefit package improvement under the Universal Health Care Law shall be used for the increase in benefit packages including, but not limited to, the expansion of 46
47   dialysis coverage, mental health outpatient coverage, improvement of Z-Benefit packages, severe acute malnutrition, all case rate, rationalization of selected medical and 47
48   surgical procedures; Zero Balance Billing (ZBB) Program for DOH and LGU hospitals nationwide; introduction and scale-up of benefit packages for catastrophic and high-cost 48
49   conditions, including those under the Z-Benefit packages and related packages; expansion of coverages for outpatient and primary care services through the Yaman ng 49
50   Kalusugan Program (YAKAP), including the Guaranteed Accessible Medications for Outpatient Treatment (GAMOT) Program; and the implementation of the comprehensive 50
51   outpatient benefit package, including free consultation fees, laboratory tests, other diagnostic services, outpatient drug benefit, and emergency medical services.                                   51
52         3. PAyapa at MAsaganang PamayaNAn Program. The amount of Thirty Two Million Two Hundred Ninety Thousand Pesos (P32,290,000) appropriated 52

13         4. Subsidy for National Irrigation Systems and Communal Irrigation Systems. The amount of Fourteen Billion Forty Three Million Five Hundred                               13
14   Fifty Two Thousand Pesos (P14,043,552,000) appropriated herein shall be used for expenses directly related to the implementation of National Irrigation Systems and             14
15   Communal Irrigation Systems. The NIA shall ensure that the master plan for irrigation projects gives priority to key production areas in major rice producing provinces         15
16   and irrigation projects are undertaken by qualified Irrigators Associations consistent with the standard specifications set by DPWH, taking into account climate risk           16
17   information, and using coconut bio-engineering solutions and high-density polyethylene pipes.                                                                                   17
18         In no case shall said amount be used for administrative expenses or for the payment of Personnel Services or MOOE requirements.                                           18
19         5. Subsidy for Small Irrigation Projects. The amount of Two Hundred Million Pesos (P200,000,000) appropriated herein under the Special Irrigation Sub-                    19
20   program for Small Irrigation Projects (SIPs) shall be used for the implementation of irrigation projects that will generate new service areas within a year and the             20
21   construction of dams or intake structures and canals, and drainage structures and facilities.                                                                                   21
22         Upon completion of the construction of the SIPs, NIA may turn over its operation and maintenance to capable Irrigators Association concerned, which shall commit to       22
23   shoulder the costs thereof. Implementation of this project shall be subject to the guidelines issued by NIA.                                                                    23
24         6. Subsidy for Quick Response Fund. The amount of One Billion Seven Hundred Million Pesos (P1,700,000,000) appropriated herein for the Quick Response                     24
25   Fund (QRF) shall serve as a stand-by fund to be used for reconstruction and rehabilitation programs, activities or projects in order that the situation and living conditions   25
26   of people in communities or areas stricken by calamities, epidemics, crises, and catastrophes, which occurred in the last quarter of the immediately preceding year and         26
27   those occurring during the current year may be normalized as quickly as possible. In no case shall the QRF be used for pre-disaster activities, such as conduct of              27
28   training, insurance of assets, and public information and education initiatives, or any other purpose not authorized in this provision.                                         28
29         Utilization of the QRF shall be subject to DBM-OCD J.C. No. 2025-01 dated April 2, 2025, and such other guidelines as may be issued by the OCD and DBM.                   29
30         7. Transparency Of Irrigation Projects. Of the amounts appropriated herein under the Operating Subsidy, the amount of Fifty Million Pesos (P50,000,000) shall             30
31   be allocated for the set-up, operation, and maintenance of systems, including activities related to data integration, information systems development, geo-tagging, and         31
32   capacity building of concerned NIA offices.                                                                                                                                     32
33          The NIA shall establish and maintain a publicly accessible online dashboard on its official website for all irrigation projects to ensure transparency and               33
34   accountability. The dashboard shall include the project timeline, name of contractors, details of awarded contracts, physical and financial status, and geo-tagged photos of    34
35   the projects taken at the start, middle, and completion stages.                                                                                                                 35
36         8. Reportorial Requirement. The NIA shall submit to the DBM, the Speaker of the House of Representatives, the President of the Senate of the Philippines,                 36
37   the House Committee on Appropriations and Senate Committee on Finance, either in printed form or by way of electronic document, quarterly reports on the utilization of         37
38   funds, including the master plan of irrigation projects and inventory of all existing and ongoing irrigation projects. The Administrator of NIA and the Administration's web    38
39   administrator or his/her equivalent shall be responsible for ensuring that said quarterly reports are likewise posted on the NIA's website.                                     39
40         9. Special Provisions Applicable to All Government-Owned or -Controlled Corporations. In addition to the foregoing special provision, the Special                         40
41   Provisions Applicable to All GOCCs shall be observed by the NIA.                                                                                                                41

45   Special Provision(s) Applicable to All GOCCs                                                                                                                                     45
46        1. Budgetary Support to Government Corporations. Income and revenues collected by GOCCs from all sources shall be used to cover all its operating                           46
47   requirements. Any deficiency may be augmented by the budgetary support from the National Government, which may either be:                                                        47
48        (a) Subsidy, which shall be used in accordance with the purposes identified in this Act: Provided , That unless otherwise stated in the special provisions, subsidy         48
49             releases may be used by GOCCs which are financially unable to pay for the separation or retirement benefits and incentives resulting from an approved                  49
50             reorganization, merger, streamlining, abolition, or privatization plan under R.A. No. 10149, other laws and issuances.                                                 50
51        (b) Equity, which shall be used as capital investment of the National Government in accordance with the capitalization requirement under pertinent laws. In no case         51
52             shall equity investments be used for the payment of salaries, allowances, incentives, and retirement and separation benefits, except in cases authorized by the        52
53             DBM.                                                                                                                                                                   53
54         2. Offsets Against Budgetary Support to Government Corporations. The appropriations authorized herein may be offset by the BTr against the: (i)                            54
55   corporate payments of cash dividends under R.A. No. 7656; (ii) guarantee fees; (iii) advances for loans relent to corporations; (iv) obligations which are guaranteed by the     55
56   National Government; and (v) other receivables of the government from the GOCCs.                                                                                                 56
57        If the total level of actual revenues at the end of the immediately preceding year, including income from liquid assets such as, but not limited to, interest in cash       57
58   deposits, short-term and bond investments, and other fund sources of the GOCC, exceed the corresponding projections considered in the formulation of the current year's          58
59   budgetary support program, the excess may be deducted from said program and the budgetary support may be reduced to the extent of such favorable result.                         59
     558 GENERAL APPROPRIATIONS BILL, FY 2027



 1         3. Prior Years' Subsidy Releases from the National Government. The GOCCs concerned are hereby authorized to use subsidy released for programs                           1
 2   and projects in prior years to cover the additional funding requirements of activities or projects covered by the programs or sub-programs indicated in this Act.             2
 3   Accordingly, they shall prepare a work and financial plan covering the projects or activities to be funded from prior years' subsidies subject to the endorsement of the      3
 4   GOCC's governing board, to be submitted to the DBM for approval.                                                                                                              4
 5        Implementation of this provision shall be subject to the guidelines issued by the DBM.                                                                                   5
 6         4. Payment of Compensation and Benefits. Payment of basic salaries, allowances, benefits, and incentives by GOCCs shall be made in accordance with                      6
 7   applicable laws, rules, and regulations such as, but not limited to, P.D. No. 985, as amended, R.A. No. 6758, as amended, R.A. No. 10149, E.O. No. 95, s. 2025, Memorandum    7
 8   Order No. 20, s. 2001, and Corporate Compensation Circular No. 10 dated February 15, 1999. In addition, payment of separation or retirement benefits shall be computed        8
 9   in accordance with the rates, conditions, and procedure prescribed under existing separation or retirement laws, and such pertinent guidelines issued thereon.                9
10         5. Submission of Corporate Operating Budgets and Other Related Financial Statements. All GOCCs, including GFIs, whether or not receiving                               10
11   budgetary support from the National Government, shall prepare their FY 2027 Corporate Operating Budgets (COBs) in accordance with E.O. No. 518, s. 1979, and the             11
12   procedures and guidelines prescribed by the DBM. Said COBs, together with their supporting financial statements, shall be approved by their governing boards, and            12
13   submitted to the Secretary of Budget and Management for review and evaluation as part of the budget process pursuant to Section 10, Chapter 4, Title XVII, Book IV of        13
14   E.O. No. 292, s. 1987. The NEA, NAPOCOR, and PNOC shall be governed further by the provisions of R.A. No. 7638.                                                              14
15         6. Implementation of Infrastructure Projects. The respective heads of GOCCs shall comply with the restrictions on critical geo-hazard areas or no-build                15
16   zones identified by the Mines and Geosciences Bureau and such other conditions provided under the General Provision on the Implementation of Infrastructure Projects         16
17   under this Act. In the case of housing projects, the shelter agencies shall likewise adopt and promote the use of new and innovative housing technologies and materials      17
18   to bring down the cost of housing and reduce any adverse impact of construction on the environment.                                                                          18
19         7. Tobacco Fund. The amount chargeable against the SAGF reflected in the BESF Table B.15 under the FY 2027 Proposed Expenditures shall be used by the                  19
20   National Tobacco Administration (NTA) for its operating requirements sourced from the forty percent (40%) of the balance of the entire collection from the specific taxes    20
21   on locally-manufactured Virginia-type cigarettes and tariff duties on imported leaf tobacco, after setting aside the share of the LGUs and BIR, in accordance with Section   21
22   5 of R.A. No. 4155, as amended by Section 3 of R.A. No. 5447.                                                                                                                22
23          Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of a budget request and other relevant budgetary requirements, and in accordance with judicious fiscal            23
24   programming by the National Government, as well as applicable laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                  24
25         8. Proceeds from the Exploration, Development and Exploitation of Energy Resources. The amount chargeable against the SAGF reflected in the                            25
26   BESF Table B.15 under the FY 2027 Proposed Expenditures shall be used for the payment of stranded contract costs and stranded debts transferred to and assumed by the        26
27   Power Sector Assets and Liabilities Management Corporation (PSALM), including anticipated shortfalls in accordance with Section 4 of R.A. No. 11371, sourced from the        27
28   proceeds of the net national government share from the Malampaya Fund under Section 8 of P.D. No. 910.                                                                       28
29          Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of a budget request and other relevant budgetary requirements, and in accordance with judicious fiscal            29
30   programming by the National Government, as well as applicable laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                  30
31         9. Tourism Promotions Fund. The amount chargeable against the SAGF reflected in the BESF Table B.15 under the FY 2027 Proposed Expenditures shall be                   31
32   used for tourism promotions and marketing activities of the Tourism Promotions Board (TPB) sourced from the following and constituted into the Tourism Promotions Fund       32
33   in accordance with Section 55 of R.A. No. 9593:                                                                                                                              33
34         (a) At least twenty five percent (25%) of the National Government share from PAGCOR; and                                                                               34
35         (b) At least twenty five percent (25%) of the National Government share from international airports and seaports.                                                      35
36          Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of a budget request and other relevant budgetary requirements, and in accordance with judicious fiscal            36
37   programming by the National Government, as well as applicable laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                  37
38         10. Remittance of Cash Dividends. Cash Dividends equivalent to at least fifty percent (50%) of the annual net earnings of GOCCs shall be remitted to the               38
39   National Treasury as income of the General Fund pursuant to R.A. No. 7656.                                                                                                   39
40         11. Transparency Seal. To enhance transparency and enforce accountability, and promote systematized access to government information, all GOCCs shall                  40
41   maintain a Transparency Seal to be posted on their websites. The Transparency Seal shall contain the following:                                                              41
42         a) corporation's mandate and functions, names of its officials with their position and designation, and its contact information;                                       42
43         b) approved COB and corresponding targets including any amount of budgetary support from the National Government;                                                      43
44         c) budgetary adjustment;                                                                                                                                               44
45         d) annual procurement plan/s and contracts awarded with the winning supplier, contractor, or consultant;                                                               45
46         e) major programs or projects and their target beneficiaries;                                                                                                          46
47         f) status of implementation, evaluation, or assessment reports of said programs or projects;                                                                           47
48         g) all subsidy and assistance programs of the government, including details on the manner of the execution, the amounts allocated, and relevant data of the target     48
49              beneficiaries subject to R.A. No. 10173 or the Data Privacy Act;                                                                                                  49
50         h) Budget and Financial Accountability Reports;                                                                                                                        50
51         i) Updated People's Freedom of Information (FOI) Manual signed by head of agency, Updated One-Page FOI Manual, and Agency FOI Reports;                                 51
52         j) year-end financial reports for the last three (3) fiscal years;                                                                                                     52
53         k) particulars of concessions, permits, or authorizations granted by the GOCC, subject to R.A. No. 10173 or the Data Privacy Act; and                                  53
54         l) current news and updated events conducted by GOCCs.                                                                                                                 54
55         GOCCs shall ensure that the content posted under the Transparency Seal is regularly reviewed, updated, and maintained using internal systems and procedures that       55
56   support accountability, data integrity, and operational efficiency.                                                                                                          56
57        The respective heads of GOCCs and their web administrators or equivalent shall be responsible for ensuring compliance with this requirement.                            57

 3         12. Fund Releases. Funds appropriated herein shall be under the administration of the DBM and released directly to the recipient GOCCs through the BTr,                   3
 4   subject to the submission of a budget request and other relevant budgetary requirements, as applicable, in accordance with applicable laws, rules, and regulations. All         4

 7   electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the GOCC has fully adopted the BTMS, within thirty (30) days after the end of every quarter.          7
 8         Likewise, the GOCCs shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                               8
 9         The GOCCs shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on their websites to the House of Representatives, Senate of the Philippines,         9
10   House Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, and regulations.     10
11   The date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                                          11

36                                                                                                                                                                              36
37   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                       37
38         1. Operating Requirements of the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority. All income and revenues collected by the MMDA from all sources,                          38
39   including the national tax allotment and the mandatory remittances of component LGUs, shall be used to cover all of its operating requirements. The subsidy appropriated   39
40   in this Act for MMDA shall be used only to augment any deficiency from its income and revenues to cover valid and authorized expenditures.                                 40
41         The MMDA shall submit to the DBM, not later than November 15 of the preceding year, its detailed and consolidated operating budget for the current fiscal year.      41
42   The detailed and consolidated operating budget shall reflect the MMDA's income and revenues from all sources, including its national tax allotment and the mandatory       42
43   remittances of component LGUs, as well as its projected expenditures, targeted program, activities, and projects.                                                          43
44         The MMDA shall likewise submit to the DBM, the Speaker of the House of Representatives, the President of the Senate of the Philippines, the House Committee on       44
45   Appropriations, and the Senate Committee on Finance, either in printed form or by way of electronic document, an annual report on financial and physical                   45
46   accomplishments. The Chairperson of MMDA and the Authority's web administrator or his/her equivalent shall be responsible for ensuring that said report shall likewise     46
47   be posted on the MMDA's website.                                                                                                                                           47
48         2. Implementation of Flood Control Projects. In the implementation of flood control projects, the MMDA shall conform with the respective flood control               48
49   master plans of LGUs and the drainage master plan approved by the Metro Manila Council.                                                                                    49
50         3. Promotion of People Mobility. The MMDA shall promote people mobility through road sharing projects and activities as well as the use of non-motorized             50
51   modes of transportation. The amount appropriated herein for the Traffic Management Program shall be used to cover the funding requirements for the promotion of people     51
52   mobility.                                                                                                                                                                  52
53         4. Appropriations for Activities or Projects. The amounts appropriated herein shall be used specifically for the following activities or projects in the             53
54   indicated amounts and conditions:                                                                                                                                          54

33          1. Financial Assistance to Local Government Units. The amount of Thirty Seven Billion Four Hundred Ninety Two Million Five Hundred Seventy Eight 33
34   Thousand Pesos (P37,492,578,000) appropriated herein shall be used for financial assistance to all LGUs for the following projects:                                                                             34
35            (a) implementation of agriculture-related programs and projects, such as: (i) provision of agricultural support services, which include planting materials distribution 35
36   system and operation of farm produce collection and buying stations; (ii) extension of on-site research services and facilities related to agriculture and fishery activities; 36
37   (iii) construction, restoration, and improvement of infrastructure facilities, including farm-to-market roads, slaughterhouses, small water impounding projects, fish ports, and 37
38   water supply systems; and (iv) provision of various production inputs for crops, livestock and poultry, and fisheries;                                                                                          38
39            (b) implementation of programs, projects, and activities for the protection, preservation and promotion of cultural heritage, including restoration, rehabilitation, 39
40   repair, improvement and/or maintenance of national heritage structures and sites;                                                                                                                               40
41            (c) Information and Communications Technology systems and infrastructure development, such as, but not limited to, establishment of Integrated Business Permit 41
42   and Licensing System, digitalization of payments for collections and disbursements, and purchase and installation of Closed-Circuit Television (CCTV) Surveillance System;                                      42
43            (d) construction, concreting, rehabilitation, repair, improvement, expansion, or upgrading of any of the following: (i) local roads or bridges; (ii) public markets; (iii) 43
44   multi-purpose buildings; (iv) multi-purpose halls; (v) sports stadiums; (vi) hospital buildings; (vii) health stations; (viii) water supply and sanitation projects; (ix) evacuation 44
45   centers; and (x) public cemeteries;                                                                                                                                                                             45
46            (e) construction, rehabilitation, repair, upgrading or improvement of the following projects: (i) green open spaces such as public parks and plazas, nature and 46
47   family/recreational parks, arboretum, botanical gardens and river esplanades; (ii) infrastructure for active mobility, such as: (a) physically separated bicycle lanes and 47
48   trails; (b) bicycle parking facilities; (c) pedestrian walkways and bridges; and (d) recreational trails; and (iii) nature-based investments aimed at increasing the resilience 48
49   of urban infrastructure, such as: (a) greening of public buildings; and (b) creation of green corridors;                                                                                                        49
50            (f) purchase of medical or hospital equipment;                                                                                                                                                         50
51            (g) establishment of Materials Recovery Facility with sorting station, drop-off center, composting facility, and recycling facility;                                                                   51
52             (h) implementation of programs, projects, and activities for disaster response, rehabilitation, and recovery, which include procurement/acquisition of disaster 52
53   equipment and vehicles for disaster response and rescue activities;                                                                                                                                             53
54            (i) adaptation and mitigation projects;                                                                                                                                                                54
55            (j) purchase of ambulance, mobile medical vehicle with apparatus/equipment, trucks, including mini firetrucks, and multi-purpose vehicles;                                                             55
56            (k) conversion of day care centers to child development center standards by fourth and fifth class municipalities;                                                                                     56
572 GENERAL APPROPRIATIONS BILL, FY 2027



 1            (l) support for the initial creation by LGUs of plantilla positions for child development teachers with at least a salary grade 11 level and child development workers          1
 2   with at least a salary grade 8 level for the fourth and fifth class municipalities, subject to the professional requirements under R.A. No. 12199, existing civil service laws,          2
 3   rules, and regulations, and the DBM issuances on organization, staffing, position classification, and compensation. The DBM and DILG, in coordination with the Early                     3
 4   Childhood Care and Development Council, shall issue the guidelines to ensure that LGUs can fund on a sustainable basis the requirements therefor; and                                    4
 5            (m) assistance to individuals in crisis situations in any of the following forms: (i) rice distribution projects; (ii) medical/health related projects; (iii) funeral, which    5
 6   includes burial or cremation; (iv) transportation; (v) food assistance; (vi) educational assistance/scholarship; and (vii) purchase of construction or repair materials for              6
 7   houses destroyed during human-induced or natural calamities, upon endorsement by the local social welfare and development office or equivalent of partially/totally                      7
 8   destroyed houses.                                                                                                                                                                        8

10   consideration LGUs' adherence to established governance standards.                                                                                                                      10
11          Disbursement and utilization by LGUs shall be subject to the pertinent provisions of existing government procurement laws, applicable budgeting, accounting, and                 11
12   auditing rules and regulations, and such other guidelines to be issued by the DBM in coordination with the relevant agencies.                                                           12
13          2. Support to the Barangay Development Program of the National Task Force to End Local Communist Armed Conflict. The amount of                                                   13
14   Nine Billion Seven Hundred Forty Million Pesos (P9,740,000,000) appropriated herein shall be used for the implementation of specific programs and projects of the National              14
15   Task Force to End Local Communist Armed Conflict (NTF-ELCAC) for the one thousand nine hundred forty eight (1,948) cleared barangays as certified by the NTF-ELCAC,                     15
16   listed in Volume I-B of this Act: Provided , That each cleared barangay shall be allocated with an amount to be used for the following projects: (i) farm-to-market road;               16
17   (ii) school building; (iii) water and sanitation system; (iv) health stations; and (v) electrification.                                                                                 17
18         The release of funds shall be subject to the guidelines to be issued by the DBM, in coordination with the NTF-ELCAC.                                                              18
19         3. Participatory Budgeting Support for Local Government Units. The amount of One Billion Pesos (P1,000,000,000) appropriated herein shall be used to                              19
20   support the implementation of the following priority local development projects: (a) local roads; (b) bridges; (c) farm-to-market roads; (d) agriculture-related project-water          20
21   supply system; (e) multi-purpose buildings; (f) water supply and sanitation projects; (g) evacuation centers; (h) public market; (i) purchase and installation of CCTV                  21
22   Surveillance System; and (j) assistance to individuals in crisis situations in any of the following forms: (i) medical/health-related programs; (ii) funeral, which includes            22
23   burial or cremation; (iii) transportation; (iv) food assistance; and (v) educational assistance/scholarship.                                                                            23
24          The fund shall be used to support eligible LGUs based on the following criteria: (a) the proposed projects are identified as priority programs or projects in the duly           24
25   approved Annual Investment Programs of the recipient LGUs and are aligned with the pertinent Regional Development Plans; (b) the identification, prioritization, and                    25
26   endorsement of such projects are undertaken through transparent, participatory, and inclusive mechanisms, with the concurrence of duly accredited civil society                         26
27   organizations represented in the Local Development Councils, in accordance with existing laws, rules, and regulations; and (c) the recipient LGUs are able to demonstrate,              27
28   through appropriate documentary evidence, existing initiatives or institutional mechanisms promoting open government pursuant to E.O. No. 31, s. 2023, institutionalizing               28
29   the Philippine Open Government Partnership.                                                                                                                                             29
30          Disbursement and utilization by the LGUs shall be subject to pertinent provisions of existing government procurement laws, applicable budgeting, accounting, and                 30
31   auditing rules and regulations, and such other guidelines to be issued by the DBM in coordination with the relevant agencies.                                                           31
32          4. Growth Equity Fund. The amount of Ten Billion Three Hundred Million Pesos (P10,300,000,000) appropriated herein shall be used as financial assistance to                      32
33   assist poor, disadvantaged, lagging, and low-income LGUs, and those with fiscal gaps arising from the devolution, or to augment provincial resources for inter-municipal                33
34   programs and projects, in order to gradually enable the full and efficient implementation of the functions, services and facilities devolved to the LGUs concerned in                   34
35   accordance with Section 17 of R.A. No. 7160 and other pertinent laws, as well as E.O. No. 138, s. 2021, as amended by E.O. No. 103, s. 2025.                                            35
36           Release of funds shall be subject to the guidelines to be issued by the DBM, in coordination with the DILG, DOF, DEPDev, and other relevant agencies.                           36
37          5. Use of Local Government Support Fund. The amounts appropriated for the Local Government Support Fund (LGSF) shall be used exclusively in                                      37
38   accordance with the purposes specified under the relevant special provisions in this Act.                                                                                               38
39         In no case shall the LGSF be used for the following: (i) programs, projects, and activities of the beneficiary LGUs, such as construction of waiting sheds, purchase of           39
40   road studs, attendance to study tours or seminars, conduct of capacity building activities, implementation of flood control projects, and for those projects already fully              40
41   covered by other sources of funds; (ii) administrative expenses; and (iii) payment of personnel services expenses, such as salaries, honoraria, allowances, and bonuses,                41
42   except as otherwise provided herein.                                                                                                                                                    42

16   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                                                                       16
17         1. Contingent Fund. The amount of Thirteen Billion Pesos (P13,000,000,000) appropriated herein shall cover the funding requirements of new or urgent activities 17
18   or projects of national government agencies, GOCCs, and LGUs that need to be implemented or paid during the year, such as, but not limited to, the following: (i) legal 18
19   obligation of the National Government arising from final and executory decisions of competent authorities, such as compromise agreements, arbitral awards, mediation 19
20   settlement agreements, and professional services in connection thereto; (ii) requirements of newly created offices; or (iii) deficiencies in the appropriations for local and 20
21   external travels of the President of the Philippines.                                                                                                                                                                      21
22         In no case shall this Fund be used for: (i) the provision of confidential and intelligence funds to civilian departments and agencies with no mandate to perform 22
23   security and intelligence-related functions unless the President certifies as to the extreme necessity thereof; or (ii) the purchase of motor vehicles, including any 23
24   improvements thereon.                                                                                                                                                                                                      24
25         Release of funds shall be made directly to the agencies concerned, except for GOCCs and LGUs which shall be made through the BTr, subject to the approval by the 25
26   President of the Philippines, other than payment resulting from final and executory decisions of competent authorities, which shall be subject to the approval of the DBM.                                                 26
27         The DBM shall include information on the releases from the Contingent Fund in its quarterly and annual reports submitted to Congress.                                                                                27
28         2. Appropriations under the Contingent Fund. The DBM is hereby authorized to approve the use of amounts from one allotment class to another within 28
29   the authorized purpose.                                                                                                                                                                                                    29

20         (a) Pension of: (i) AFP retirees; (ii) war or military veterans of the DND; (iii) retired uniformed personnel of the DILG, including those for retired PNP uniformed 20
21              personnel to be paid by the National Police Commission pursuant to R.A. No. 6975, as amended by R.A. No. 8551, Philippine Constabulary-Integrated National 21
22              Police (PC-INP), NAMRIA, and Philippine Coast Guard; and (iv) other retirees of the National Government;                                                                          22
23         (b) Retirement benefits of: (i) optional retirees of the National Government; (ii) retired personnel of GOCCs, which are financially unable to pay said benefits, subject 23
24              to the submission of the streamlining program and measures that will enhance efficiency and effectiveness; and (iii) personnel devolved to LGUs in accordance 24
25              with N.B.C. Nos. 429 and 429-A dated September 30, 1993 and December 29, 1993, respectively;                                                                                      25
26         (c) Separation benefits or incentives of affected personnel pursuant to the implementation of: (i) reorganization, streamlining, optimization, merger/consolidation, 26
27              abolition, privatization, and other forms of organizational restructuring authorized under applicable laws, rules, and regulations; and (ii) abolition of the 27
28              Autonomous Regional Government in Muslim Mindanao pursuant to R.A. No. 11054;                                                                                                     28
29         (d) Monetization of leave credits of National Government personnel and transferred leave credits of National Government personnel devolved to the LGUs in 29
30              accordance with R.A. No. 7160, as implemented by E.O. No. 503, s. 1992 and N.B.C. Nos. 429 and 429-A; and                                                                         30
31         (e) Other deficiencies in the authorized appropriations for retirement and terminal leave benefits.                                                                                    31
32         In no case shall this Fund be used to pay any additional compensation component of pension or retirement and terminal leave benefits, such as year-end bonus, cash 32
33   gifts, bonuses, per diems, allowances, overtime pay or such other benefits, unless otherwise specifically authorized under existing laws.                                                    33

36   169466 promulgated on May 9, 2007 shall be based on the list of eligible PC-INP retirees with the corresponding computation of their respective retirement benefits and 36
37   pensions. Said list shall be duly authenticated by the PNP and submitted to the DBM for validation of computed benefits. The computation shall exclude retirement 37

17   Special Provision(s)                                                                                                                                                                                      17
18         1. Availment of the Unprogrammed Appropriations. The amounts authorized herein for Purpose Nos. 1-3 may be used when any of the following exists: 18
19         (a) Excess revenue collections in any one of the identified non-tax revenue sources from its corresponding revenue collection target, as reflected in the BESF;                                     19
20         (b) New revenue collections or those arising from new tax or non-tax sources which are not part of, nor included in, the original revenue sources reflected in the 20
21              BESF; or                                                                                                                                                                                       21
22         (c) Approved loans for foreign-assisted projects.                                                                                                                                                   22
23         Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of a budget request and other relevant budgetary requirements in accordance with applicable laws, rules, and 23
24   regulations, and the following: (i) for excess revenue collections, issuance of a certification that remitted collections to the BTr from a particular revenue source has 24
25   exceeded the corresponding revenue collections target; or (ii) for new revenue collections, issuance of a certification that remitted collections identified were not part of, 25
26   nor included in, the original revenue collection targets reflected.                                                                                                                                       26
27         In the case of approved loans for foreign-assisted projects, the issuance of SARO covering the loan proceeds shall be subject to submission by the agency concerned 27
28   of a budget request supported by a copy of the perfected loan agreement, as approved in accordance with pertinent laws, rules, regulations, and guidelines issued thereon. 28
29         Nevertheless, prioritization of funding of the purposes under the Unprogrammed Appropriations may be as follows, presented from top priority:                                                       29
30         (a) Not requiring excess/new revenue collections:                                                                                                                                                   30
31              (i) Support to Foreign-Assisted Projects; and                                                                                                                                                  31
32              (ii) Conversion of National Government Advances into Subsidy for GOCCs;                                                                                                                        32
33         (b) Requiring excess/new revenue collections:                                                                                                                                                       33
34              (i) Program on Risk Management; and                                                                                                                                                            34
35              (ii) Restoration of the Fund Balances of the Philippine Deposit Insurance Corporation.                                                                                                         35
36         In view of the nature of the sources of funding for Unprogrammed Appropriations, the validity period of releases covering Unprogrammed Appropriations shall be 36
37   until December 31, 2027, while obligations and disbursements therefrom shall be subject to the rule provided in the General Provision on Cash Budgeting System under this 37
38   Act.                                                                                                                                                                                                      38
39         2. Restoration of the Fund Balances of the Philippine Deposit Insurance Corporation. The amount of Fifty Seven Billion Pesos (P57,000,000,000) 39
40   authorized herein for the Restoration of the Fund Balances of the Philippine Deposit Insurance Corporation under Purpose No. 1 shall be used to restore part of the amount 40
41   of the fund balances of the Philippine Deposit Insurance Corporation remitted to the National Government pursuant to Special Provision No. 1(d), Unprogrammed 41
42   Appropriations of the FY 2024 General Appropriations Act.                                                                                                                                                 42
43         Release of funds for the purpose shall be subject to Special Provision No. 1 hereof.                                                                                                                43
44          3. Program on Risk Management. The amount of Three Billion Six Hundred Million Pesos (P3,600,000,000) authorized herein for Program on Risk 44
45   Management under Purpose No. 2 shall be used for the payment of contigent liabilities arising from Public-Private Partnerships, in accordance with R.A. No. 11966 and its 45
46   IRR.                                                                                                                                                                                                      46
47          Release of funds shall be subject to Special Provision No. 1 hereof, and to the issuance of new guidelines which shall be formulated by the Public-Private 47
48   Partnership Center of the Philippines, in coordination with the Inter-Agency Technical Working Group on Contingent Liabilities, as approved by the DBCC.                                                  48
49         4. Conversion of National Government Advances into Subsidy for Government-Owned or -Controlled Corporations. The amount of Eight 49
50   Billion Eight Hundred Thirty One Million Pesos (P8,831,000,000) used to cover the National Government advances for debt servicing of loan obligations of GOCCs and 50
51   interest on the National Government advances, shall be converted into subsidy. Such conversion shall require the issuance of SARO for book entry purposes chargeable 51
52   against Conversion of National Government Advances into Subsidy for GOCCs under Purpose No. 4.                                                                                                            52
53          5. Amounts under the Unprogrammed Appropriations. The DBM is hereby authorized to approve the use of amounts from one allotment class to 53
54   another within each authorized purpose.                                                                                                                                                                   54
55         6. Reportorial Requirement. The DBM shall submit to the Speaker of the House of Representatives, the President of the Senate of the Philippines, the House 55
56   Committee on Appropriations, and the Senate Committee on Finance, either in printed form or by way of electronic document, quarterly reports on releases from the 56
57   Unprogrammed Appropriations.                                                                                                                                                                              57

53   Projects, and the rehabilitation, repair or reconstruction of distribution facilities damaged by natural and human-induced calamities, and provision for electric cooperatives'   53
54   capital requirements through loans outlay. The funds shall be sourced from the unutilized balances of prior years' subsidy by the National Government, new funding sources        54

11   the total amount approved in this Act exclusively for the MOOE and Capital Outlay requirements related to missionary electrification, and rehabilitation and management of          11
12   watershed areas due to the effects of peso devaluation, fuel price increase in the market, improvement or changes in power generation activities or demand of customers,            12
13   electrification of new areas, increase in taxes and production costs, or imposition of new taxes, man-made crises, including but not limited to armed conflict, sabotage,           13
14   terrorism, cyberattacks, or other human-induced disruptions that materially affect power generation, transmission, distribution, or watershed management operations, and            14
15   circumstances arising from government actions, policies, or directives, such as regulatory disputes, imposition of new compliance requirements, delays or suspension of             15
16   permits, or other governmental measures that materially hinder or disrupt NAPOCOR's operations, electrification programs, or watershed management activities.                       16
17         The fund shall be sourced from new funding sources, such as income arising from increase in universal and generation charges approved by the Energy Regulatory                17
18   Commission or grant of financial assistance by LGUs and other sources as authorized under existing laws, guidelines and issuances such as, but not limited to, R.A. No.             18
19   9136 and its IRR, as certified by the Chief Accountant and President of NAPOCOR.                                                                                                    19
20         In no case shall Personnel Services allocation be augmented beyond the total amount approved in this Act.                                                                     20
21         7. Collection of Delinquent Receivables from Electric Cooperatives under the Small Power Utilities Group. In order to augment the fund sources                                21
22   necessary to support the budgetary requirements of the NAPOCOR and ensure the viability of its operations, the NAPOCOR Board of Directors is hereby authorized to act               22
23   with finality, without further need of confirmation, appraisal, or assessment from other government agencies, the settlement and compromise of accrued penalties, interest          23
24   and other charges due from electric cooperatives. In all cases, the NAPOCOR Board of Directors shall ensure that the approved settlement and compromise shall not be                24
25   against provisions of law or public policy, and shall be consistent with public interest and redound to the benefit of the National Government.                                     25
26         8. Remittance of Cash Dividends. Cash dividends equivalent to at least fifty percent (50%) of the annual net earnings of the NAPOCOR shall be deposited with                  26
27   the National Treasury as income of the General Fund pursuant to R. A. No. 7656.                                                                                                     27
28         9. Audit of Government Funds. Government funds authorized herein to be invested as equity by the corporation to its subsidiaries, as well as the grant of                     28
29   subsidy, loan contribution or any kind of financial assistance to end-user entities both in the private or public sector, shall be subject to audit by the COA pursuant to the      29
30   provisions of P.D. No. 1445, as amended.                                                                                                                                            30

 7         Sec. 3. The General Appropriations Act as the Allotment Order. The General Appropriations Act (GAA), upon its effectivity, shall be considered the                           7
 8   allotment authorizing agencies to obligate in accordance with its provisions, except for the following:                                                                            8
 9         (a) Appropriations that by virtue of law, general or special provisions, and rules and regulations have conditions or requirements before release; and                       9
10         (b) Lump-sum appropriations in the agency budget and special purpose funds that have no details necessary for release.                                                      10
11         In the case of automatic appropriations, the allotment shall be issued by the DBM upon compliance with the conditions provided by law.                                      11
12         The DBM shall identify the items of appropriations in the GAA which are not covered by the GAA as the allotment order and submit a copy thereof to the Speaker              12
13   of the House of Representatives, President of the Senate of the Philippines, House Committee on Appropriations, and Senate Committee on Finance.                                  13

17          Sec. 4. Receipts or Revenues Collected by Agencies. As a general rule, all fees, charges, assessments, and other receipts or revenues collected by                         17
18   departments, bureaus and offices of the National Government, including Constitutional Offices enjoying fiscal autonomy in the exercise of their mandated functions, at such       18
19   rates as are now or may be approved by the appropriate approving authority shall be deposited with the National Treasury as income of the General Fund pursuant to                19
20   Section 44, Chapter 5, Book VI of E.O. No. 292, s. 1987, and Section 65 of P.D. No. 1445.                                                                                         20
21         Exceptions to the foregoing are:                                                                                                                                            21
22         (a) Receipts authorized by law to be recorded as a Special Account in the General Fund (SAGF), Trust Fund, or a fund other than the General Fund which shall be             22
23              established in accordance with rules and regulations as may be issued by the Permanent Committee created under Section 45, Chapter 5, Book VI of E.O. No.              23
24              292. The said special funds may be made available for expenditure, subject to any special provision of the agencies concerned; and                                     24
25         (b) Other instances authorized by law.                                                                                                                                      25
26         Disbursements or expenditures by agencies from use or retention of income absent the above legal authority or from income deposited outside of the National                 26
27   Treasury without legal basis shall be void and shall subject the erring officials and employees to disciplinary actions in accordance with Section 43, Chapter 5, and             27
28   Section 80, Chapter 7, Book VI of E.O. No. 292, and to appropriate civil and criminal actions under existing laws.                                                                28
29         All agencies shall ensure that fees, charges, and assessments collected cover the costs of services delivered to the public. They may be allowed to raise their fees        29
30   and charges in accordance with A.O. No. 31, s. 2012, DOF-DBM-NEDA J.C. No. 1-2013 dated January 30, 2013, and such other guidelines issued by the agencies concerned.             30
31   The schedule of fees, charges, and assessments collectible by any government agency, as well as any updates thereon, shall be posted on their respective websites and in          31
32   big bold characters in a conspicuous place within the agency, including its regional, provincial, field, or extension offices.                                                    32
33         Sec. 5. Special Accounts in the General Fund. The amount chargeable against the SAGFs reflected in the BESF Table B.15 under the FY 2027 Proposed                           33
34   Expenditures shall be used for purposes authorized under their respective substantive laws, and shall be governed by the conditions prescribed therein, as well as the            34
35   applicable budgeting, accounting, and auditing laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                                      35
36          Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of a budget request and other relevant budgetary requirements, and in accordance with judicious fiscal                 36
37   programming by the National Government, as well as applicable laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                       37
38         Sec. 6. Donations. Departments, bureaus, and offices of the National Government, including Constitutional Offices enjoying fiscal autonomy and SUCS may accept              38
39   donations, contributions, grants, bequests, or gifts, in cash or in kind, from various sources, domestic or foreign, for purposes relevant to their functions. In the case of     39
40   grants, in cash or in kind, from governments of foreign countries, their agencies and instrumentalities or multilateral institutions or organizations, acceptance thereof shall   40
41   be subject to the prior clearance and approval by the President or his authorized representative based on the recommendation of the Secretary of Finance. On the other            41
42   hand, other donations, in cash or in kind, from foreign governments shall require prior clearance and approval by the President or his authorized representative based on         42
43   the recommendation of the Secretary of Foreign Affairs.                                                                                                                           43
44         Receipts from donations, whether in cash or in kind, shall be accounted for in the books of the donee-government agency in accordance with accounting and auditing          44
45   rules and regulations. The receipts from cash donations and proceeds from sale of donated commodities shall be deposited with the National Treasury and recorded as               45
46   SAGF and shall be available to the implementing agency concerned through a budget request and other relevant budgetary requirements in accordance with applicable                 46
47   laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                                                                                     47
48         The cash value of the donations shall be deemed automatically appropriated for the purpose specified by the donor. Donations with a term not exceeding one (1) year         48
49   shall be treated as trust receipts in accordance with the General Provision on Trust Receipts under this Act.                                                                     49
50         Disbursements or expenditures by agencies in violation of the above requirements shall be void and shall subject the erring officials and employees to disciplinary         50
51   actions in accordance with Section 43, Chapter 5, and Section 80, Chapter 7, Book VI of E.O. No. 292, and to appropriate civil and criminal actions under existing laws.          51
52         The donee-agency concerned shall submit its quarterly reports of all donations received, whether in cash or in kind, and expenditures or disbursements thereon              52
53   through the Unified Reporting System (URS) or other electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully adopted the Budget             53
54   and Treasury Management System (BTMS), within thirty (30) days after the end of every quarter.                                                                                    54
55         Likewise, the agency shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                                55
56         The donee-agency concerned shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the House of Representatives, Senate of              56
57   the Philippines, House Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, COA, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws,          57
58   rules, and regulations. The date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                     58

 1         Sec. 7. Trust Receipts. The following shall be deposited with the National Treasury and recorded as trust receipts in accordance with E.O. No. 338, s. 1996, as 1

 4   autonomy and SUCS: (i) from non-tax sources, such as insurance proceeds, acting as trustee, agent, or administrator; (ii) as a guaranty for the fulfillment of an obligation; 4

 6         (b) Those classified by law or regulations as trust receipts.                                                                                                             6

45         Sec. 10. Revolving Funds. The following receipts may be constituted, established, and maintained as revolving funds:                                                     45
46         (a) Those expressly created and authorized by law;                                                                                                                       46
47         (b) Rentals for the use of buildings and facilities or from fees imposed for board and lodging, by agencies to be used for the MOOE or Capital Outlay requirements 47
48               of said buildings and facilities. subject to any guidelines issued by the agency concerned and to budgeting, accounting, and auditing rules and regulations; and   48
49         (c) Other business-type activities of agencies, including sale of products, which are authorized by the Permanent Committee to be utilized for the operational 49
50               expenses of said business-type activity, subject to any conditions prescribed under the special provision of the agency concerned and the rules and regulations 50
51               as may be prescribed by the Permanent Committee.                                                                                                                   51
52          Revolving funds shall be separately recorded and deposited in an authorized government depository bank, and considered self-perpetuating and self-liquidating. All 52
53   eligible obligations or expenditures incurred for the operations of the foregoing activities shall be charged against the revolving fund. In no case shall said fund be used 53

56   actions in accordance with Section 43, Chapter 5, and Section 80, Chapter 7, Book VI of E.O. No. 292, and to appropriate civil and criminal actions under existing laws.       56

 5          Sec. 11. Revolving Fund for Research and Development, Science and Technology Capability Building, and Technology Transfer                                               5
 6   Activities. All income generated from commercialization of intellectual property and/or intellectual property rights from research and development funded by public            6
 7   funds shall be constituted as a revolving fund for use of the research and development institutes or institutions undertaking technology transfer, deposited in an             7
 8   authorized government depository bank, subject to accounting and auditing rules and regulations: Provided , That said income shall be used to defray intellectual property     8
 9   management costs and expenses and to fund research and development, science and technology capability building, and technology transfer activities, including operation        9
10   of technology licensing offices: Provided, further, That no amount of said income shall be used for payment of salaries and other allowances: Provided, finally, That the     10
11   use of said income shall be subject to the limitations provided under Section 18 of R.A. No. 10055.                                                                           11
12        Disbursements or expenditures by agencies in violation of the above requirement shall be void and shall subject the erring officials and employees to disciplinary       12
13   actions in accordance with Section 43, Chapter 5, and Section 80, Chapter 7. Book VI of E.O. No. 292, and to appropriate civil and criminal actions under existing laws.      13
