20          Sec. 12. Reversion, Closure, and Transfer of Balances of Special Accounts, Fiduciary or Trust Funds, Revolving Funds, and                                              20
21   Unauthorized Accounts. Executive agencies, such as, but not limited to, departments, bureaus, offices, and instrumentalities of the National Government, including            21
22   Constitutional Offices enjoying fiscal autonomy, SUCS, and GOCCS shall immediately assess the status of all Special Accounts, Fiduciary or Trust Funds, and Revolving         22
23   Funds and submit assessment reports to the Permanent Committee within ninety (90) days from the issuance of the guidelines for the purpose.                                   23
24         The agency shall, based on its assessment, close and revert all balances of Special Accounts, Fiduciary or Trust Funds, and Revolving Funds to the General Fund in      24
25   any of the following instances: (i) when there is no legal basis for its creation; (ii) when their terms have expired; (iii) when they are no longer necessary for the        25
26   attainment of the purposes for which said funds were established; (iv) when their purpose is duplicative or unnecessarily overlaps with the purposes of other funds; (v)      26
27   when their purposes are fulfilled or accomplished; (vi) when they have remained dormant for an unreasonable length of time; or (vii) when their purposes are funded           27
28   under this Act.                                                                                                                                                               28
29         In case an agency fails or refuses to implement such closure, reversion or transfer, the Permanent Committee may recommend for approval of the President the            29
30   closure, reversion or transfer of Special Accounts, Fiduciary or Trust Funds, Revolving Funds and Unauthorized Accounts, as the case may be, on any applicable grounds,       30
31   to wit: (i) in the cases above-mentioned; (ii) when used in violation of the rules and regulations issued by the Permanent Committee; or (iii) when needed by the General     31
32   Fund in times of emergency.                                                                                                                                                   32
33         Said agencies shall likewise transfer to the National Treasury all balances of unauthorized accounts with any banking institution. Unauthorized Accounts shall refer    33
34   to cash account balances maintained by agencies without legal basis or those while legally authorized are maintained outside of the National Treasury in violation of law.    34
35         Implementation of this Section shall be subject to Permanent Committee J.C. No. 4-2012 dated September 11, 2012, and such other guidelines to be issued by the          35
36   Permanent Committee.                                                                                                                                                          36
37         Sec. 13. Transparency on Public Funds. Consistent with the State policy on full public disclosure of government transactions, the BTr shall post on its                 37
38   official website information relating to all Special Accounts and Funds deposited with the National Treasury, which shall include, but not limited to the following: (i)      38
39   agency under whose name the account or fund was constituted or created; (ii) funding source/s of the account or fund; (iii) legal basis for the creation of the account or    39
40   fund; (iv) allowable uses/purposes of the account or fund; (v) monthly balances of each account or fund; and (vi) such other pertinent information as may be reasonably       40
41   required to be posted on the BTr website.                                                                                                                                     41
42         In like manner, departments, bureaus, offices, and instrumentalities of the National Government, including Constitutional Offices enjoying fiscal autonomy, SUCS, and   42
43   GOCCS shall post on their respective official websites information relating to public funds deposited, maintained, and invested by them with any banking or financial         43
44   institution which shall include, but not limited to the following: (i) name of the banking or financial institution/s where public funds are deposited, maintained or         44
45   invested; (ii) specific income or fund sources; (iii) legal basis for depositing, maintaining or investing said income/fund source/s with the bank/s or financial             45
46   institution/s; (iv) allowable uses/purposes of the income or fund; (v) monthly balances of each account or fund; and (vi) such other pertinent information as may be          46
47   reasonably required to be posted by the agency concerned on its website.                                                                                                      47
48         The head of the agency concerned and the agency's web administrator or his/her equivalent shall be responsible for ensuring compliance with the foregoing               48
49   requirements.                                                                                                                                                                 49
50         Agencies shall ensure that posts in their website are searchable for public's easy access of information regarding matters on public funds.                             50
51         Sec. 14. Conduct of Seminar, Conference, Training, and Oath Taking Programs. Departments, bureaus, offices, and instrumentalities of the National                       51
52   Government, including Constitutional Offices enjoying fiscal autonomy which conduct seminar, conference, training, and oath taking programs, in relation to their mandated    52
53   functions are authorized to collect fees from government and private agency participants for said activities. The proceeds derived from each seminar, conference, training,   53
54   and oath taking activities shall be deposited with the National Treasury as income of the General Fund pursuant to Section 44, Chapter 5, Book VI of E.O. No. 292.            54
55         However, the agencies which do not have sufficient appropriations in their budgets for the purpose may use the proceeds for the conduct of the said seminar,            55
56   conference, training, and oath taking activities subject to budgeting, accounting, and auditing rules and regulations. Any excess proceeds shall be deposited with the        56
57   National Treasury as income of the General Fund.                                                                                                                              57

30        Sec. 17. National Internal Revenue Taxes and Import Duties. The amounts pertaining to the following taxes and duties shall be considered as both                         30
31   revenue and expenditure of the government, and are deemed automatically appropriated:                                                                                         31
32         (a) National internal revenue taxes and import duties payable or assumed by departments, bureaus, offices, and instrumentalities of the National Government,            32
33             including Constitutional Offices enjoying fiscal autonomy and SUCS to the government arising from foreign donations, grants, and loans;                             33
34         (b) Non-cash tax transactions of the following government agencies: (i) the BTr for documentary stamp taxes on the issuance of foreign and domestic securities, and     34
35             foreign currency acquisition for payment of debt service; (ii) DND and PNP on importations of military hardware, software, munitions, arms and equipment; (iii)     35
36             Bureau of Fire Protection on importations of fire-fighting equipment, rescue equipment, and personal protective gears; (iv) the DOTr for the Metro Rail Transit     36
37             Line 3 System incurred starting FY 1997 in accordance with the provisions of the Build- Lease-Transfer Agreement executed thereon; (v) Philippine Coast Guard       37
38             and National Coast Watch Center of the Office of the President of the Philippines on importation, grants, and donations of hardware, software, munitions, arms,     38
39             and equipment for maritime security and law enforcement, marine environmental protection, maritime safety, maritime communications, maritime domain                 39
40             awareness, and search and rescue; (vi) special hospitals, specialty hospitals, DOH-retained hospitals and SUC hospitals on importation of health equipment; (vii)   40
41             Office of the President on donations of electric vehicles to the government; and (viii) other tax obligations assumed by the National Government pursuant to a      41
42             valid PPP agreement; and                                                                                                                                            42
43         (c) Tax expenditure subsidies approved by the Fiscal Incentives Review Board, which include, among others, the AFP Commissary and Exchange Service, the PNP             43
44             Service Store System, and the Procurement Service Exchange Marts or PX Marts, in accordance with E.O. No. 93, s. 1986, as amended, R.A. No. 11534, and other        44
45             pertinent laws, rules, and regulations issued thereon.                                                                                                              45
46          Implementation of this Section shall be subject to the guidelines issued by the DOF and DBM, and such other guidelines issued by the agencies concerned.               46
47          Sec. 18. Loan Agreements. Departments, bureaus, offices, and instrumentalities of the National Government, including Constitutional Offices enjoying fiscal            47
48   autonomy, SUCS, and GOCCs, except those engaged in banking, shall in no case enter into foreign or domestic loan agreements, whether in cash or in kind, unless the           48
49   following conditions, as may be applicable are complied with:                                                                                                                 49
50         (a) Prior approval of the President of the Philippines;                                                                                                                 50
51         (b) Concurrence of the Monetary Board;                                                                                                                                  51
52         (c) Conditions provided by pertinent laws; and                                                                                                                          52
53         (d) Issuance of Forward Obligational Authority (FOA) by the DBM for project loans or issuance of a DBCC resolution covering the full amount in the case of program      53
54             loans, and an equivalent document for those undertaken by GOCCs. In the issuance of a FOA, the DBM shall consider the budgetary implications of foreign-            54
55             assisted projects.                                                                                                                                                  55
56         The Monetary Board shall, within thirty (30) days from the end of every quarter, submit to the Congress a report of its decisions on applications for loans to be       56
57   contracted or guaranteed by the government or GOCCs which have the effect of increasing the foreign debt.                                                                     57

 3         Sec. 19. Use of Government Funds. Government funds shall be utilized in accordance with the appropriations authorized for the purpose and comply with                          3
 4   applicable laws, rules, and regulations, such as, but not limited to, the following:                                                                                                 4
 5         (a) Purchase of goods, infrastructure projects, and consulting services, including common-use supplies, shall be made in accordance with the existing government               5
 6              procurement laws, rules, and regulations;                                                                                                                                 6
 7         (b) Purchase of motor vehicles shall be made pursuant to A.O. No. 14, s. 2018, GPPB Resolution No. 06-2024 dated October 4, 2024, B.C. No. 2022-1 dated February               7
 8              11, 2022, B.C. No. 2022-1A dated March 1, 2023, and such other pertinent guidelines; Provided , That priority shall be given to motor vehicles deemed critical to         8
 9              health, uniformed services, and disaster risk preparedness and response;                                                                                                  9
10         (c) Purchase of electric vehicles in compliance with the targets of the Comprehensive Roadmap for the Electric Vehicle Industry shall be made pursuant to R.A. No.            10
11              11697, its IRR, and other pertinent guidelines;                                                                                                                          11
12         (d) Payment of foreign travel expenses of any government official and employee for training, seminar, or conference abroad when the foreign mission cannot                    12
13              effectively represent our country or travels necessitated by authorized international commitments shall be made in accordance with E.O. No. 77, s. 2019, and             13
14              such other issuances as may be issued thereon: Provided. That no official or employee may be sent to foreign training when they are due to retire within one             14
15              (1) year after the said foreign travel;                                                                                                                                  15
16         (e) Provisions for fuel, parts, repair and maintenance of government vehicles shall be made a priority during transport crisis, such as that occasioned by street             16
17              demonstrations, welgang bayan , floods, typhoons, and other emergencies, to ensure availability of government vehicles of any type which may be utilized to              17
18              transport, for free, commuters on a round-the-clock basis; and                                                                                                           18
19         (f) Provisions for food and refreshments in government meetings, seminars, conferences, and other activities shall observe preference and priority to locally                 19
20              produced goods or Philippine products consistent with Section 4(f) of R.A. No. 6713 in relation to Section 2(g) of R.A. No. 11981.                                       20
21       All agencies of the government are encouraged to optimize the use of government funds through the implementation of efficiency measures that would result in the                21
22   reduction of overhead and non-vital maintenance and other operating expenses.                                                                                                       22
23        In the implementation of programs, activities, or projects authorized in this Act, all heads of agencies of the government, including GOCCS, GFIs, SUCs, and LGUs, are         23
24   responsible for all government funds and property pertaining to their agencies, consistent with Section 51, Chapter 9, Subtitle B, Title I, Book V of E.O. No. 292.                 24
25        In accordance with the budgetary principle that an item of appropriation is characterized by singular correspondence, which is an allocation of a specified singular           25
26   amount for a specified singular purpose, all heads of agencies shall ensure that budgetary proposals shall not include multiple entries for the same item of appropriation.         26
27        In case of multiple entries for a single item of appropriation, the funding for the same purpose shall only be released once. Any other duplicative funding for the            27
28   same item of appropriation shall no longer be released and shall lapse after the end of the validity period thereof, subject to pertinent budgeting. accounting and auditing        28
29   laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                                                                                       29
30           Sec. 20. Prohibition on Political Involvement in the Distribution of Cash and Other Forms of Financial Assistance. All cash assistance                                      30
31   and other forms of financial aid distributions shall be conducted exclusively by authorized government officers and personnel or accredited partners.                               31
32           No public officials holding elective positions, electoral candidates, politicians, political parties, or any of their representatives, except for officials having direct   32
33   administrative and executive authority over the implementing agency, shall influence, be present in, participate in, or take part in the actual distribution of any cash            33
34   assistance and other forms of financial aid in the following programs: Protective Services for Individuals and Families in Difficult Circumstances, Tulong Panghanapbuhay           34
35   sa Ating Disadvantaged/Displaced Workers, Medical Assistance to Indigent and Financially-Incapacitated Patients Program, and other similar government financial                     35
36   assistance programs.                                                                                                                                                                36
37         No political signage, branding, paraphernalia, or activity shall be displayed or conducted within the distribution area.                                                      37
38          The national government agencies responsible for distributing cash assistance and other forms of financial aid shall establish, formulate, adopt, and enforce                38
39   mandatory requirements, protocols, and reporting mechanisms to ensure strict compliance with this policy.                                                                           39
40         The Joint Congressional Oversight Committee on Public Expenditures shall monitor agencies' compliance with the requirements of this General Provision.                        40
41           Sec. 21. Prohibition on the Display and/or Affixture of the Name, Image, and Likeness of Public Officials on Government Projects.                                           41
42   The display and/or affixture of the name, picture, image, motto, logo, color motif, initials, or other symbol or graphic representation associated with any public official,        42
43   whether elected or appointed, on signboards for all programs, activities, and projects funded under this Act shall be considered as unnecessary pursuant to COA Circular            43
44   No. 2013-004 dated January 30, 2013, as amended, and therefore, prohibited.                                                                                                         44
45           Sec. 22. Strict Adherence to Procurement Laws, Rules, and Regulations. All agencies of the government shall strictly adhere to the provisions of                            45
46   existing government procurement laws, rules, and regulations in the procurement of goods, infrastructure projects, and consulting services.                                         46
47          To promote transparency and achieve efficiency in the procurement process, the Philippine Government Electronic Procurement System (PhilGEPS) shall be the                   47
48   primary source of information and channel in the conduct of all procurement activities of the government.                                                                           48
49         Sec. 23. Early Procurement Activities. For goods to be delivered, infrastructure projects to be implemented, and consulting services to be rendered in the                    49
50   following fiscal year, agencies are authorized to undertake early procurement activities as soon as the proposed national budget is submitted to Congress. However,                 50
51   agencies may only proceed with the issuance of notice of award of contract upon approval or enactment of their respective appropriations and issuance of budget                     51
52   authorization document and based on the amount authorized therein.                                                                                                                  52
53         For foreign-assisted projects, agencies may undertake early procurement activities in accordance with R.A. No. 12009 and guidelines issued by the GPPB.                       53
54         Sec. 24. Procurement of Common-Use Supplies and Equipment. Consistent with Section 40 of R.A. No. 12009 and its IRR, all national government                                  54
55   agencies, GOCCS, GFIs, SUCS, and LGUs shall procure their common-use supplies and equipment from the Procurement Service-DBM (PS-DBM), subject to availability. In                  55
56   case of unavailability of stock or for purposes of efficiency, practicality, and/or economic viability, procuring entities may procure their common-use supplies and                56
57   equipment from other sources, subject to guidelines issued by the GPPB.                                                                                                             57
58         Common-Use Supplies and Equipment shall refer to goods, materials, and equipment that are used repetitively in the day-to-day operations of procuring entities in the         58
59   performance of their functions which are included in the Electronic Catalogue of the PhilGEPS.                                                                                      59

 1         The PhilGEPS Virtual Store and Electronic Marketplace shall be utilized for the procurement of common- use supplies and equipment, subject to existing procurement           1

 3         Sec. 25. Printing Expenditures. All agencies of the government shall engage the services of the National Printing Office, BSP, and APO Production Unit as                    3
 4   Recognized Government Printers (RGPs) for the printing of accountable forms and sensitive, high quality or high volume requirements, subject to the following:                     4

 7              certification by the RGPs that they are unable to service the said requirements. Said engagement of private printers shall be in accordance with existing               7
 8              government procurement laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                                                    8

10   Technology (ICT) equipment shall be used for the provision of personal computers inclusive of operating systems, basic software and other essential electronic devices to         10
11   their respective officials and employees. Said ICT equipment, if included in the electronic catalogue of the PhilGEPS, shall be procured exclusively from the PS-DBM as           11
12   common-use supplies and equipment in accordance with R.A. No. 12009.                                                                                                              12

22   for ICT requirements shall be used in accordance with the agency's Information Systems Strategic Plan and other issuances of the MITHI Steering Committee.                        22
23         Sec. 29. Inventory of Supplies, Materials, and Equipment Spare Parts. The inventory of supplies, materials, and equipment spare parts to be procured                        23
24   shall not exceed the agency's two-month requirement.                                                                                                                              24
25         The head of agencies may increase their inventory of critical supplies, materials and equipment spare parts to be procured in any of the following instances: (i) in        25
26   anticipation of cost increases; (ii) necessitated by a national emergency: (i) when there is an impending shortage; and (iv) when otherwise authorized in this Act or in the      26
27   charter of the agency concerned. The purchase of stocks exceeding an agency's one-year requirement shall be subject to approval by the President of the Philippines,              27
28   upon the joint recommendation of the Chairperson of the COA and the agency head concerned.                                                                                        28
29         Sec. 30. Implementation of Infrastructure Projects. The following requirements shall be observed in the implementation of infrastructure projects:                          29
30         (a) The location, areas or sites of all infrastructure projects are not included in the critical geo-hazard areas or no build zones identified or certified by the Mines    30
31              and Geosciences Bureau;                                                                                                                                                31
32         (b) The standards of construction, rehabilitation, improvement or repair of all infrastructure projects in all areas and zones, including the standards on rehabilitation   32
33              or construction of government buildings or office spaces, and the acquisition or outright purchase of lots and buildings, are consistent with the pertinent rules      33
34              and regulations determined by the DPWH and/or other relevant agencies, which shall consider, among others, the structural strength and climate and disaster            34
35              resilience required for infrastructure projects in all areas and zones;                                                                                                35
36         (c) The planning and construction of all infrastructure projects to be implemented within the National Integrated Protected Area System are done in a way that              36
37              eliminates or minimizes the risk of biodiversity loss while the specifications thereon are in accordance with those determined by the DPWH, in coordination with       37
38              the DENR. Major infrastructure projects may only be undertaken in said areas if intended to enhance biodiversity. The DPWH shall consider climate data and             38
39              risk assessment and green building standards in the planning, designing, construction, engineering, and renovation of government buildings and facilities;             39
40         (d) For foreign-assisted projects and infrastructure projects utilizing government-managed Official Development Assistance funds, the implementing agencies shall           40
41              ensure that technical knowledge for the application and implementation of relevant processes, including the technologies required for such application and             41
42              implementation, for the operation, maintenance, and further development of such projects, shall be systematically transferred to the government: Provided , That       42
43              such technology transfer agreements shall abide by any and all relevant laws, rules, and regulations; and                                                              43
44         (e) In accordance with the General Provision on the Use of Government Funds under this Act, all heads of agencies of the government are responsible for all                 44
45              government funds and property pertaining to their agencies.                                                                                                            45
46          Sec. 31. Installation of Rainwater Collection System. Rainwater collection system (RWCS) shall be installed in public markets, school sites, and                           46
47   government buildings and sites as an adaptation measure to combat climate change and to ensure sufficient water supply, which shall be in accordance with the                     47
48   prescribed design of DPWH. In no case shall the RWCS be constructed in private lots or privately-owned or operated market places.                                                 48
49         Sec. 32. Certification of Availability of Funds. No obligations chargeable against any authorized allotment shall be incurred by departments, bureaus, and                  49
50   offices of the National Government, including Constitutional Offices enjoying fiscal autonomy, SUCS, GOCCS, and LGUs, without first securing a certification of availability      50
51   of funds (CAF) for the purpose from the agency Chief Accountant, subject to Section 40, Chapter 5, and Section 58, Chapter 7, Book VI of E.O. No. 292. The CAF sufficient         51
52   to cover the cost of the contracted activities shall be contained in, and made part of, the contract duly signed by the Chief Accountant of the contracting agency.               52
53         For multi-year projects, the CAF shall be issued annually based on the budget for the year. In case of multi-year projects with no funding requirement on any given         53
54   year, instead of the CAF, the Chief Accountant shall issue a certification that no fund is needed for the year, as indicated in the approved multi-year contractual               54
55   authority (MYCA).                                                                                                                                                                 55
56         Sec. 33. Multi-Year Contracts. The issuance of a MYCA or any similar document shall be required before agencies may enter into multi-year contracts, subject                56
57   to the requirements and guidelines prescribed by the DBM: Provided , That for foreign-assisted projects funded by foreign loans, the issuance of a MYCA shall no longer be        57
58   necessary.                                                                                                                                                                        58
                                                                                                                                               GENERAL PROVISIONS 611



 1         In the procurement of multi-year projects, the MYCA or any similar document shall be required prior to commencement of any procurement activity.                           1
 2         In the case of GOCCs, they shall secure prior authority from their respective governing boards before entering into multi-year contracts.                                  2
 3         For LGUs, they shall secure any equivalent document issued by their respective sanggunian authorizing them to enter into multi-year contracts.                             3
 4         For the multi-year PPP projects with government undertakings authorized under R.A. No. 11966, the same shall be covered by a letter of commitment (LOC) issued in          4
 5   accordance with the guidelines issued by the DBM.                                                                                                                                5
 6          The implementing agency shall ensure that the annual funding requirements for the multi-year projects shall be included in its budget proposals for the covered           6
 7   years, consistent with the funding schedule in the MYCA and equivalent authorities, and LOC. In the case of national government agencies and qualified GOCCs, the DBM            7
 8   shall ensure that the funding requirement for the multi-year projects are included in the National Expenditure Program to be submitted to Congress who shall give due            8
 9   consideration of the said proposal. In the case of GOCCs and LGUs, due consideration shall be given by the governing board of GOCCs and the sanggunian of the LGUs,              9
10   respectively.                                                                                                                                                                   10
11   In all instances, the disbursements to be incurred for multi-year contracts shall in no case exceed the cash appropriations for the purpose during the year. Procurement of     11
12   multi-year projects shall be subject to the provisions of existing government procurement laws, rules, and regulations.                                                         12
13        Sec. 34. Harmonized National Research and Development Agenda. All government agencies shall align their research and development agenda programs                           13
14   under the Harmonized National Research and Development Agenda for funding amounting to Ten Million Pesos (P10,000,000) and above.                                               14
15          The DOST, in coordination with government research institutions and other agencies, shall facilitate dissemination of all output programs and projects under the         15
16   Harmonized National Research and Development Agenda to appropriate government agencies, LGUs, academe, industry and communities, whenever applicable.                           16
17         A copy of the progress report shall also be submitted to the Speaker of the House of Representatives, President of the Senate of the Philippines, House Committee on      17
18   Appropriations, and Senate Committee on Finance, either in printed form or by way of electronic document.                                                                       18
19         Sec. 35. Programs and Projects Related to Gender and Development. All agencies of the government shall formulate a Gender and Development (GAD)                           19
20   Plan designed to address gender issues within their concerned sectors or mandate and implement the applicable provisions under R.A. No. 9710, Convention on the                 20
21   Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, the Beijing Platform for Action, the Philippine Plan for Gender-Responsive Development (1995-2025), and the           21
22   Philippine Development Plan (2023-2028).                                                                                                                                        22
23          The GAD Plan shall be integrated in the regular activities of the agencies, which shall be at least five percent (5%) of their budgets. For this purpose, activities     23
24   currently being undertaken by agencies which relate to GAD or those that contribute to poverty alleviation, economic empowerment especially of marginalized women,              24
25   protection, promotion, and fulfilment of women's human rights, and practice of gender-responsive governance are considered sufficient compliance with said requirement.         25
26   Utilization of GAD budget shall be evaluated based on the GAD performance indicators identified by said agencies.                                                               26
27        The annual GAD Plan and Budget and the Annual GAD Accomplishment Report shall be prepared in accordance with the guidelines issued by the Philippine Commission            27
28   on Women (PCW) and other concerned agencies.                                                                                                                                    28
29          Sec. 36. Gender and Development Budget Tagging. All national government agencies, SUCS, GOCCS, and LGUS shall tag their GAD Budget and the                               29
30   utilization thereof by submitting the Annual GAD Plan and Budget and the Annual GAD Accomplishment Report, respectively, to the PCW and the DBM through the Gender              30
31   Mainstreaming Monitoring System (GMMS).                                                                                                                                         31
32          The data from the submitted reports shall be used in the development of a Gender Financing Framework, to be undertaken by the PCW, which shall serve as a                32
33   roadmap to the Philippine compliance with the international standards of GAD Budgeting.                                                                                         33
34          The DBM shall create an enabling Public Financial Management System which shall support the GAD Budget Tagging initiative. The implementation of the system              34
35   shall be subject to the guidelines to be issued jointly by the PCW and the DBM.                                                                                                 35
36          Sec. 37. Programs and Projects Related to Senior Citizens and Persons with Disability. All agencies of the government shall formulate plans,                             36
37   programs, and projects intended to address the concerns of senior citizens and persons with disability, insofar as it relates to their mandated functions, and integrate the    37
38   same in their regular activities.                                                                                                                                               38
39          Moreover, all government infrastructures and facilities shall provide architectural or structural features, designs or facilities that will reasonably enhance the       39
40   mobility, safety, and welfare of persons with disability pursuant to Batas Pambansa Blg. 344 and R.A. No. 7277, as amended.                                                     40
41          All national agencies, GOCCS and LGUS shall provide qualified Filipino sign language interpreters and accessible materials for all public transactions, services and     41
42   facilities involving the deaf, whenever necessary or requested, in accordance with R.A. No. 11106.                                                                              42
43          Sec. 38. Projects Related to the Youth. All agencies of the government are encouraged to provide allocations for youth development projects and activities               43
44   within the framework of the Philippine Youth Development Plan (2023-2028).                                                                                                      44
45          Sec. 39. Institutional Linkage with the National Cultural Agencies. In the implementation of their activities or projects authorized in this Act,                        45
46   agencies identified under Section 32 of R.A. No. 10066, as amended, shall consult, coordinate, and work closely with the National Commission for Culture and the Arts           46
47   (NCCA) to ensure that their respective responsibilities embodied under the said law are implemented.                                                                            47
48         Sec. 40. Protection of Built Heritage, Cultural Properties, and Cultural Landscapes. Alteration, renovation, demolition of government buildings and                       48
49   open spaces declared or presumed to be important cultural properties by government cultural agencies concerned shall be undertaken only upon prior approval of the said         49
50   government cultural agencies and proper consultation with stakeholders and cultural groups to be administered by the NCCA. This includes the protection of the sight line       50
51   with regard to built heritage, cultural properties, and cultural landscapes.                                                                                                    51
52         In addition, the DPWH shall be responsible in the planning, design, construction, and maintenance of national roads and bridges as they impact on heritage structures     52
53   or aspects of heritage conservation pursuant to R.A. No. 10066, as amended.                                                                                                     53
54          Sec. 41. Disaster Risk Reduction and Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation Measures Incorporated in All Agencies Projects and                                         54
55   Activities. All agencies of the government including LGUs, SUCS, and GOCCs should implement projects incorporating risk reduction, climate change adaptation, and               55
56   where feasible, climate change mitigation.                                                                                                                                      56
57          To ensure that the disaster risk reduction and climate change adaptation measures are appropriate in the light of intensifying hazards, all national government          57
58   projects should be subjected to multi-scenario probabilistic analysis. For this purpose, the CCC shall extend the necessary technical and capacity building assistance in the   58
59   conduct of risk assessment, as well as adaptation and mitigation planning.                                                                                                      59
     612 GENERAL APPROPRIATIONS BILL, FY 2027



 1         Agencies shall likewise integrate energy efficiency and conservation measures and consider climate resilience in the planning and implementation of all infrastructure           1
 2   projects, office programs, and activities, as well as assess their organizational carbon footprint and pursue appropriate emission reduction measure to achieve net zero               2
 3   emissions, to mitigate and adapt to the effects of climate change pursuant to the provisions of R.A. No. 9729, as amended.                                                             3
 4         Sec. 42. Disaster Risk Budget Tagging. All national government agencies, SUCS, GOCCS, and LGUs shall endeavor to tag their budgets relating to disaster risk                     4
 5   and resilience management and to submit periodic reports on the utilization thereof in the form to be prescribed by the DBM.                                                           5
 6          The data from the submitted reports shall guide the formulation of the succeeding budget to mainstream disaster risk and resilience management strategies in the                6
 7   national development process.                                                                                                                                                          7
 8          The DBM shall create an enabling Public Financial Management System which shall support the disaster risk budget tagging initiative. The implementation of the                  8
 9   system shall be subject to the guidelines to be issued jointly by the OCD and the DBM.                                                                                                 9
10         Sec. 43. Climate Budget Tagging. All national government agencies, SUCS, and GOCCs shall tag their budgets for climate change adaptation and mitigation in                      10
11   accordance with the DBM-CCC J.M.C. No. 2015- 01 dated March 24, 2015, and the LGUS shall tag their climate budget in their Annual Investment Plans pursuant to DBM-                   11
12   CCC-DILG J.M.C. No. 2015-01 dated July 23, 2015.                                                                                                                                      12
13         The DBM and CCC shall issue guidelines on the reporting of the utilization of the items tagged as climate change expenditures.                                                  13
14          The results of the budget tagging shall guide the formulation of subsequent budgets to mainstream climate change adaptation and mitigation strategies in the                   14
15   national development process.                                                                                                                                                         15
16          Sec. 44. Government Compliance to the Electric Vehicle Industry Development Act. All government entities (GEs), including national government                                  16
17   agencies, LGUS, GOCCS, Constitutional Offices enjoying fiscal autonomy, as well as the Legislative and Judicial branches, shall comply with R.A. No. 11697 and its IRR. All           17
18   GES shall ensure that at least five percent (5%) of their fleet, whether owned or leased, shall be electric vehicles within the time frame indicated in the Comprehensive             18
19   Roadmap for the Electric Vehicle Development Industry: Provided , That only recognized electric vehicles shall be purchased based on guidelines issued by the DOE and                 19
20   subject to the provisions of existing government procurement laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                            20
21          All GEs, through their head offices, shall inform the DOE of the new electric vehicle purchases for government use. GEs shall also ensure regular updating of their            21
22   fleets through the Government Energy Management Program (GEMP) online system.                                                                                                         22
23         Sec. 45. Energy Efficiency. All national government agencies, LGUs, and GOCCs shall comply with the GEMP, and existing laws, rules, and regulations on energy                   23
24   efficiency and conservation. These energy efficiency measures may include the (i) adoption of a standard thermostat level based on the DOE's energy conservation                      24
25   program; (ii) use of energy efficient lighting, such as light-emitting diode (LED) lamps, in their office buildings, school buildings, hospitals, markets, parks, street lights and   25
26   other public places; (iii) use of inverter type air-conditioning units or similar equivalent technologies in their office buildings, school buildings, hospitals, and similar         26
27   facilities; and (iv) adoption of flexible work arrangement, which may include the combination of a four (4)-day onsite work and one (1)-day uniform work from home                    27
28   arrangement, consistent with CSC M.C. No. 6 dated June 6, 2022, DBM-COA J.C. No. 1 dated September 13, 2022 and Inter-Agency Energy Efficiency and Conservation                       28
29   Committee Resolution No. 7, s. 2023, and other pertinent laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                                29
30         Sec. 46. Maintenance and Operation of Dams. As part of the disaster risk reduction program of the government, agencies and GOCCS that have control or                           30
31   supervision over the major dams shall ensure that said dams are properly maintained, managed, and operated with updated and promulgated protocols. The agencies and                   31
32   GOCCs concerned shall take into account climate change and extreme weather events and ensure coordination with the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and                            32
33   Astronomical Services Administration on precipitation forecast. They shall also establish and maintain an efficient and effective early flood warning system and functional           33
34   water level monitoring system that is periodically tested together with the LGUs and communities at risk of flooding from dam water releases.                                         34
35          Sec. 47. Multi-Hazard Impact-Based Forecasting and Early Warning Systems for Climate and Disaster Resilience. The National Government                                          35
36   shall promote the establishment of multi-hazard impact- based forecasting and early warning systems and services, including the development and enhancement of                        36
37   protocols for climate, weather, and risk communication, early warning dissemination, and implementation of early action procedures, to prevent and minimize loss and                  37
38   damage from impacts of extreme weather and slow onset events in communities. Such instrumentation, communication, and implementation protocols should be actionable                   38
39   and verifiable to the last mile, reaching the most vulnerable.                                                                                                                        39
40          Sec. 48. Protection of Biodiversity. All agencies of the government, including LGUS, SUCS, and GOCCS, shall support the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity                   40
41   Framework and its implementation through the Philippine Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan, and shall, where applicable, ensure that protection, conservation and                  41
42   restoration of biological diversity are integrated and mainstreamed in the planning and implementation of their respective programs and projects.                                     42
43          Sec. 49. Mainstreaming Green Practices. All national government agencies, LGUS, SUCS, and GOCCS shall, as much as possible, institute practices that                           43
44   promote the protection and conservation of the environment. Day-to-day operations of agencies shall be guided by principles directed towards sustainability and mitigation            44
45   of the effects of climate change.                                                                                                                                                     45
46          Agencies shall, in the implementation of their respective programs, activities, and projects, practice energy efficiency and conservation, recycling initiatives, and          46
47   explore alternative solutions that promote conservation of natural resources, such as the use of electronic and digital platforms for provision of resource materials.                47
48          Sec. 50. Implementation of Sustainable Practices in Government Operations. Departments, bureaus, offices, and instrumentalities of the National                                48
49   Government, including Constitutional Offices enjoying fiscal autonomy, SUCS, GOCCS, and LGUs, shall review their day-to-day operations and adopt necessary measures to                49
50   integrate sustainable practices and initiatives as applicable. These efforts aim to ensure that the government addresses the present needs without compromising the ability           50
51   of future generations to meet their own.                                                                                                                                              51
52         Agencies shall develop their respective Sustainability Strategic Plans in accordance with the guidelines to be issued by the DBM.                                               52
53         Sec. 51. Sustainable Development Goals, Resilience and Protection of the Environment. For the purpose of protecting the people and the planet,                                  53
54   the State must develop strategies to build resilience to achieve intergenerational fairness and ensure a better life for all, national government agencies, GOCCS, and LGUS           54
55   shall adopt measures to support the following:                                                                                                                                        55
56         (a) The 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development;                                                                                                                                56
57         (b) The Philippine Development Plan (PDP) 2023-2028;                                                                                                                            57
58         (c) The Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) of the Philippines;                                                                                                            58
                                                                                                                                              GENERAL PROVISIONS 613



 1         (d) The NDC Implementation Plan 2020-2030 and Gender Action Plan 2024-2030 of the Philippines;                                                                            1
 2         (e) The National Adaptation Plan (NAP) of the Philippines 2023-2050;                                                                                                      2
 3         (f) The Philippine Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan 2024-2040;                                                                                                       3
 4         (g) Monitoring and evaluation of programs, projects, and activities consistent with the applicable Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) indicators and targets; and        4
 5         (h) SDG mapping and alignment of programs and expenditures.                                                                                                               5
 6         Sec. 52. Repair and Retrofitting of Government Structures. The government agencies concerned shall prioritize the repair and retrofitting of government                   6
 7   structures in areas considered highly vulnerable to seismic activity and shall ensure that the retrofitting shall result in structural strength and energy efficiency in        7
 8   accordance with R.A. No. 10121, R.A. No. 11285, the National Structural Code of the Philippines, and other pertinent laws, rules, and regulations.                              8
 9         Sec. 53. Materials Recovery Facility. All government agencies shall establish a Materials Recovery Facility (MRF) in a suitable open space within the office              9
10   premises to promote environmental awareness and action. The design of the MRF shall be pursuant to the guidelines under R.A. No. 9003.                                         10
11         Sec. 54. Philippine Open Government Partnership. Departments, bureaus, offices, and instrumentalities of the National Government, including Constitutional               11
12   Offices enjoying fiscal autonomy, SUCS, GOCCS, and LGUs, shall adopt the open government partnership values of transparency. accountability, citizen participation, and        12
13   leveraging on technology in the implementation of their programs, activities, and projects, as institutionalized under E.O. No. 31, s. 2023.                                   13
14         The Philippine Open Government Partnership (PH-OGP) Steering Committee shall embed open government values in government policies and programs and promote                14
15   open and participatory governance through advocacy and outreach programs, activities, and projects. Funding for the implementation of the PH-OGP programs, activities,         15
16   and projects shall be in accordance with Section 7 of E.O. No. 31.                                                                                                             16
17         The implementation of this provision shall be consistent with E.O. No. 31, the strategies identified under the Philippine Development Plan (2023-2028), and the          17
18   applicable guidelines to be issued by the DBM, in coordination with other agencies concerned.                                                                                  18
19         Sec. 55. Use of Alternative Dispute Resolution. Pursuant to Section 2 of R.A. No. 9285, all government agencies shall continually promote and provide the                19
20   means for the use of Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) as an efficient tool and alternative procedure for the resolution of appropriate cases to achieve speedy and         20
21   impartial justice and declog court dockets, including the enlistment of active private sector participation in the settlement of disputes.                                     21
22         Agencies in the Executive branch, including departments, administrative offices, quasi-judicial bodies, and GOCCS, shall develop, fund, implement, and report ADR        22
23   programs in accordance with their respective administrative and regulatory functions and external and internal services, and E.O. No. 97, s. 2012 and applicable issuances     23
24   of the DOJ, the Office for Alternative Dispute Resolution, and other concerned agencies.                                                                                       24

28         Sec. 56. Employment of Contractual Personnel. Contractual personnel may be hired by agencies as part of their organization in order to perform agency                    28
29   functions or specific vital activities or services which cannot be provided by the regular or permanent staff of the hiring agency, subject to compliance with the             29
30   organizational, staffing and compensation standards set by DBM. The total annual Personnel Services requirement for contractual personnel, to cover salaries, and other        30
31   personnel benefits and fixed expenditures, shall in no case exceed the lump-sum appropriations for the purpose, except when there is an urgent need to hire contractual        31
32   personnel in the implementation of the priority activities or projects, subject to approval of the DBM. In which case, the payment for contractual personnel shall be          32
33   sourced from the Miscellaneous Personnel Benefits Fund.                                                                                                                        33
34         Contractual personnel shall be considered as an employee of the hiring agency but only during the period when their services are reasonably required. Existing           34
35   qualified contractual employees shall be considered by the government agencies for appointment to their vacant positions, subject to existing civil service laws, rules, and   35
36   regulations, as well as the CSC-approved Merit Selection Plan of agencies concerned.                                                                                           36

 5         Sec. 58. Cultural and Athletic Activities. An amount not exceeding One Thousand Five Hundred Pesos (P1,500) in a year, may be used for the purchase of                      5
 6   uniform or costume and other related expenses in the conduct of cultural and athletic activities per employee-participant.                                                        6
 7         Sec. 59. Funding of Personnel Benefits. Notwithstanding any provision of law to the contrary, all personnel benefits costs of government personnel shall be                 7
 8   charged against the same funding source from which their salaries are drawn. In cases where personnel benefits costs are funded partly from the General Fund and partly           8
 9   from other sources, only the portion corresponding to the General Fund shall be charged for the payment of retirement benefits, terminal leave benefits and pensions.             9
10         In no case shall personnel benefits costs drawn from Special Accounts, Trust Funds or other funding sources be charged against the General Fund of the National            10
11   Government.                                                                                                                                                                      11
12         The personnel benefits costs of officials and employees detailed to other offices, including representatives and support personnel of auditing units assigned to serve     12
13   other offices or agencies, shall be charged against the appropriations of their parent agencies, unless otherwise authorized by the DBM.                                         13
14         Personnel benefits costs shall include salary increases, step increments, all kinds of authorized allowances, benefits and incentives, monetized vacation and sick leave   14
15   credits, government contributions for retirement and life insurance premiums, employees' compensation insurance premiums, health insurance premiums, Home Development            15
16   Mutual Fund (HDMF) contributions, and other authorized benefits.                                                                                                                 16
17         Sec. 60. Appropriations for Personnel Services. The appropriations for Personnel Services under this Act shall be used for the payment of personnel                        17
18   benefits authorized by law to be given to National Government personnel. Any available allotment for Personnel Services within a department or agency may be utilized            18
19   by said department or agency for the payment of deficiencies in authorized personnel benefits.                                                                                   19
20         Implementation of this Section shall be subject to guidelines issued by the DBM.                                                                                           20
21        Sec. 61. Remittance of Compulsory Contributions. The government and employee shares in the compulsory contributions to the Employees' Compensation                          21
22   Commission, PhilHealth, GSIS, and HDMF pursuant to P.D. No. 626, as amended, R.A. No. 6111, R.A. No. 7875, as amended, R.A. No. 8291, and R.A. No. 9679, respectively,           22
23   shall be remitted directly by departments, bureaus, and offices of the National Government, including Constitutional Offices enjoying fiscal autonomy and SUCs to the            23
24   respective recipient agencies unless a different arrangement is agreed upon in writing between the DBM and the recipient agency.                                                 24
25         Any proposed increase in government and employee compulsory contributions may only be implemented after consultation by the agency concerned with the DBM in               25
26   order that the budgetary implications of such proposal be duly considered. The implementation of any increase in government and employee compulsory contributions, after         26
27   said consultation, shall be made effective only upon inclusion thereof in an appropriations law.                                                                                 27
28         Sec. 62. Authorized Deductions. Deductions from salaries and other benefits accruing to any government employee, chargeable against the appropriations for                 28
29   Personnel Services, may be allowed for the payment of an individual employee's contributions or obligations due the following:                                                   29
30         (a) The BIR, PhilHealth, GSIS, and HDMF;                                                                                                                                   30
31         (b) The National Government, as decreed in a final and executory decision of COA;                                                                                          31

33              the benefit of government employees;                                                                                                                                  33
34         (d) Associations or Provident Funds organized and managed by government employees for their benefit and welfare;                                                           34
35         (e) GFls and authorized government depository banks authorized by law and accredited by appropriate government regulating bodies to engage in lending;                     35
36         (f) Licensed insurance companies; and                                                                                                                                      36
37         (g) Thrift banks or rural banks accredited by the BSP.                                                                                                                     37
38         Obligations due the BIR and contributions to PhilHealth, GSIS, and HDMF shall be satisfied ahead of all other obligations. The remaining obligations due the other         38
39   entities listed above shall be satisfied in the order in which they were incurred.                                                                                               39
40         In no case shall the foregoing deductions reduce the employee's monthly net take home pay to an amount lower than Five Thousand Pesos (P5,000).                            40
41         Sec. 63. Personnel Economic Relief Allowance. In order to supplement the salaries of government personnel covered by R.A. No. 6758, as amended,                            41
42   Personnel Economic Relief Allowance (PERA), in the amount of Two Thousand Pesos (P2,000) per month, is granted to the following:                                                 42
43         (a) Civilian government personnel stationed in the Philippines, whether occupying regular, contractual or casual positions, appointive or elective; and                    43
44         (b) Military and uniformed personnel.                                                                                                                                      44
45         Government personnel stationed abroad shall be granted overseas allowances to defray the cost of their living expenses and shall no longer be entitled to receive          45
46   PERA for the duration of their station abroad.                                                                                                                                   46
47         The grant of PERA shall be subject to the rules and regulations prescribed under B.C. No. 2009-3 dated August 18, 2009, as amended, and such other guidelines              47
48   issued by the DBM or by the GCG for GOCCs/GFIs covered by R.A. No. 10149.                                                                                                        48

50   or clothing allowance to each qualified government employee, subject to B.C. No. 2024-1 dated April 4, 2024, and such other guidelines issued by the DBM.                        50
51          Sec. 65. Medical Allowance for the Availment of Health Maintenance Organization (HMO)-type Benefit. An amount not exceeding Seven                                         51
52   Thousand Pesos (P7,000) per year is hereby authorized for the grant of Medical Allowance as subsidy to qualified government employees for the availment of HMO-type              52
53   benefits, subject to B.C. No. 2024-6 dated December 12, 2024, and such other the guidelines issued by the DBM.                                                                   53

55   researchers, and other science and technology personnel in the government shall be subject to the guidelines of the DBM.                                                         55

11        Sec. 69. Night Shift Differential Pay. Night shift differential pay at a rate not exceeding twenty percent (20%) of the hourly basic rate of the employee, as              11

18        Sec. 70. Honoraria. Honoraria may be paid only to the following:                                                                                                           18
19        (a) Teaching personnel of the DepEd, TESDA, SUCs, and other educational institutions, engaged in actual classroom teaching, whose teaching load is outside of the          19
20             regular office hours or in excess of the regular load;                                                                                                                20
21        (b) Those who act as lecturers, resource persons, coordinators and facilitators in seminars, training programs, and other similar activities in training institutions;     21
22        (c) Chairpersons and members of commissions, boards, councils, and other similar entities, including personnel thereof who are not paid salaries nor per diems but         22
23             compensated in the form of honoraria as provided by laws, rules, and regulations;                                                                                     23
24        (d) Those who are involved in science and technological activities and render services beyond their regular workload; and                                                  24

26             (i) Said special projects are reform-oriented or developmental, contribute to the improvement of service delivery and enhancement of the performance of the           26

28             (ii) Such assignment entails rendition of work in addition to, or over and above, their regular workload. In these instances, the rates of honoraria shall depend     28
29                   on the level of responsibilities, nature of work rendered, and extent of individual contribution to produce the desired outputs. The total honoraria received   29
30                   from all special projects shall not exceed twenty five percent (25%) of the annual basic salaries; and                                                          30
31             (iii) Officials and employees authorized to receive honoraria under existing government procurement laws, rules, and regulations.                                     31

33   dated April 23, 2007 and N.B.C. No. 2007-510 dated May 8, 2007, B.C. No. 2007-2 dated October 1, 2007, B.C. No. 2004-5A dated October 7, 2005, as amended by B.C. No.           33
34   2007-3 dated November 29, 2007, DBM-DOST J.C. No. 1 dated June 25, 2013, and such other guidelines issued by the DBM.                                                           34

19   concerned.                                                                                                                                                                  19

22         Sec. 74. Mid-year Bonus. The Mid-year Bonus equivalent to one (1) month basic salary, shall be granted to all National Government personnel, whether under            22
23   regular, temporary, casual, or contractual status, on full-time or part-time basis, subject to the following:                                                               23
24         (a) Personnel have rendered at least a total or an aggregate of four (4) months of service from July 1 of the immediately preceding year to May 15 of the current     24
25              year and who are still in the government service as of May 15 of the current year;                                                                               25
26         (b) Personnel have obtained at least a satisfactory performance rating in the immediately preceding rating period; and                                                26
27         (c) The provisions of R.A. No. 11466 dated January 8, 2020, B.C. No. 2017-2 dated May 8, 2017, B.C. No. 2019-4 dated July 5, 2019, and such other guidelines issued   27

29         Personnel of GOCCs covered by the Compensation and Position Classification System (CPCS) under R.A. No. 6758, as amended, and LGUs are likewise entitled to Mid-      29
30   year Bonus chargeable against their respective corporate and local funds.                                                                                                   30
31         Sec. 75. Year-end Bonus and Cash Gift. The Year-end Bonus equivalent to one (1) month basic salary and additional Cash Gift of Five Thousand Pesos                    31
32   (P5,000) provided under R.A. No. 6686, as amended by R.A. No. 8441, shall be granted to all National Government personnel, whether under regular, temporary, casual, or     32
33   contractual status, on full-time or part-time basis, subject to the following:                                                                                              33
34         (a) At least a total of four (4) months of service including leaves of absence with pay from January 1 to October 31 have been rendered during the current year,      34
35              and who are still in the service by October 31 of the same year;                                                                                                 35
36         (b) Those who have rendered at least a total or an aggregate of four (4) months of service from January 1 of the current year but who have retired or separated       36
37              from government service before October 31 of the same year shall be granted within the month of retirement or separation, a prorated share of the Year-end       37
38              Bonus based on the monthly basic pay immediately preceding the date of retirement or separation and a Cash Gift of P5,000; and                                   38
39         (c) The provisions of B.C. No. 2016-4 dated April 28, 2016, as amended by B.C. No. 2024-3 dated October 22, 2024, and such other guidelines issued by the DBM.        39

41   respective corporate and local funds.                                                                                                                                       41

45   retirement laws, rules, and regulations.                                                                                                                                    45
