13        Sec. 78. Suspension of Expenditure. The President is authorized to suspend or otherwise stop further expenditure of funds allotted for any agency, or any                       13
14   other expenditure authorized in this Act, except for Personnel Services, under the Executive branch, when any of the following conditions are present: (i) when public               14
15   interest so requires; or (ii) when there is unmanageable National Government budget deficit.                                                                                         15
16         Unmanageable National Government budget deficit as used in this Section shall be construed to mean that: (i) the actual National Government budget deficit has                 16
17   exceeded the quarterly budget deficit targets consistent with the full-year target deficit as indicated in the BESF submitted by the President and approved by Congress              17
18   pursuant to Section 22, Article VII of the Constitution; or (ii) there are clear economic indications of an impending occurrence of such condition, as determined by the             18
19   DBCC and approved by the President.                                                                                                                                                  19
20         Implementation of this provision shall be in accordance with the guidelines to be issued by the DOF, in coordination with the DBM.                                             20
21         Sec. 79. Prohibition Against Retention or Deduction of Funds. Fund releases from appropriations provided in this Act shall be transmitted to the                               21
22   agency concerned, subject to the General Provisions on the General Appropriations Act as the Allotment Order under this Act, applicable special and general provisions,              22
23   and budgeting rules and regulations. No retention or deduction as reserves or overhead shall be made, except as authorized by law, the general or special provisions in              23
24   this Act.                                                                                                                                                                            24
25         Sec. 80. Direct Release of Funds to Regional Offices and Operating Units. Funds appropriated in this Act shall be released directly to the Regional                            25
26   Offices (ROs) and Operating Units (OUs) of agencies where funds are specifically appropriated to the ROs and OUs of agencies, except non-implementing units.                         26
27         Sec. 81. Lump-Sum Appropriations. Release of lump-sum appropriations shall be made upon compliance with the requirements under the applicable general                          27
28   and/or special provisions and submission by the agency concerned of a budget request, and other relevant budgetary requirements in accordance with applicable laws,                  28
29   rules, and regulations. The budget request shall include the complete details of the activities or projects covering the lump-sum appropriations with the corresponding cost         29
30   up to the lowest level, i.e., provincial, city or municipal level, as the case may be.                                                                                               30
31         Sec. 82. Fund Transfers to Civil Society Organizations. A government agency may transfer public funds to a Civil Society Organization (CSO) only if all                        31
32   of the following conditions are present:                                                                                                                                             32
33         (a) The CSO is either:                                                                                                                                                         33
34              (i) implementing a government program or project jointly with the government agency; or                                                                                   34
35              (ii) a beneficiary of a government program or project.                                                                                                                    35
36         (b) There is an appropriation in the GAA or some other appropriation law for such government program or project.                                                               36
37         (c) The government agency has accredited the CSO in accordance with its guidelines. The guidelines shall include, as a minimum, the following requirements:                    37
38              (i) The presence of the CSO in its stated address and area of operation has been validated;                                                                               38
39              (ii) The CSO has an identified membership and leadership and defined organizational structure;                                                                            39
40              (iii) The CSO is in good standing with all government agencies from which the CSO has received public funds;                                                              40
41              (iv) The CSO is not in default or in delay in liquidating any public funds received from any government agency;                                                           41
42              (v) For implementing CSOs, the CSO must have a proven track record and good standing in undertaking civil society works; the CSO must not have any                        42
43                    Director, Trustee, Officer or key personnel related within the fourth civil degree of consanguinity or affinity to any official involved in the processing of its   43
44                    accreditation, or any official of the government agency funding or implementing the program or project to be implemented by the CSO; and the CSO must               44
45                    have proven legal existence; and                                                                                                                                    45
46              (vi) For beneficiary CSOs, the CSO must have the appropriate social preparation from the government agency providing the grant of financial assistance.                   46
47              In case of a cooperative who wishes to become a CSO partner, the submission of certificate of registration and certificate of compliance as issued by the                 47
48              Cooperative Development Authority specifically for that purpose including meeting the minimum requirements as stated herein shall be sufficient for it to qualify         48
49              as a CSO partner.                                                                                                                                                         49
50              Government agencies shall post the lists of their accredited CSOs in their respective websites, and shall update such lists quarterly.                                    50
51              A government agency may opt to consider a CSO accredited by another government agency as deemed accredited for its purpose.                                               51
52         (d) The CSO has liquidated in accordance with existing COA regulations all fund transfers due for liquidation. Only CSOs with proven absorptive capacity and good              52
53              track records to implement several projects at the same time shall be considered as implementing CSO of multiple projects.                                                53
54         (e) The CSO was selected by the government agency in accordance with existing government procurement laws, rules, and regulations.                                             54
55         To ensure the CSOs comply with all pertinent rules and regulations covering the transfer, use, liquidation, and audit of public funds, government agencies shall put           55
56   into place the needed monitoring, evaluation, and reporting mechanisms. Government agencies shall remain accountable for funds transferred to CSOs in accordance with                56
57   government accounting and auditing rules and regulations.                                                                                                                            57

 5          Sec. 83. Authority to Use Savings. The President of the Philippines, the President of the Senate of the Philippines, the Speaker of the House of                            5
 6   Representatives, the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court, the Heads of the CSC, the COMELEC, and the COA are hereby authorized to augment a deficiency in any existing              6
 7   item of their respective appropriations in this Act.                                                                                                                               7
 8         The foregoing constitutional officers authorized to use savings shall be responsible for ensuring that a semestral and annual report on their respective use of savings      8
 9   shall be submitted to the President of the Senate of the Philippines and the Speaker of the House of Representatives, copy furnished the DBM. The report shall indicate,           9
10   among others, the amount of savings generated, the sources and grounds used therefor, and the existing program, activity, or project in their respective appropriations           10
11   augmented. They shall likewise ensure that said reports are posted on their respective websites.                                                                                  11
12         Sec. 84. Meaning of Savings. Savings refer to portions or balances of any released appropriations in this Act which have not been obligated as a result of                  12
13   any of the following:                                                                                                                                                             13
14         (a) Completion, final discontinuance, or abandonment of a program, activity, or project for which the appropriation is authorized; or                                       14
15         (b) Implementation of measures resulting in improved systems and efficiencies and thus enabled an agency to meet and deliver the required or planned targets,               15
16              programs, and services approved in this Act at a lesser cost.                                                                                                          16
17         In case final discontinuance or abandonment is used as basis in the declaration of savings, such discontinued or abandoned program, activity, or project shall no           17
18   longer be proposed for funding in the next two (2) fiscal years; Provided, That this prohibition shall not apply to programs, activities, or projects discontinued or             18
19   abandoned due to the declaration of a state of national emergency or any similar declaration.                                                                                     19
20         Allotments that were not obligated due to the fault of the agency concerned shall not be considered savings.                                                                20
21         Sec. 85. Rules on Augmentation. Augmentation is the act of the constitutional officers authorized to use savings in their respective appropriations in this Act             21
22   to cover a deficiency in any existing item of appropriation within their respective offices. A deficiency in an item of appropriation may result from:                            22
23         (a) Unforeseen modifications or adjustments in the program, activity, or project; or                                                                                        23
24         (b) Re-assessment in the use, prioritization, and/or distribution of resources.                                                                                             24
25         An item of appropriation shall pertain to the amount appropriated for an activity or project authorized in this Act.                                                        25
26         The particulars of the expenditures to be funded from savings should be within the scope of, or covered by, an existing activity or project. The existence of an            26
27   activity or project regardless of the availability of allotment class/es is sufficient for the purpose of augmentation.                                                           27
28         In no case shall a non-existent activity or project be funded by augmentation from savings or by the use of appropriations authorized in this Act.                          28
29         Sec. 86. Priority in the Use of Savings. In the use of savings, priority shall be given to the payment of compensation, Year-end Bonus and Cash Gift,                       29
30   retirement gratuity, terminal leave benefits, old-age pension of veterans, and other personnel benefits authorized by law, as well the implementation of programs,                30
31   activities, or projects that address and respond to natural or human-induced disasters and calamities covered in this Act.                                                        31
32         Sec. 87. Rules on Modification in the Allotment. As a general rule, departments, bureaus and offices of the National Government, including Constitutional                   32
33   Offices enjoying fiscal autonomy, and SUCs shall spend what is programmed in their respective appropriations in this Act. In exceptional circumstances, agencies may              33
34   modify the allotment issued within an activity or project subject to approval of the following ensued by the timely submission of reports by all offices concerned:               34
35         (a) The heads of agencies or their duly authorized representatives who shall be the official next-in-rank, for the following: (i) change in the details of an activity or   35
36              project without changing its nature and within the same operating unit; and (ii) change in the object of expenditure (travelling expenses or investment outlays)       36
37              within an allotment class (MOOE or Capital Outlays);                                                                                                                   37
38         (b) The DBM, from one allotment class to another; and                                                                                                                       38
39         (c) The President of the Philippines, for the payment of intelligence funds within the Executive branch.                                                                    39
40         All modifications in the allotment shall not entail any increase in the total amount appropriated for an activity or project.                                               40
41         Sec. 88. Rules in the Grant of Collective Negotiation Agreement Incentive. Departments, bureaus, and offices of the National Government, including                          41
42   Constitutional Offices enjoying fiscal autonomy, and SUCs may grant Collective Negotiation Agreement (CNA) Incentive sourced from the allowable MOOE allotments                   42
43   identified by the DBM, subject to the following:                                                                                                                                  43
44         (a) There is a valid CNA executed between the agency and the recognized employee organization which includes a provision on cost-cutting measures to be                     44
45              undertaken collectively by the agency and its personnel;                                                                                                               45
46         (b) The one-time annual payment of CNA Incentive shall be made through a written resolution signed by agency representatives from both labor and management,                46
47              and approved by the agency head;                                                                                                                                       47
48         (c) The CNA Incentive that may be granted shall be limited to the amount determined by the DBM; and                                                                         48
49         (d) The use of MOOE for the payment of CNA Incentive shall be subject to approval by the agency head and made only during the validity of appropriations. Any               49
50              excess amounts therefrom after payment of the CNA Incentive shall revert to the General Fund.                                                                          50
51         GOCCs and LGUs may likewise grant CNA Incentive to their respective personnel, subject to the policies, rules and regulations issued by the DBM.                            51
52         Sec. 89. Mandatory Expenditures. The amounts programmed for petroleum, oil and lubricants, water, illumination and power services, telephone and other                      52
53   communication services, and rental expenses shall be disbursed exclusively for such items of expenditures. Any available allotment from these items after taking into             53
54   consideration the agency's full year requirements may be modified only in the last quarter and subject to the General Provision on the Rules on Modification in the               54
55   Allotment under this Act.                                                                                                                                                         55
56         Disbursements or expenditures by agencies in violation of this Section shall be void and shall subject the erring officials and employees to disciplinary actions in        56
57   accordance with Section 43, Chapter 5, and Section 80, Chapter 7, Book VI of E.O. No. 292, and to appropriate civil and criminal actions under existing laws.                     57

31         Sec. 96. Incurrence or Payment of Unauthorized or Unlawful Obligation or Expenditure. Disbursements or expenditures incurred in violation of                                 31

39         Sec. 97. Institutional Strengthening and Productivity Improvement in Agency Organization and Operations. Heads of departments, bureaus,                                      39
40   offices, and instrumentalities under the Executive branch shall adopt institutional strengthening measures to enhance productivity and improve service delivery. For this          40
41   purpose, they shall: (i) conduct a comprehensive review of their respective mandates, missions, objectives, and functions, systems and procedures, programs, activities, and       41
42   projects, and corresponding human resource system: Provided , That they shall prioritize the filling up of existing and relevant vacant plantilla positions prior to requesting    42
43   the creation of new positions; and (ii) identify areas where improvements are necessary and more resources need to be rechanneled.                                                 43
44         In pursuit of said institutional strengthening efforts, the DBM, in consultation with the agencies, shall determine the functions, programs, activities, and projects that   44
45   could be strengthened, scaled down, phased out or abolished and recommend the corresponding structural, functional, and operational adjustments to streamline the                  45
46   organization and operations of the agency and improve its performance and productivity.                                                                                            46
47          Accordingly, the DBM may recommend the: (i) creation, abolition, renaming, consolidation, or merger of bureaus, offices and units; or (ii) creation, abolition,             47
48   reclassification, conversion, or transfer of existing positions, from one unit to another.                                                                                         48
49         The President of the Philippines or the DBM, as the case may be, is authorized to approve the organizational and staffing modifications needed in streamlining and           49
50   improving productivity in agency organization and operations, in accordance with the General Provision on Organizational Structure and Staffing Pattern Changes under              50
51   this Act.                                                                                                                                                                          51
52         Sec. 98. Organizational Structure and Staffing Pattern Changes. Notwithstanding any provision of law to the contrary and within the limits of the                            52
53   appropriations authorized in this Act, the President of the Philippines is authorized to create new offices and modify the existing organizational structure of the agencies       53
54   in the Executive branch, as well as create new positions or modify existing ones whenever public interest so requires.                                                             54
55         The DBM may approve minor changes in the organizational structure and staffing pattern of agencies, and create positions up to a division chief and equivalent               55
56   level under the Executive branch. It may likewise determine the organizational structure and provide positions in the organizational units of agencies or offices created or       56
57   reorganized pursuant to law.                                                                                                                                                       57
     620 GENERAL APPROPRIATIONS BILL, FY 2027



 1         Sec. 99. Foreign Travel of Government Officials. In order to ensure that the delivery of services and the operations of the agency is not hampered, all                    1
 2   personal and official foreign travels of Department Secretaries or those of equivalent in rank in the Executive Department, Chairpersons and Members of Governing Boards         2
 3   and Chief Executive Officers of GOCCs and GFIs under or attached to the Office of the President, as well as the heads of national government agencies under or attached          3
 4   thereto, shall require clearance from the Office of the President prior to foreign travel, pursuant to Section 10 of E.O. No. 77, s. 2019, and such other guidelines that may    4
 5   be issued for the purpose.                                                                                                                                                       5
 6         Sec. 100. Allocation for Reorganized Departments, Bureaus, and Offices of the National Government, including Constitutional Offices                                        6
 7   Enjoying Fiscal Autonomy and State Universities and Colleges. The amount appropriated in this Act for departments, bureaus, and offices of the National                          7
 8   Government, including Constitutional Offices enjoying fiscal autonomy and SUCs, which were reorganized during the immediately preceding fiscal year and the current              8
 9   year, shall be released to the successor agency subject to any transitory provision in the issuance authorizing its reorganization, and budgeting, accounting, and auditing      9
10   rules and regulations.                                                                                                                                                          10
11         Sec. 101. National Tax Allotment of Local Government Units. The national tax allotment which is automatically appropriated in accordance with Section                     11
12   4 of R.A. No. 9358 shall be apportioned among LGUs, including those created, approved, and ratified in FY 2026 in accordance with the allocation formula prescribed under       12
13   Section 285 of R.A. No. 7160, taking into consideration the following:                                                                                                          13
14         (a) The land area shall be based on the FY 2001 Land Management Bureau (LMB) certified Masterlist of Land Area unless the latest LMB certified Masterlist of              14
15              Land Area has been validated by the DILG, NAMRIA, and representatives of the Leagues of Provinces, Cities, and Municipalities, and endorsed by the Secretary         15
16              of DENR and the Chief Minister of the BARMM to DBM on or before December 31, 2026; and                                                                               16
17         (b) The population shall be based on the FY 2024 Census of Population by Province, City, Municipality, and Barangay, as approved under Presidential Proclamation          17
18              No. 973 dated July 11, 2025.                                                                                                                                         18
19         All valid adjustments, changes, modifications, or alterations in any of the factors affecting the computation of national tax allotment that occurred or happened,        19
20   including final and executory court decisions, and new certifications relative to the aforementioned items (a) and (b), which were made effective during the current fiscal     20
21   year, shall only be considered and implemented by the DBM in the subsequent fiscal year from receipt by the DBM of the notice of said change.                                   21
22         LGUs shall include in their budgets income from both local and external sources, including the amount of their national tax allotment, based on the allocation by the     22
23   DBM, and receipts from borrowings, which shall be approved by their respective sanggunian .                                                                                     23
24         Enforcement of the Personnel Services limitations under Sections 325(a) and 331(b) of R.A. No. 7160 shall be waived to enable LGUs to: (i) absorb the cost of hospital    24
25   services transferred from provinces to newly created cities; (ii) pay the CNA incentives of their employees upon compliance with the rules and regulations issued by the        25
26   DBM; (iii) pay the retirement and terminal leave benefits, including the monetization of leave credits of their employees; (iv) pay the minimum Year-end Bonus of One           26
27   Thousand Pesos (P1,000) for the punong barangay and Six Hundred Pesos (P600) for other mandatory barangay officials, and their Cash Gifts; (v) pay the salaries and             27
28   benefits of health/medical personnel that may be hired to perform functions related to emergency situations; (vi) pay the special benefits that may be authorized to be         28
29   granted to LGU personnel during emergency situations; (vii) pay the salary differentials of LGU-hired public health workers to fully implement the provisions of R.A. No.       29
30   7305; (viii) pay the salaries and other benefits of additional personnel that may be hired by the LGUs to implement the full devolution of certain functions of the             30
31   Executive branch to LGUs, subject to the guidelines to be issued by the DBM; and (ix) pay the compensation of the Child Development Teachers and Child Development              31
32   Workers hired by the LGUs. The waiver of the enforcement of the Personnel Services limitation shall be implemented in accordance with the guidelines to be issued by            32
33   the DBM.                                                                                                                                                                        33
34         The national tax allotment, and all LGU shares appropriated herein, shall be directly released by the BTr to the LGU beneficiaries through authorized government          34
35   servicing banks.                                                                                                                                                                35
36         Sec. 102. Implementation of Nationally Funded Projects. Pursuant to Section 17(c) of RA. No. 7160, the national government agencies, such as DPWH,                        36
37   DA, NIA, DOH, DSWD, DepEd. DENR, DILG, and DOTr, may designate LGUs as implementing agencies for public works and infrastructure projects and other programs,                   37
38   services, and facilities, including the construction of local roads and facilities appropriated in this Act, subject to the following:                                          38
39         (a) The LGU has the capability to implement the foregoing by administration or contract and in accordance with the design, plan, specifications, and such other           39
40              standards and policies of the National Government;                                                                                                                   40
41         (b) The LGU-recipient of nationally funded public works and infrastructure projects and other programs, services, and facilities shall commit to fund the cost of         41
42              maintenance and repairs thereof; and                                                                                                                                 42
43         (c) The amounts appropriated for the nationally funded projects to be implemented by LGUs shall be released during the fiscal year to be deposited in a trust fund        43
44              and shall be made available for disbursement for the purpose specified until December 31, 2028.                                                                      44
45          After the end of validity period, all unreleased appropriations, unobligated allotments, and obligated allotments for goods/services/projects not yet delivered,         45
46   rendered, or completed, and accepted shall revert to the unappropriated surplus of the General Fund in accordance with Section 28, Chapter 4, Book VI of E.O. No. 292 and       46
47   shall not thereafter be available for expenditure except by subsequent legislative enactment.                                                                                   47
48         The LGU shall submit quarterly reports on fund utilization and accomplishments through electronic means and post the required reports on the LGU's website.               48
49         The LGU shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the DBM, House of Representatives, Senate of the Philippines,         49
50   House Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, and regulations.      50
51   The date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                                           51
52         Sec. 103. Digital Payments for Government Financial Transactions. All national government agencies, SUCS, GOCCS, and LGUS shall utilize secure and                        52
53   efficient digital disbursements in the payment of goods, services and other disbursements, such as government purchase cards (GPC), and offer a digital mode of collecting      53
54   payments for taxes, fees, tolls, and other charges and impositions, in accordance with E.O. No. 170, s. 2022. The agencies may use facilities of government servicing banks     54
55   and engage the services of established Financial Service Providers registered with the BSP: Provided , That only interoperable digital payment solutions which are              55
56   compliant with the National Retail Payment System Framework shall be availed, subject to the existing procurement laws, rules, and regulations.                                 56
57         Sec. 104. Government Purchase Card Program. All national government agencies shall adopt the GPC as an additional mode of payment for the purchase of                     57
58   eligible goods and services used for official functions and purposes.                                                                                                           58
59         Implementation of the GPC program shall be in accordance with DBM B.C. No. 2025-1 dated March 12, 2025, and such other guidelines as may be issued thereon.               59
                                                                                                                                                GENERAL PROVISIONS 621



 1         Sec. 105. Submission of Annual Reports and Audited Financial Statements on Accounts Deposited Outside of the National Treasury. All                                         1
 2   departments, bureaus, offices, and instrumentalities of the National Government, including Constitutional Offices enjoying fiscal autonomy and SUCS authorized by law to          2
 3   retain or use income and deposit the same outside of the National Treasury shall submit their respective audited financial statements, annual reports, and narrative report       3
 4   stating therein a detailed description of the utilization of funds through the URS or other electronic means for reports not covered by the URS. until such time that the         4
 5   agency has fully adopted the BTMS.                                                                                                                                                5
 6         Likewise, the agency shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                                6
 7         The statement and report shall include the beginning balance, income collected and its sources, expenditures, and ending balance for the preceding fiscal year.             7
 8         The agency shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the House of Representatives, Senate of the Philippines,             8
 9   House Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, and regulations.        9
10   The date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                                            10
11        Sec. 106. Report on Commission on Audit Observations and Recommendation. Within sixty (60) days from receipt of the COA Annual Audit Report,                                11
12   agencies concerned shall submit to the COA, ether in printed form or by way of electronic document, a status report on the actions taken on said audit observations and          12
13   recommendations using the form prescribed by the COA. Upon receipt. COA shall publish said status report in the COA website as appendix to the annual audit report of            13
14   the agency concerned.                                                                                                                                                            14
15         The COA shall likewise furnish copies of the annual audit reports, either in printed form or electronic document, to the following offices:                                15
16         (a) President of the Philippines;                                                                                                                                          16
17         (b) President of the Senate;                                                                                                                                               17
18         (c) Speaker of the House of Representatives;                                                                                                                               18
19         (d) Chairperson, Senate Committee on Finance;                                                                                                                              19
20         (e) Chairperson, House Committee on Appropriations;                                                                                                                        20
21         (f) Secretary of the DBM; and                                                                                                                                              21
22         (g) GCG.                                                                                                                                                                   22
23           Further, the Chairperson of COA and the Commission's web administrator or his/her equivalent shall publish in the COA website the copies of the annual audit             23
24   reports on or before October 31 of the following year.                                                                                                                           24
25          Sec. 107. Citizen Participatory Audit. To promote transparency, accountability, and citizen engagement in government audits, all departments, bureaus,                    25
26   offices, and instrumentalities of the National Government, including GOCCs and LGUs, shall support the Citizens Participatory Audit (CPA) Program of the COA, pursuant to        26
27   COA Resolution No. 2018-006 and related issuances.                                                                                                                               27
28         The CPA shall serve as a formal mechanism for civil society to help audit programs, projects, and activities funded by this Act, ensuring public funds are used            28
29   legally and efficiently.                                                                                                                                                         29
30         The COA shall submit to Congress, on an annual basis, a report on CPA implementation, including the agencies and projects audited, findings and recommendations,           30
31   and measures undertaken to strengthen citizen participation and improve public financial accountability.                                                                         31
32         Sec. 108. Financial and Physical Accountability Reports. Departments, bureaus, offices, and instrumentalities of the National Government, including                        32
33   Constitutional Offices enjoying fiscal autonomy and SUCs, shall submit quarterly reports on its financial and physical accomplishments, on a monthly, quarterly, or yearly       33
34   basis, as required under existing guidelines through the URS or other electronic means for reports not covered by the URS, until such time that the agency has fully             34
35   adopted the BTMS.                                                                                                                                                                35
36         Likewise, the agency shall post said reports on its website.                                                                                                               36
37         The agency shall send written notice when said reports have been submitted or posted on its website to the House of Representatives. Senate of the Philippines,            37
38   House Committee on Appropriations, Senate Committee on Finance, COA, and other offices where the submission of reports is required under existing laws, rules, and               38
39   regulations. The date of notice to said agencies shall be considered the date of compliance with this requirement.                                                               39
40         The DBM shall likewise submit to the Speaker of the House of Representatives, President of the Senate of the Philippines, House Committee on Appropriations, and           40
41   Senate Committee on Finance, either in printed form or by way of electronic document, quarterly reports on releases from, obligations incurred, liquidated and unliquidated      41
42   obligations, total disbursements and balances of, regular agency fund including Special Purpose Funds, Supplemental Appropriations, Continuing Appropriations and                42
43   Automatic Appropriations as well as modification of funds approved by it pursuant to the General Provisions of this Act.                                                         43
44         Failure to comply with any of the foregoing shall result in the automatic suspension of the salaries of the responsible official or employee until they have complied      44
45   with the above requirements pursuant to Section 57, Chapter 6, Book VI of E.O. No. 292.                                                                                          45
46         Repeated failure or refusal of said official or employee to submit the above reports without any justifiable cause may be ground for administrative disciplinary           46
47   action, subject to pertinent civil service rules and regulations. The head of agency shall be responsible for ensuring compliance with this penalty provision.                   47
48         Sec. 109. Submission of Post FY 2027 Budget Status. The DBM shall submit to the Speaker of the House of Representatives, President of the Senate of the                    48
49   Philippines, House Committee on Appropriations, and Senate Committee on Finance a post FY 2027 budget status report not later than May 31, 2028. The report shall                49
50   indicate a brief accomplishment on all programs, activities, and projects of agencies of the government as reflected in this Act and including specific activities or projects   50
51   funded from lump-sum appropriations and special purpose funds.                                                                                                                   51
52         The DBM shall post the said report on its website. The heads of the agencies and the agencies' web administrators or their equivalent shall be responsible for             52
53   ensuring that the portion of the status report pertinent to them are likewise posted on their respective websites.                                                               53
54         Sec. 110. Transparency in Infrastructure Projects. All agencies of the government shall post the following on their respective websites, within the period                 54
55   indicated:                                                                                                                                                                       55
56         (a) The project title, location, and detailed description: detailed estimates in arriving at the Approved Budget for the Contract; and winning contractor and the          56
57              detailed estimates of the bid as awarded. within thirty (30) calendar days from entering into contract; and                                                           57
58         (b) The detailed actual cost of the project and variation orders issued, if any, within thirty (30) calendar days from the issuance of a certificate of completion.        58
     622 GENERAL APPROPRIATIONS BILL, FY 2027



 1         Further, all agencies shall post updates on the financial and physical status of infrastructure projects in the Project Digital Information for Monitoring and Evaluation    1
 2   (DIME) transparency website, subject to the guidelines that may be issued by the DBM.                                                                                              2
 3         The heads of the agencies and web administrators or their equivalent shall be responsible for ensuring compliance with this Section.                                         3
 4         Sec. 111. Transparency Seal. To enhance transparency, enforce accountability, and promote systematized access to government information, all agencies of the                 4
 5   government shall maintain a Transparency Seal to be posted on their websites. The Transparency Seal shall contain the following:                                                   5
 6         (a) the agency's mandates and functions, names of its officials with their position and designation, and contact information;                                                6
 7         (b) approved budgets and corresponding targets, immediately upon approval of this Act;                                                                                       7
 8         (c) modifications made pursuant to the general and special provisions in this Act;                                                                                           8
 9         (d) annual procurement plan/s and contracts awarded with the winning supplier, contractor, or consultant;                                                                    9
10         (e) major programs, activities, or projects and their target beneficiaries;                                                                                                 10
11         (f) status of implementation, evaluation or assessment reports of said programs, activities, or projects;                                                                   11
12         (g) all subsidy and assistance programs of the government, including details on the manner of the execution, the amounts allocated, and relevant data of the target         12
13              beneficiaries, subject to R.A. No. 10173 or the Data Privacy Act;                                                                                                      13
14         (h) Budget and Financial Accountability Reports;                                                                                                                            14
15         (i) Updated People's Freedom of Information (FOI) Manual signed by head of agency, Updated One-Page FOI Manual and Agency FOI Reports;                                      15
16         (j) annual reports on the status of income authorized by law to be retained or used and be deposited outside of the National Treasury, which shall include the legal        16
17              basis for its retention or use, the beginning balance, income collected and its sources, expenditures, and ending balance for the preceding fiscal year;               17
18         (k) particulars of concessions, permits, or authorizations granted by the agency, subject to R.A. No. 10173 or the Data Privacy Act; and                                    18
19         (l) current news and updated events conducted by agencies.                                                                                                                  19
20        Agencies shall ensure that the content posted under the Transparency Seal is regularly reviewed, updated, and maintained using internal systems and procedures that          20
21   support accountability, data integrity, and operational efficiency.                                                                                                               21
22        The heads of the agencies and their web administrators or their equivalent shall be responsible for ensuring compliance with this Section.                                   22
23        The DBM shall post on its website the status of compliance by all agencies of the government. The agencies are responsible in ensuring that the contents and data of         23
24   their posts in their respective official websites and communication channels are searchable for the public's easy access to information regarding matters on public funds.        24
25         Sec. 112. Joint Congressional Oversight Committee on Public Expenditures. The Senate and the House of Representatives shall constitute a Joint                              25
26   Congressional Oversight Committee on Public Expenditures which shall primarily monitor compliance by agencies with the requirements or conditions in the utilization of           26
27   public funds under this Act and pertinent laws.                                                                                                                                   27
28         The Joint Congressional Oversight Committee shall be co-chaired by the Chairperson of the Committee on Finance of the Senate and the Chairperson of the Committee           28
29   on Appropriations of the House of Representatives. The President of the Senate and the Speaker of the House of Representatives shall each designate seven (7) Senators            29
30   and seven (7) members of the House of Representatives, respectively, as members of the Joint Congressional Oversight Committee. The minority group in the Senate and              30
31   the House of Representatives shall each have at least one (1) seat in the Joint Congressional Oversight Committee.                                                                31
32         The Joint Congressional Oversight Committee on Public Expenditures shall not intervene, participate, or undertake any role or function in any of the various post-          32
33   enactment stages of the budget execution, such as, but not limited to, project identification or modification, fund releases, and other activities beyond its congressional       33
34   oversight functions as defined under applicable laws or jurisprudence.                                                                                                            34
35         Sec. 113. Exemption from Garnishment, Levy, and Execution. Any court, agency, or office is hereby cautioned from garnishing or subjecting to levy                           35
36   and execution all public funds, especially the amounts appropriated under this Act.                                                                                               36
37         Sec. 114. Separability Clause. If for any reason, any section or provision of this Act is declared unconstitutional or invalid, other sections or provisions which          37
38   are not affected thereby shall continue to be in full force and effect.                                                                                                           38
39         Sec. 115. Effectivity. The provisions of this Act, detailed in Volume Nos. I-A, I-B, I-C and II shall take effect on January One, Two Thousand and Twenty Seven,            39
40   unless otherwise provided herein.                                                                                                                                                 40

OPERATIONS                                                                                                                     572,924,074,000




   ORGANIZATIONAL OUTCOME 1 : Ensure Safe and Reliable National Road System                                                    199,585,796,000


       Asset Preservation Program                                                                                               68,418,283,000

       The program aims to improve the quality of national roads to international standards and ensure resiliency to natural
       disasters. This program encompasses the preservation of the existing paved national roads through the following sub-
       programs: Preventive Maintenance; Rehabilitation/ Reconstruction/Upgrading of damaged paved national roads;
       Rehabilitation/Reconstruction of National Roads with slips, slope collapse, and landslide; construction,
       upgrading/rehabilitation of drainage along national roads.


            Preventive Maintenance                                                                                              30,741,918,000
92 GENERAL APPROPRIATIONS BILL, FY 2027



                                         PROGRAMS / ACTIVITIES / PROJECTS                                                            AMOUNT (Php)


          Preventive maintenance is a sub-program under the Asset Preservation Program that aims to preserve and prolong the
          lifespan of national roads. This program is typically carried out on roads that are in fair to poor condition, with the
          primary objective of preventing and delaying further deterioration to a state where extensive rehabilitation is
          necessary. Preventive maintenance aims to prevent and delay the deterioration of national roads to a bad condition
          where ultimately rehabilitation is required, which typically involves Asphalt Overlay, Asphalt Overlay with Correction,
          and Concrete Reblocking.Asphalt Overlay is done on roads in fair condition. It involves the application of an additional
          layer of asphalt, that covers imperfections in existing asphalt or concrete. It is commonly applied to pavement that
          hasminor damage like light cracking, mild deterioration, or slightly sunken areas. The process of overlaying asphalt
          commonly includes a leveling out of the old asphalt pavement, ensuring a smooth, even surface on which to add
          additional layers.Asphalt Overlay with Correction is done on roads in poor condition. It involves the repair of short
          intermittent damaged sections before applying asphalt overlay. For concrete roads, the most common type of
          corrective maintenance is a combination of concrete pavement restoration (CPR) in terms of the replacement of
          intermittent shattered slabs and asphalt overlay.Concrete reblocking is done on national roads in poor condition which
          involves selective reblocking or replacement of intermittent shattered slabs in bad condition. process aims to improve
          the pavement's load-bearing capacity, reduce the risk of potholes, and enhance the pavement's durability and
          longevity.

          Rehabilitation/ Reconstruction/ Upgrading of Damaged Paved Roads                                                       25,018,092,000

          The Rehabilitation, Reconstruction, and Upgrading of Damaged Paved National Roads is the sub-program aimed at
          restoring the national roads to an optimal condition. This sub-program under Asset Preservation Program targets
          national roads that are in poor condition and are no longer cost-effective to maintain.Upgrading from asphalt to
          concrete is also a part of this sub-program. This involves replacing the asphalt surface with a concrete one, which
          provides enhanced durability, resistance to heavy loads, and reduced maintenance costs.

Rehabilitation/ Reconstruction of Roads with Slips, Slope Collapse, and Landslide                                          9,442,356,000

The Rehabilitation and Reconstruction of National Roads with Slips, Slope Collapse, and Landslide is a sub-program
under the Asset Preservation Program that aims to protect and secure national roads against the devastating effects of
natural disasters, particularly landslides, erosion, and slope collapses. This sub-program is designed to enhance the
engineering design of national roads to withstand the impact of severe storms and natural calamities in support of
climate change adaptation.

      Network Development Program                                                                                                            92,179,924,000

      The Network Development Program focuses specifically on the expansion and improvement of the national road network.It
      aims to expand the capacity of the national road network by constructing new roads that meet the functional classification
      criteria and improving the quality of existing national roads through various activities. Eligibility for later classification as a
      national road is determined by a feasibility study and the functional classification criteria set by DPWH. This is also achieved
      through a range of activities such as road widening, the construction of bypasses and diversion roads, the construction of
      missing links/new roads, the construction of flyovers, interchanges, underpasses, long-span bridges, off-carriageway
      improvement, and the paving of unpaved roads.The program includes several sub-programs aimed at achieving its
      objectives. These sub-programs include: Road Widening; Construction of By-Passes and Diversion Roads; Construction of
      Missing Links/ New Roads; Construction of Flyovers/ Interchanges/ Underpasses/ Long Span Bridges; Off-Carriageway
      Improvement; Paving of Unpaved Roads




            Road Widening                                                                                                                    16,469,280,000
           This involves widening the existing road pavement to accommodate more lanes to ease traffic congestion, improve
           traffic flow, and increase road capacity. Road widening is essential in high-traffic areas where there is a need to
           increase the capacity of the national road network.

      New Bridges.
